### Real backend surface — confirmed by reading the actual code before writing any frontend code

Read `instances.controller.ts`, every `approvals/api/dto/*.ts`, `appr-instance.entity.ts`/`appr-level.entity.ts`, `approval-engine.service.ts` in full (routing/authorization/self-approval logic), `receipts.controller.ts`'s two reverse handlers, `receipts.service.ts`'s `reverseReceipt()`, and the `0900` seed migration's `SINGLE_LEVEL_WORKFLOW_SEEDS` array, before writing any frontend code:

- **`InstanceResponseDto` genuinely has zero human-readable context** — just `{id, workflowVersionId, domainCode, entityType, entityId, amount, initiatorId, status, currentLevel, submittedAt, decidedAt}`, confirmed directly. `<EntityLabel>`'s resolver design (below) exists specifically to close this gap.
- **`GET /approvals/instances/inbox` already excludes the caller's own submissions** server-side (`ApprovalEngineService.listPendingForApprover()`'s own `if (instance.initiatorId === userId) continue` — BR-APPR-01) — re-confirmed live, not just by reading the code (Phase 1 of verification below: User A's own inbox never contained the instance User A itself initiated).
- **Self-approval is a real, three-layer server rule (BR-APPR-01)**, confirmed by reading `ApprovalEngineService.decide()` directly: `actorId === instance.initiatorId` throws `AuthorizationException` (403, message contains `BR-APPR-01`) BEFORE any level/authorization resolution even runs; a second check catches the deeper "the legitimate approver whose authority is being exercised is the initiator" case (delegation/role-overlap); a DB trigger (`trg_appr_no_self_approval`, migration `0050`) is the third layer. `features/approvals/lib/errors.ts`'s `isSelfApprovalError()` matches the exact stable marker.
- **Comment-required for REJECT/RETURN is a real server rule (FR-APPR-003.1)**: `ApprovalEngineService.decide()`'s very first check — `if ((decision==="REJECT"||decision==="RETURN") && !comment) throw ValidationException(...)` (422, message contains `FR-APPR-003.1`) — confirmed by reading it directly, then re-confirmed live with a real raw bypass (Phase 2 of verification below).
- **`GET /approvals/instances?domainCode=` has no `entityId` filter param** (confirmed by reading `InstancesController.list()` directly — only `status`/`domainCode`) — the plan's own workaround (fetch the whole domain-filtered list, pick the most recently submitted match client-side) was implemented exactly as specified, and independently confirmed to match `ApprovalEngineService.getStatus()`'s own real server-side semantics: `ApprInstanceRepository.findLatestByEntity()` does `ORDER BY submitted_at DESC` (read directly) — `features/payments/lib/reversal.ts`'s `pickLatestInstanceForEntity()` replicates this exact tie-break rule (max `submittedAt`), not a guess.
- **`PAYMENT_REVERSALS` is genuinely a single-level, ROLE-based (`System Admin`) workflow** — confirmed directly in the `0900` seed migration's own doc comment (`SINGLE_LEVEL_WORKFLOW_SEEDS`, `seedSingleLevelWorkflow()`) — this is what made the live self-approval test buildable with only System-Admin-role throwaway users, no delegation/routing-rule setup needed.
- **A real, confirmed discrepancy between the plan's two sections, resolved in favor of the verified endpoint**: the plan's "Screens" section describes the Request Reversal dialog as collecting a reason-code `<Select>`, but the plan's own separately-verified "backend facts" section states `POST .../reverse/request` takes **no body at all** — re-confirmed directly by reading `ReceiptsController.requestReversal()` (`@Param("id") id, @Req() req` only, no `@Body()`). The reason code only exists on `ReverseReceiptDto` (the EXECUTE step, `POST .../reverse`). Resolved by moving the reason-code `<Select>` to `<ExecuteReversalDialog>` (where the real DTO actually has the field) and making `<RequestReversalDialog>` a plain confirm dialog — documented inline in both components and in `receipts.api.ts`'s own doc comment on `requestReceiptReversal()`.
- **`reverseReceipt()`'s response is the CONTRA receipt, not the original** — confirmed directly in `ReceiptsService.reverseReceipt()`'s return statement (`return contra`) — the original only flips to `REVERSED` as a side effect (`original.status = "REVERSED"` saved separately). `useReverseReceipt()`'s cache invalidation explicitly targets `detailKey(receiptId)` (the ORIGINAL's own query key) for exactly this reason — the mutation's own response alone would never surface the original's status flip.
- **A real, previously-undocumented quirk found live, not by reading the code**: `InstancesController.decide()`/`ReceiptsController.reverse()` both carry `@ApiResponse({status:200,...})` in their Swagger decorators, but neither has an `@HttpCode` override — NestJS's real runtime default for a bare `@Post()` handler is **201**, not 200. Confirmed live in every decide/execute call this pass made (`approve1.status === 201`, `execute1.status === 201`, etc., never 200). This has NO effect on the frontend (`unwrapApiResult()` only checks `response.ok`, i.e. any 2xx), but is a real, minor Swagger-doc-vs-runtime mismatch, the same class of gap this codebase's own prior slices have flagged elsewhere (e.g. `AcademicCalendarController`'s missing response types) — not fixed (`packages/server` out of scope this pass), noted here for whoever next does a Swagger-annotation pass.
- **`GET /users/{id}` has zero `@ApiResponse({type})`** (confirmed directly — `UsersController.findOne()` returns `this.usersService.findByIdOrFail(id)` raw, no DTO/view-mapper), the SAME class of gap `features/billing/types.ts`'s `AcademicYearResponse` already documents — confirmed in `openapi-types.ts`: `UsersController_findOne`'s `responses: {200:{...,content?:never}}`. `features/approvals/types.ts`'s `UserSummary` hand-types only the three fields actually needed (`id`/`username`/`fullName`) — deliberately NOT a full entity mirror, since the real `UsrUserEntity` carries `passwordHash`/2FA secret columns this app has no legitimate reason to reference.

### The entity-resolver design — and why it's extensible

`features/approvals/components/entity-label.tsx`'s `<EntityLabel entityType entityId>` is the resolver the plan asked for: given `(entityType, entityId)`, if `entityType === "pay_receipt"` it calls `features/payments/hooks/use-receipts.ts`'s existing `useReceipt()` (conditionally enabled — `useReceipt(isReceipt ? entityId : undefined)`, the same `enabled: !!id`-style pattern every hook in this app already follows) and renders a real label (receipt number, payer, amount) + a deep link to `/payments/receipts/{id}`; for every other `entityType`, it renders a generic, safe fallback (`{entityType} · {shortId}…`) — never a crash, never a blocked row (`isLoading`/`isError` both degrade to the same fallback text, confirmed by code review of every branch).

**Why this generalizes rather than being a one-off**: this engine already backs 18 real domain codes total (confirmed via the `0900` seed migration's `SINGLE_LEVEL_WORKFLOW_SEEDS` array) — `PAYMENT_REVERSALS` plus 17 more across Billing (concessions/credit-notes/refund-vouchers/late-fee-batches), GL budgets, Wallet (transfers/refunds/adjustments), Procurement (requisitions/POs/supplier-payments), Inventory (stock adjustments), Expenses (vouchers/replenishments/claims), Payroll (loans/runs), Banking (transfers/deposits/withdrawals), and Fixed Assets (depreciation/disposals/verifications). Adding a resolver for any of those later is exactly one more `entityType === "..."` branch calling that domain's own existing detail hook the same conditionally-enabled way — no plugin registry or dynamic-hook-dispatch mechanism was built (a deliberate choice, not an oversight: this codebase's own established preference is direct, readable code over abstraction, and only ONE entity type has both an approval-gated action AND an existing frontend screen to link to today). The inbox table, the instance detail page, and the receipt-reversal status indicator all reuse this exact same component — one resolver, three call sites, zero duplication.

### Two real, confirmed OpenAPI-codegen gaps found and worked around, both frontend-only fixes — the SAME class `sessions.api.ts`'s `closeSession()` already documents

1. `BounceChequeDto`'s generated type declares `applyBounceFee: boolean` (REQUIRED) even though the real server DTO has it `@ApiPropertyOptional()` + `applyBounceFee?: boolean` — `@nestjs/swagger`'s combination of `@ApiPropertyOptional()` with a `@default` annotation still emits a required Swagger property here. Fixed with one documented, narrow cast at `cheques.api.ts`'s `bounceCheque()` call site — the real JSON sent over the wire (including a genuinely omitted field) is unaffected.
2. `CreateBulkAllocationBatchDto`'s generated type declares `instrument: Record<string, never>` — the real server DTO has `@ApiProperty({ type: Object }) instrument!: Record<string, unknown>` (`bulk-allocation.dto.ts`), and `type: Object` gives Swagger no property-value type to reflect, the exact same gap `CloseSessionDto.counted` already established. Fixed with the same narrow-cast pattern at `bulk-allocation.api.ts`'s `createBulkAllocationBatch()`.

### A real, previously-undocumented, verification-blocking backend bug found live — confirmed, root-caused, deliberately NOT fixed

`BulkAllocationService.matchAndPost()` computes `externalRef = \`bulk-batch-${batchId}-line-${line.id}\`` (two real UUIDs plus literal text, ~89 characters) for BOTH the receipt split's own `pay_receipt_split.external_ref` AND — on the very `catch` block meant to gracefully park a failed line into suspense — `pay_suspense_item.external_ref`. Both columns are real `varchar(60)` (migration `0080`, confirmed by reading the DDL directly). Every line's capture attempt throws a raw Postgres `value too long for type character varying(60)` error; the fallback INSERT inside the `catch` block hits the IDENTICAL limit for the identical reason, so the error is never actually caught anywhere — it propagates out of `matchAndPost()` entirely as an uncaught `500`, not even the documented "partial-failure-tolerant, parks into suspense" degradation the method's own doc comment promises. **Confirmed live, not assumed**: a real batch (2 valid lines, `POST /payments/bulk-allocations` → real `201`) hit a real `500` (`{"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"value too long for type character varying(60)"}}`) on `POST .../match-and-post`, every single time. The batch itself survives (stuck at `status:"MATCHING"` forever — the loop never reaches its own status-finalizing save), and both lines remain `receiptId:null` with no silent partial success hiding behind the `500`.

`packages/server` is out of scope for this frontend-only slice (the one pre-approved addition is the suspense `GET :id` endpoint only) — matching Slice 4's own precedent for a similarly real, similarly left-unfixed gap (the CHEQUE/CARD/POS clearing-account seed gap), this is documented here plainly, not silently patched around, and not fixed. The frontend's own `useMatchAndPostBulkAllocationBatch()`/`bulk-allocations/[id]/page.tsx` still call the real endpoint correctly and surface whatever comes back — including this real `500` — via the same `ApiError`-driven `Alert variant="destructive"` every other mutation error in this app already uses (verified by code review: `handleRunMatching()`'s `catch` block is unconditional, not scoped to any particular error shape). The mechanism itself (partial-failure-tolerance, the try/catch/park-to-suspense shape) remains covered by `bulk-allocation.service.spec.ts`'s real, passing unit tests (mocked repositories, so they never touch the real `varchar(60)` constraint) — a real, if partial, form of coverage, restated here rather than left implicit.

## Slice 7 — Bulk Allocation Fix + Integration Settings — 2026-07-31

**Verdict: both pieces of this slice are built and verified live end-to-end. (1) The real, previously-documented `BulkAllocationService.matchAndPost()` bug Slice 6 found and deliberately left unfixed is now genuinely fixed** — `pay_bulk_allocation_batch` gained a real `bank_account_id` FK (migration `0220`), threaded through `createBatch()`/`matchAndPost()` in place of the fabricated `bulk-batch-${batchId}` string, with `externalRef` shortened to `line.id` alone — confirmed live: a real batch (2 real students, a real bank account) now runs `match-and-post` to a genuine `COMPLETED`, and Slice 6's own 2 real residue batches (stuck at `MATCHING` since 2026-07-30, backfilled by this migration) both now show `COMPLETED`/`createdReceipts:2` for real. **(2) The first Settings-area frontend screen — Integrations (M-Pesa paybill configuration) — is built**, reusing the fully-existing encrypted credential-store backend (`SetIntegrationConfigEntity`/`IntegrationConfigsController`/`MpesaAdapterResolverService`) almost entirely as-is; the one real backend change is `IntegrationConfigService.testConnection()`'s new `MPESA` branch, replacing the hardcoded stub with a genuine Daraja OAuth token-fetch attempt.

### Part 1 — why `bankAccountId` needed a real column, not a string tweak

Slice 6's write-up already root-caused the crash: `matchAndPost()` set `bankAccountId: \`bulk-batch-${batchId}\`` (a non-UUID string) against `pay_receipt_split.bank_account_id`, a real `uuid` FK to `bank_account` (migration `0141`, `ON DELETE RESTRICT`) — every capture failed outright, and the `catch` block's own suspense fallback hit the identical `varchar(60)` overflow on `externalRef` (`\`bulk-batch-${batchId}-line-${line.id}\`, ~89 chars), so the "gracefully park to suspense" degradation never actually caught anything either. Shortening the string alone would only have fixed the `externalRef` half — `bankAccountId` was never a length problem, it was a **type/shape** problem: no string, however short, satisfies a `uuid` FK column. The only real fix is a real bank account, chosen once per batch.

**Migration `0220-add-bulk-allocation-bank-account.ts`**: `ADD COLUMN bank_account_id uuid NULL` → backfill `UPDATE ... SET bank_account_id = (SELECT id FROM app.bank_account WHERE kind='BANK' ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 1) WHERE bank_account_id IS NULL` → `ALTER COLUMN ... SET NOT NULL` → `ADD CONSTRAINT fk_pay_bulk_allocation_batch_bank_account_id FOREIGN KEY (bank_account_id) REFERENCES app.bank_account(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` — mirrors migration `0141`'s exact FK style. **Real data state checked before deciding the backfill approach, not guessed**: `docker exec ... psql` confirmed 2 real pre-existing rows (both `status='MATCHING'`, `created_receipts=0`, real residue from Slice 6's own verification hitting this exact bug) and confirmed a real active `kind='BANK'` account existed ("Main Operating Account", `019f8b20-6d42-7455-a925-1b8ee37d7b67` — the same account every prior Payments slice's own verification has reused) — the backfill subquery resolved to it for both rows, confirmed via `SELECT id, status, bank_account_id FROM app.pay_bulk_allocation_batch` immediately after running the migration.

**Code changes**: `PayBulkAllocationBatchEntity` gained `bankAccountId!: string` + a `ManyToOne(() => BankAccountEntity, {onDelete:"RESTRICT"})` relation (direct entity-file import, the same circular-require-avoidance discipline `PayReceiptSplitEntity`'s own `BankAccountEntity` import already established — no new `module-deps.json` edge needed, `domains/payments` already lists `domains/banking`). `CreateBulkAllocationBatchDto` gained a required `bankAccountId` (`@IsUUID()`); `BulkAllocationBatchResponseDto` gained `bankAccountId`. `BulkAllocationService.createBatch()` gained a `bankAccountId` parameter, stored on the batch row (no pre-check against `BankAccountRepository` — deliberately, matching `ReceiptsService`'s own established convention of relying on the real DB FK for referential integrity rather than a redundant service-layer existence check; `@IsUUID()` catches the format case). `matchAndPost()` now reads `batch.bankAccountId` (the real FK) for every line's `BANK_TRANSFER` split, and `externalRef: line.id` (36 chars, well under `varchar(60)`) in both the happy path and the suspense-fallback `catch` block. `bulk-allocation.controller.ts` threads `dto.bankAccountId` through to `createBatch()` and returns it on `toView()`.

**Frontend**: `apps/web/src/app/(erp)/payments/bulk-allocations/new/page.tsx` gained a required bank-account field in its Step 1 card, reusing `<BankAccountSelect>` (`features/payments/components/bank-account-select.tsx`, built in Slice 4 for receipt capture) directly — no new picker component. The preview step's submit button is now also gated on `bankAccountId` being chosen, with a destructive `Alert` if not. The detail page (`[id]/page.tsx`) gained a "Bank account" summary row, resolved via a new small `<BankAccountLabel>` component (`features/payments/components/bank-account-label.tsx`) that reuses `useBankAccounts()`'s already-cached list query (no new endpoint call) and degrades to a truncated raw id on load/error/not-found, the same template `BulkAllocationLineStudentCell` already establishes for an analogous id-to-label resolution.

**Tests**: `bulk-allocation.service.spec.ts` gained a `BANK_ACCOUNT_ID` constant threaded through every `makeBatch()`, a new `createBatch` assertion that `bankAccountId` is passed to `batchRepository.create()`, and two new `matchAndPost` tests asserting the real fix directly — `captureReceipt()` is called with `splits[0].bankAccountId === BANK_ACCOUNT_ID` (never the old fabricated string) and `splits[0].externalRef === line.id` (never the old ~89-char concatenation), plus the suspense-park test asserting the same short `externalRef` on the fallback path.

### Part 2 — Integration settings: what already existed vs. the one real fix

**Confirmed already fully built, read before writing any frontend code**: `SetIntegrationConfigEntity` (`kind` enum already includes `MPESA`, `configEnc bytea` encrypted at rest), `IntegrationConfigsController` (real `POST/GET/GET:id/PATCH/:id/test-connection`, `settings:integration:manage`/`:view`-gated), and `MpesaAdapterResolverService` (already reads live from `IntegrationConfigService.list()` on every M-Pesa call, no caching of the enabled-config SELECTION itself — only the constructed `DarajaAdapter` instance is cached, keyed by config id, re-resolved the moment a different config becomes the highest-priority enabled one). **None of this needed a new entity, service, or wiring — confirmed by reading all three files directly, matching the plan's own pre-confirmed finding.**

**The one real backend fix**: `IntegrationConfigService.testConnection()` was a hardcoded stub for every `kind`. Added a real `MPESA` branch (`testMpesaConnection()`): decrypts the row's own `configEnc`, validates `consumerKey`/`consumerSecret` are present (returns a clean `{ok:false}` with no network call if not), then calls a new `fetchDarajaOAuthToken()` (`platform/settings/infrastructure/mpesa-oauth-probe.ts`) — a genuine HTTPS `GET` against Safaricom's real OAuth token endpoint. **Why this duplicates rather than reuses `domains/payments`' own `DarajaAdapter`, a real architectural finding, not a shortcut**: `module-deps.json`'s `platform/settings` entry declares `mayImport: ["shared"]` only — importing `DarajaAdapter` (a `domains/payments` class) would add a backward dependency edge (a platform module reaching into a domain module), the exact direction this codebase's whole module-dependency architecture forbids everywhere else. `MpesaAdapterResolverService`'s own construction logic was checked first per the plan's own "prefer reuse" instruction — it is not cleanly reusable without that architecture violation, so this is a deliberate, narrowly-scoped duplication of ONLY the OAuth-token-fetch call (~50 lines, `getAccessToken()`'s real shape) — STK/status-query/B2C stay domain-owned, completely untouched. Every other `kind` (`SMTP`/`SMS`/`FCM`/`QUICKBOOKS`/`XERO`/`SAGE`/`BANK`/`WHATSAPP`) still returns the identical old stub — deliberately not touched, per the plan's explicit scope. A real, honest fix found and applied mid-verification (not left in as a known gap): the first pass forgot to thread the config's own optional `timeoutMs` through to the probe (defaulting to the probe's own 15000ms regardless of what was configured) — fixed, re-verified live (see below, the message changed from "timed out after 15000ms" to "timed out after 5000ms" matching the configured value).

**Frontend — new `features/settings/{api,hooks,components}` folder** (first use of this feature-folder name, mirrors every other module's shape exactly): `types.ts` (`IntegrationConfig`/`IntegrationKind`/`TestConnectionResult`/`MpesaConfig`, all hand-typed — `IntegrationConfigsController`'s handlers have ZERO `@ApiResponse({type})` decorators anywhere, confirmed by reading the controller directly and in the freshly-regenerated `openapi-types.ts` (`content?: never` on every one of its 5 operations), the same class of gap `features/approvals/types.ts`'s `UserSummary` already documents), `constants.ts` (`INTEGRATION_KINDS`, `CONFIGURABLE_INTEGRATION_KINDS = ["MPESA"]`), `api/integration-configs.api.ts`, `hooks/use-integration-configs.ts`, `components/{integration-status-badges,mpesa-config-form,new-integration-dialog,edit-integration-dialog,test-connection-dialog}.tsx`. `app/(erp)/settings/integrations/page.tsx` — a `<DataTable>` (kind/name/isEnabled badge/priority/lastTestedAt/lastTestResult badge/actions), a `<NewIntegrationDialog>` (kind `<Select>` — only `MPESA` renders `<MpesaConfigForm>`, every other kind shows an explicit `Alert variant="warning"` "not yet configurable in this UI" placeholder rather than a broken form), `<EditIntegrationDialog>` (name/isEnabled/priority always freely editable via `UpdateIntegrationConfigDto`'s genuinely-optional fields; an OFF-by-default "resubmit credentials" checkbox reveals a completely BLANK `<MpesaConfigForm>` — never pre-filled, since `configEnc` can never be read back, confirmed directly in the controller's own `toView()`: `const {configEnc:_configEnc, ...view} = entity`), `<TestConnectionDialog>` (manual "Run test" step, surfaces the real `{ok,message}` via `Alert variant={result.ok?"success":"destructive"}`). `consumerSecret`/`passkey`/`securityCredential` are `type="password"` inputs — the same plain convention the login/change-password screens already use, no show/hide-toggle component exists anywhere in this app to reuse.

**Nav/i18n**: `nav-links.tsx` gained one `NAV_ITEMS` entry (`{href:"/settings/integrations", labelKey:"settings", icon:Settings, allowedRoles:[]}`), same `allowedRoles:[]`/`<QueryBoundary>`-is-the-real-gate rationale as every prior entry. ## Slice 8 (Part 1 — Bulk Generate Invoice + Nav Dropdown) — 2026-07-31

**Verdict: Slices 0–2 of the approved "Billing Invoice Lifecycle" plan are built and verified live end-to-end.** New bulk ADHOC invoice generation (category + grade + student-checkbox selection, one invoice per due-date group per student, generated AND posted immediately), a new `GET .../categories-for-scope` chip-picker catalog endpoint, a new bulk "Generate Invoice" screen wired to both, a "collect from student wallet" checkbox that sequentially calls the existing single-invoice wallet transfer endpoint, and the sidebar's first-ever expand/collapse nav group (Billing → Fee Categories / Generate Invoice). Slices 3–7 (Pending/Upcoming lists, Collect Fees, receipt breakdown polish, global Receipts) are explicitly OUT of scope for this dispatch, per the plan's own phasing — not silently skipped.

### Slice 0 — shared frontend primitives

`apps/web/src/components/ui/checkbox.tsx` — a hand-authored native `<input type="checkbox">` (`appearance-none` + a `peer`-shown `lucide-react` `Check` glyph), same `border-input`/`bg-background`/`focus-visible:ring-ring` token classes as `input.tsx`. One real lint fix mid-build: an empty `interface CheckboxProps extends Omit<...>{}` tripped `@typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type` ("equivalent to its supertype") — fixed by exporting a `type` alias instead of an empty interface, not by suppressing the rule.

`apps/web/src/features/billing/components/fee-category-chip-picker.tsx` — a presentational, always-visible `flex flex-wrap` row of toggle `<button>`s (`options:{value,label}[]`/`selected:string[]`/`onChange`), active variant reusing `badge.tsx`'s own `rounded-full`/`bg-primary text-primary-foreground` default-variant pairing; inactive variant matches `input.tsx`'s bordered token shape. No `MultiSelect` reuse (per the plan — a dropdown-that-summarizes is the wrong shape for an always-visible chip row).

### Slice 1 — backend: bulk ADHOC invoice generation

**New `packages/server/src/domains/billing/application/bulk-adhoc-invoices.service.ts`** (`BulkAdhocInvoicesService.bulkGenerate()`) — same per-student-own-transaction (`runInTransaction()` per student, inside the per-student `try/catch`), partial-failure-tolerant shape `BulkBillingService.bulkGenerate()` already establishes, verified by reading that file in full first. Per student: `FeeStructuresService.findApplicableFor(studentId, termId, manager)` (reused as-is, unmodified) → `BillFeeStructureLineRepository.listByStructureAndTerm()` (confirmed this exact method already exists, exactly as the plan assumed — no guessing needed) → filter to the selected `feeCategoryIds` → group the filtered lines by `dueDate` (a plain `Map<string, BillFeeStructureLineEntity[]>`) → per due-date group, resolve each line's fee-category `name` (a small local cache, `BillFeeCategoryRepository.findByIdOrFail()`, mirroring `InvoicingService.generateInvoice()`'s own `categoryFor()` cache pattern) as the ADHOC line's `description`, then call `InvoicingService.generateInvoice(manager, {studentId, termId, source:"ADHOC", adhocLines, dueDate})` + `.postInvoice()` — both reused EXACTLY as they exist, zero internal generate/post logic duplicated. Zero matching lines (no applicable structure, or none of the selected categories present) → `NotFoundException`/`ValidationException`, caught and recorded in `failed[]`, never aborting the batch.

**Real, honestly-flagged interaction, not worked around**: `generateInvoice()` enforces `dueDate >= issueDate` (`ck_bill_invoice_due_after_issue`) — this service passes a structure line's own `dueDate` through unmodified and lets `issueDate` default to today, exactly like every other real caller. A structure line whose due date has already passed relative to today would make `generateInvoice()` throw a real `ValidationException` for that student's whole transaction (all of that student's due-date groups share one transaction, so one bad group fails the whole student, not just that one invoice) — this is INTENTIONAL, not a bug: the plan's explicit instruction was to reuse `generateInvoice()`'s existing behavior, not invent a workaround for one of its existing invariants. Verification below deliberately used future due dates to demonstrate the success path; the past-due-date failure mode was reasoned through but not separately exercised live, since exercising it would just re-prove `generateInvoice()`'s own already-tested guard, not anything new this pass built.

**New `packages/server/src/domains/billing/api/dto/bulk-adhoc-invoice.dto.ts`** (`BulkGenerateAdhocInvoicesDto`: `termId`/`classId` both `@IsUUID()`, `feeCategoryIds`/`studentIds` both `@IsArray() @ArrayMinSize(1) @IsUUID(undefined,{each:true})`; `BulkGenerateAdhocInvoicesResultDto` mirroring the service's `{succeeded:{studentId,invoiceIds}[], failed:{studentId,error}[]}` shape exactly). **New `packages/server/src/domains/billing/api/bulk-adhoc-invoices.controller.ts`** — `POST billing/invoices/bulk-generate`, `@RequirePermission("billing:bulk-billing:execute")` (confirmed this exact code already exists in `permission-catalogue.ts`, reused as-is). Kept as its OWN controller class (mirrors `BulkBillingController`'s own split from `InvoicesController`) but registered under the SAME `billing/invoices` prefix as `InvoicesController` — a deliberate deviation from `BulkBillingController`'s separate-prefix precedent, documented inline, because the endpoint's own designed path (`POST billing/invoices/bulk-generate`) is a sibling of `POST billing/invoices/generate`, not a new top-level area; Nest permits multiple controllers sharing one prefix as long as their own routes don't collide, confirmed with a clean boot.

**`FeeStructuresService.listCategoriesForScope(academicYearId, classId)`** (new method, same file) — reuses the ALREADY-EXISTING `listByYearAndClass()` (both the service method and its underlying `BillFeeStructureRepository.listByYearAndClass()` — confirmed this exact method already exists exactly as the plan assumed, no new repository method needed), filters to `status==="PUBLISHED"`, then `listByStructure()` (all lines, deliberately NOT term-filtered — this endpoint has no `termId` query param by design, letting a user browse categories before committing to a term) per structure, deduped by `feeCategoryId` into a `Map`, resolving each category's real `name` via `BillFeeCategoryRepository.findByIdOrFail()` — a NEW constructor dependency on `FeeStructuresService` (`BillFeeCategoryRepository`, appended as the LAST constructor param to minimize positional-arg churn), which required fixing two other call sites that construct `FeeStructuresService` directly (not via Nest DI): `billing-e2e.integration.spec.ts` (twice) and `fee-structures.service.spec.ts` — both already had a `feeCategoryRepository` local variable in scope, just needed threading through as the 7th arg. New endpoint `GET billing/fee-structures/categories-for-scope` on `fee-structures.controller.ts`, `@RequirePermission("billing:fee-structure:view")` (confirmed exact code, reused) — declared BEFORE `@Get(":id")` deliberately (documented inline): Nest/Express matches routes in declaration order, and `:id` would otherwise swallow the literal `categories-for-scope` segment as an id value. New `FeeCategoryForScopeResponseDto` (`feeCategoryId`/`name`/`exampleAmount` — a decimal string, the FIRST matching line's own amount for that category, display context only, not a canonical/aggregate price) added to `fee-structure.dto.ts`.

**Tests**: `packages/server/src/domains/billing/__tests__/bulk-adhoc-invoices.service.spec.ts` (new, 5 tests) — single-due-date happy path, 2-group due-date-grouping case (asserts 2 `generateInvoice()` calls with the 2 distinct `dueDate` values), the partial-failure-tolerant case (one of 3 students has no applicable structure, the other 2 still succeed, `generateInvoice()` called exactly twice), the zero-matching-category case (student lands in `failed[]`, `generateInvoice()` never called), and a `postInvoice()`-failure-aborts-the-student's-remaining-groups case (proves one transaction PER STUDENT, not per due-date group). `fee-structures.service.spec.ts` gained a `listCategoriesForScope` describe block (dedup-across-PUBLISHED-only case, empty-scope case) plus the constructor-signature fix.

### Slice 2 — frontend: bulk "Generate Invoice" screen + nav dropdown

**New `features/billing/api/bulk-adhoc-invoices.api.ts`** + **`hooks/use-bulk-adhoc-invoices.ts`** (`useCategoriesForScope`/`useBulkGenerateAdhocInvoices`) — same thin-wrapper-over-`apiClient` shape every other `features/*/api/*.api.ts` file uses.

**New `features/wallet/` folder** (first frontend touch of `domains/wallet` — `apps/web/src/features/wallet/{api,lib}`) — deliberately minimal, only what the wallet-collection checkbox needs: `api/wallets.api.ts` (`findWalletByStudent()` — `GET wallets/students/{studentId}`, deliberately NOT the `POST .../students/{studentId}` `getOrCreate` variant, so a student who never used a wallet is correctly reported as "nothing to collect" rather than having an empty wallet silently created as a side effect of a bulk invoice run; `transferToFees()` — `POST wallets/{id}/transfer-to-fees`) and `lib/errors.ts` (`isTransferNeedsApprovalError`/`isInsufficientBalanceError`, matching `FR-WALL-013.1`/`BR-WALL-01` message markers, mirroring `features/billing/lib/errors.ts`'s own established pattern).

**A real, confirmed contracts-codegen naming collision found and worked around**: `TransferToFeesDto`/`WalletTransactionResponseDto` are NOT flatly exported from `@klickit/contracts`'s root barrel — `wallet-transaction.schema.ts`'s own class names collide with an already-alphabetically-earlier-claimed name elsewhere in the generated schema universe, so the codegen re-exports the whole file under a namespace instead (`export * as domains_wallet_wallet_transaction_schema from "./domains/wallet/wallet-transaction.schema"` — confirmed by reading `packages/contracts/src/index.ts`'s own doc comment). Fixed by importing the namespace and referencing `domains_wallet_wallet_transaction_schema.TransferToFeesDto`/`.WalletTransactionResponseDto` as types — not a deep `@klickit/contracts/domains/...` path import (also valid per that same doc comment, but this app has zero existing precedent for a deep contracts import anywhere, so the namespace route stays inside the one already-established barrel entry point).

**`features/students/hooks/use-students.ts`** gained one new, additive, optional second parameter — `useStudents(params, options?: {enabled?: boolean})`, defaulting `enabled` to `true` (byte-for-byte unchanged behavior for the one pre-existing call site, `app/(erp)/students/page.tsx`, which never passes it) — needed because `useStudents()` itself has no `enabled` gate, and `StudentSelectionGrid` must not fire `GET /students` at all before a class is chosen.

**New `features/billing/components/student-selection-grid.tsx`** — 4-column checkbox grid (`grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4`) + a "Select all" toggle, backed by `useStudents({classId, status:"ACTIVE", pageSize:200}, {enabled:!!classId})`, wrapped in `<QueryBoundary>`. **New `features/billing/components/bulk-generate-invoice-form.tsx`** — `<AcademicYearTermSelect autoSelectCurrent>` (reused verbatim, byte-for-byte unmodified), a grade `<Select>` (`useActiveClasses()`, existing hook, reused), Slice 0's `<FeeCategoryChipPicker>` (fed by `useCategoriesForScope()` once both year+class are chosen, chip labels formatted `"{name} ({formatMoney(exampleAmount)})"`), Slice 0's `<Checkbox>`-backed `<StudentSelectionGrid>`, and the "Collect amount from student wallet" checkbox. On submit: calls `useBulkGenerateAdhocInvoices()`, renders a succeeded/failed summary (`FeeStructureCreateDialog`'s own established partial-result `<Alert>` shape, reused) — then, only if the wallet checkbox is checked, sequentially loops every succeeded invoice (`getInvoice()` for its real `balance`, then `transferToFees()`), classifying each outcome into `settled`/`needsApproval`/`insufficientBalance`/`noWallet`/`failed` and rendering a second summary panel with real per-outcome counts. **New route `apps/web/src/app/(erp)/billing/generate/page.tsx`.**

**Nav dropdown (`components/layout/nav-links.tsx`)** — `NavItem` gained an optional `children?: readonly {href,labelKey}[]`. `NavLinks()`'s render function now branches: an item WITH `children` renders as a `<button>` (not a `<Link>` — clicking it ONLY toggles expand/collapse, per the plan's own "use your judgment, keep it simple" guidance) with a `ChevronDown` that rotates 180° when expanded, auto-expanded via `React.useState<Record<string,boolean>>` defaulting to `item.children.some(child => isActiveNavItem(pathname, child.href, allHrefs))` (the file's OWN existing longest-prefix-match logic, reused unmodified) unless the user has manually toggled that group; every other (leaf) item renders through the EXACT SAME code path as before (the whole `motion.span layoutId="nav-active-pill"` block untouched). The Billing item gained exactly TWO children — **Fee Categories** (`/billing/fee-categories`, the current landing page, unchanged route/content, re-homed) and **Generate Invoice** (`/billing/generate`, new) — no Pending/Upcoming/Collect/Receipts children, per the plan's explicit "don't add dead links" instruction (those routes don't exist until later dispatches).

**i18n**: `shell.nav.billingFeeCategories`/`billingGenerateInvoice` + a new `billing.bulkGenerate.*` namespace (37 keys: form labels, empty/loading states, submit/result copy, 5 `walletOutcome.*` sub-keys) — added identically (English placeholder content, matching sw/fr's own established convention) to `en`/`sw`/`fr`. One deliberate simplification found mid-build: an initial draft used ICU MessageFormat nested `plural` blocks for the result-summary copy (`"Generated {invoices, plural, one {# invoice} other {# invoices}} for..."`) — this codebase has ZERO prior precedent for ICU plural anywhere in any of the 3 message files (confirmed by grep before committing to it), so it was simplified to plain interpolation (`"Generated {invoices} invoice(s) for {students} student(s)."`), matching `common.page`'s own already-established simple-interpolation style, rather than being the first-ever use of an untested pattern.

## Slice 8 (Part 2 — Pending/Upcoming Invoice Lists) — 2026-07-31

**Verdict: Slice 3 (backend) and Slice 4 (frontend) of the same "Billing Invoice Lifecycle" plan are built and verified live end-to-end.** A new paginated, student-joined `BillInvoiceRepository.findOpenPaginated()` query backs two new endpoints (`GET billing/invoices/pending`/`upcoming`), two new list screens reached from the Billing nav dropdown's two new children, and a real "Collect" row action linking into the not-yet-built Collect Fees flow (Slice 5, a later dispatch — the link intentionally 404s until then). Slices 5–7 (Collect Fees, receipt breakdown polish, global Receipts) remain explicitly out of scope for this dispatch.

### Slice 3 — backend: Pending/Upcoming invoice lists

Read `bill-invoice.repository.ts`'s existing `findOverdueOpen()`/`findOpenForStudent()`/`findAllOpen()` first to confirm the established convention — raw `WHERE`/`ORDER BY` string conditions against `balance`/`due_date`/`status` (never TypeORM's `LessThan()`/`MoreThan()`, since `balance` carries a `Money` transformer that those operators would apply to the wrong, transformed value) — before adding a fourth method in the same style.

**New `BillInvoiceRepository.findOpenPaginated(bucket: "PENDING"|"UPCOMING", asOfDate, {skip,take}, manager?)`**: `WHERE balance > 0 AND status <> 'VOID' AND due_date < :asOfDate` (PENDING) / `due_date >= :asOfDate` (UPCOMING — due exactly today lands here, not PENDING, matching `findOverdueOpen()`'s own strict-`<` "overdue" convention), `ORDER BY due_date ASC`, `leftJoinAndSelect("invoice.student","student")` (the entity's own pre-existing `ManyToOne` relation — a to-one join never fans out rows, so `getManyAndCount()`'s count stays correct under `skip`/`take`), returns `{items, total}`.

**A real, non-obvious TypeORM bug found and fixed while building this, not assumed away**: the FIRST implementation used `.orderBy("invoice.due_date", "ASC")` (the raw-column-name style every other method in this file uses) — this crashed at runtime with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'databaseName')`, reproduced and root-caused by reading TypeORM's own compiled source (`SelectQueryBuilder.js`'s `createOrderByCombinedWithSelectExpression()`, triggered specifically by `skip()`/`take()` combined with a join): it resolves `orderBy` entries via `alias.metadata.findColumnWithPropertyPath(propertyPath)`, which only recognizes entity PROPERTY names (`dueDate`), never raw column names (`due_date`) — a gap this file's other 3 methods never hit because none of them join anything. Fixed by using the property-path form, `.orderBy("invoice.dueDate", "ASC")`, documented inline in the method's own doc comment so the next person extending this file with a joined+paginated method doesn't rediscover the same crash. `where`/`andWhere` conditions keep the raw-column-name convention unchanged (that code path never hit the bug).

**New `PendingUpcomingInvoiceResponseDto`/`PendingUpcomingInvoiceListResponseDto`** (`invoice.dto.ts`): invoice fields (`id`/`number`/`dueDate`/`total`/`balance`/`status`) + the joined student's `studentId`/`admissionNo`/`studentName`/`classId`, `{items,total}` envelope matching `ListStudentsResponseDto`'s established shape.

**New `GET billing/invoices/pending`/`GET billing/invoices/upcoming`** on `InvoicesController` — `@RequirePermission("billing:invoice:view")` (confirmed the exact existing permission code, reused, no new permission minted), `@Query() pagination: PaginationQueryDto` + optional `asOfDate` (defaults to `new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)`, the same "today" convention `aging-outstanding.report.ts`/`schedules.controller.ts`/`recurring.controller.ts` already establish). **Declared BEFORE `GET :id`** — same route-ordering reasoning Part 1's own `categories-for-scope` endpoint already documented: Nest/Express matches routes in declaration order, and `:id` would otherwise swallow the literal `pending`/`upcoming` segments as id values; confirmed correct in the real boot log (`Mapped {/api/v1/billing/invoices/pending, GET}` before `Mapped {/api/v1/billing/invoices/:id, GET}`).

**New `packages/server/src/domains/billing/__tests__/pending-upcoming-invoices.integration.spec.ts`** — a real-Postgres integration spec (`AppDataSource`, self-skips without a reachable DB, mirroring `billing-triggers.integration.spec.ts`'s exact harness), not a mocked-QueryBuilder unit test — a mock would only prove the mock was called correctly, not that the real SQL predicate buckets correctly at the due-date boundary. Inserts one real student + 5 real `bill_invoice` rows via raw SQL: due yesterday (POSTED), due exactly today (POSTED), due tomorrow (POSTED), due yesterday but VOID, due yesterday but fully paid (`balance=0`, PAID). Asserts by id presence/absence (robust regardless of how much other real data already exists in whatever dev DB this runs against, deliberately not scoped by `studentId` since the real endpoint isn't either): the yesterday-POSTED invoice lands in PENDING only; the today-POSTED and tomorrow-POSTED invoices land in UPCOMING only; the VOID and the fully-paid overdue invoices land in NEITHER bucket. Also asserts the joined student fields are real (not a second lookup) and a `take`-limits-rows/`total`-reflects-the-whole-set pagination proof.

## Slice 8 (Part 3 — Collect Fees) — 2026-07-31

**Verdict: Slice 5 of the same "Billing Invoice Lifecycle" plan is built and verified live end-to-end — the most safety-critical dispatch in the feature, a real payment-capture code path.** `AllocationService.resolveAllocations()` gained an optional `invoiceIds` scoping filter, threaded through `ReceiptsService.captureReceipt()` and `ReceiptsController.capture()`; ONE shared `CollectFeesFlow` component (reusing the existing student-search + split-row/payment-method building blocks, plus a new `InvoiceSelectionPanel` checklist) now backs both `/billing/collect` entry points — the bare nav link (built this pass) and every Pending/Upcoming row's "Collect" link (built in Part 2, previously a real 404). Verified with 5 real end-to-end scenarios against the live stack and direct `psql` cross-checks, not just unit tests or UI trust. Slice 6 (receipt breakdown display polish) and Slice 7 (global Receipts list) remain explicitly out of scope for this dispatch.

### Backend — directed multi-invoice collection

Read `allocation.service.ts`/`receipts.service.ts`/`receipt.dto.ts`/`receipts.controller.ts` in full first, per the dispatch's own explicit instruction, before touching anything — confirmed exactly how `allocations` flows from `resolveAllocations()` through `pay_receipt_allocation` writes and `applyInvoiceAllocation()`, so the change could be scoped to WHICH invoices get considered, never HOW they're applied.

**`AllocationService`** — `ResolveAllocationsInput` gained `invoiceIds?: string[]`. Inside `resolveAllocations()`: `findOpenForStudent()`'s result (already sorted `due_date ASC`) is filtered in-memory (`.filter(invoice => invoiceIds.includes(invoice.id))`) to the given subset BEFORE the existing FIFO loop, only when `invoiceIds` is present and non-empty — an empty array is treated identically to omitted (unscoped), not as "select nothing," a deliberate choice confirmed by a dedicated test. No new repository method — a student's open-invoice count is always small, exactly as the dispatch anticipated. The FIFO loop, the `toPrepayment` remainder rule (BR-PAY-03), and every line below it are byte-for-byte unchanged — only the candidate list feeding the loop is narrower.

**`ReceiptsService`** — `CaptureReceiptInput` gained `invoiceIds?: string[]`, passed straight through to `resolveAllocations()`. Nothing else in `captureReceipt()`'s 12-step algorithm was touched — the `pay_receipt_allocation` writes, journal posting (P-08/P-09), and `applyInvoiceAllocation()`/`bill_installment` bookkeeping are exercised completely unchanged, just against a possibly-narrower invoice set, exactly as the dispatch required.

**`CaptureReceiptDto`** — gained `invoiceIds?: string[]` (`@IsOptional() @IsArray() @IsUUID(undefined,{each:true})`, `@ApiPropertyOptional`). **`ReceiptsController.capture()`** — passes `dto.invoiceIds` straight through to the service input, no transformation.

**Tests** — `allocation.service.spec.ts` gained a 5-test `describe("invoiceIds scoping")` block, all against a fixed 3-invoice fixture (`invoice-old`/`invoice-mid`/`invoice-new`, oldest-due-first): (a) checking the oldest+newest (skipping the middle, proving real `.filter()`, not "first N" slicing) allocates to exactly those 2; (b) omitted `invoiceIds` — unscoped FIFO across all 3, an explicit regression guard, not just a new-behavior test; (b') an empty array behaves identically to omitted; (c) an amount less than the checked-set total — the older-of-the-checked-set gets fully paid, the newer partially, and the unchecked (cheaper, actually-oldest-overall) invoice gets nothing despite being FIFO-eligible under the unscoped rule; (d) an amount more than the checked-set total — the excess still becomes a `toPrepayment` allocation exactly as today, confirming BR-PAY-03 is unaffected by scoping. `receipts.service.spec.ts` gained a 2-test `describe("captureReceipt — invoiceIds plumbing")` block confirming `captureReceipt()` forwards `input.invoiceIds` to `AllocationService.resolveAllocations()` unchanged, and that omitting it forwards `invoiceIds: undefined` — the exact same call shape every pre-existing caller already makes.

**Verdict: Slices 6 and 7 of the same "Billing Invoice Lifecycle" plan are built and verified live end-to-end — the FINAL two slices of the whole Slice 8 feature.** Receipt allocation rows now resolve and display the real invoice number (`BIL-000090` instead of the generic word "Invoice") and a `toPrepayment:true` row now renders as a distinct `soft-warning` badge reading "Overpayment / credit balance" instead of blending in as a plain row. ### Slice 6 — backend: real invoice numbers on receipt allocations

Read `receipts.controller.ts`'s `findOne()`/`toAllocationView()` and `receipt.dto.ts`'s `ReceiptAllocationResponseDto` in full first (per the dispatch's own explicit instruction), confirming the exact real names before touching anything — both matched the plan's own assumption exactly, no surprises.

**`ReceiptAllocationResponseDto`** (`receipt.dto.ts`) gained `invoiceNumber: string | null` — `@ApiProperty({ type: String, nullable: true })`, the explicit `type: String` deliberate (not just `nullable: true`): a `string | null` union return type can't be reflected by Nest/Swagger's decorator-metadata inference on its own, and omitting it reproduces the exact pre-existing codegen gap `lib/api-error.ts`'s own doc comment already documents for several Students-domain DTOs (an ambiguous placeholder instead of a real `string | null` in the generated `openapi-types.ts`) — caught live during this pass's own contracts-fetch verification step (see below) and fixed outright rather than reproduced in new code.

**`ReceiptsController`** — gained a `BillInvoiceRepository` constructor dependency (barrel import, `../../billing`, the exact same cross-domain-read precedent `AllocationService` already established for this identical repository). `toAllocationView()` moved from a free module-level function to a private async controller method, resolving `invoiceNumber` via `BillInvoiceRepository.findByIdOrFail(entity.invoiceId)` for each non-null-`invoiceId` row (`Promise.all` over the small allocation list — a receipt has at most a handful of allocations, same small-N-lookup precedent `domains/reporting`'s aging report already uses), `null` unconditionally for the `toPrepayment:true` row. `findOne()`'s only other change: `allocations.map(toAllocationView)` (sync) became `await Promise.all(allocations.map((a) => this.toAllocationView(a)))` (async) — nothing else in that method touched.

### Slice 7 — backend: the new permission + migration

Read `permission-catalogue.ts` and grepped every migration numbered after `0900` before writing anything — confirmed (not assumed) that **no later migration anywhere in this codebase yet shows the precedent for "add one new permission after the initial 0900 seed"**; this dispatch is the first.

**`permission-catalogue.ts`** gained `payments:receipt:view-all` (`isWrite: false`) — a real, separately-granted scope escalation over the existing `payments:receipt:view` (per the plan's own explicit judgement call: "seeing every family's payment history unscoped is a real privacy escalation over viewing one student's own receipts").

**New `packages/server/src/migrations/0230-add-payments-receipt-view-all-permission.ts`** — deliberately does NOT edit the already-applied `0900-seed-permissions-and-roles.ts` (a migration that has already run against a real environment is never edited retroactively — TypeORM only re-runs migrations it hasn't recorded yet, so editing `0900` now would have zero effect here and would misrepresent what that migration actually did when it ran). Idempotent (`usr_permission` upsert by `code`, `ON CONFLICT (code) DO UPDATE`, same shape `0900`'s own loop uses) and grants the new permission to `System Admin` (every permission) and `Auditor` (BR-SEC-04 — every `isWrite:false` permission), the same two roles `0900` would have granted it to had it existed at seed time — `ON CONFLICT (role_id, permission_id) DO NOTHING`, same shape `0900`'s own `grantPermission()` helper uses. Role names (`"System Admin"`/`"Auditor"`) are duplicated as local literals rather than imported from `0900`'s own (unexported) consts — the correct direction of dependency for a later migration referencing an earlier one's seeded data by natural key, not its private constants. **Applied live**: `pnpm --filter server run migration:run` — `AddPaymentsReceiptViewAllPermission1700000000230 has been executed successfully`, confirmed via the migration's own query log (real `usr_permission`/`usr_role_permission` INSERT statements, real ids).

### Slice 7 — backend: the paginated/filterable query + the third `list()` mode

Read `receipts.controller.ts`'s `list()` (confirmed it throws `ValidationException` when neither `studentId` nor `sessionId` is given, exactly as the dispatch described) and `pay-receipt.repository.ts` in full first.

**New `PayReceiptRepository.findAllPaginated(filters, pagination)`** — `filters: {studentId?, cashierId?, dateFrom?, dateTo?, method?}` (the plan's own literal signature; `studentId` included for the method's own general-purpose reuse value even though `ReceiptsController.list()` itself never reaches this branch WITH a `studentId` set — that always short-circuits to the pre-existing `listByStudent()` branch first). `leftJoinAndSelect("receipt.student"/"receipt.cashier", ...)` — both pre-existing `ManyToOne` relations on `PayReceiptEntity`, both to-one, so neither fans out rows under pagination (same safe-to-paginate reasoning `BillInvoiceRepository.findOpenPaginated()` already documents). `orderBy("receipt.receiptDate", "DESC")` uses the property-path form deliberately, not the raw-column form this file's other methods use — **the exact same real TypeORM pagination-plus-join bug `BillInvoiceRepository.findOpenPaginated()`'s own doc comment already found and documents was avoided here from the start** by following that precedent, not rediscovered. `method` filters via a raw `EXISTS` subquery against `pay_receipt_split` (method lives on the SPLIT, not the receipt) rather than an `innerJoin` — a receipt can carry two splits of the same method, which an `innerJoin` would fan out into duplicate rows under pagination; `EXISTS` never can.

**`ReceiptsController.list()`** — gained a THIRD mode. `studentId`-given and `sessionId`-given branches are the exact original two lines, completely untouched (confirmed by diff, not just by intent). When neither is given: resolves the caller's granted permissions via `resolveGrantedPermissions(user, this.redis)` — the exact same dynamic, hand-rolled permission check `ReportsController.execute()` already established for its own "a route needs a permission code a static `@RequirePermission` can't express" situation (`platform/auth/application/permission-check.util.ts`'s own doc comment) — and rejects with a real `AuthorizationException` (403) if `payments:receipt:view-all` is missing. `@RequirePermission("payments:receipt:view")` on the route decorator itself is UNCHANGED — it still gates all three branches at the coarse level, with the third branch additionally hand-checking the stricter code. New constructor deps: `BillInvoiceRepository` (Slice 6, above) and `@Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) redis: Redis` — no `payments.module.ts` edit needed for either: `BillInvoiceRepository` is already exported via `BillingModule` (already imported into `PaymentsModule`), and `REDIS_CLIENT` is a `@Global()` provider (`SharedInfraModule`, imported once by `AppModule`) — confirmed by reading both files first rather than assuming.

**New `ReceiptListItemResponseDto extends ReceiptResponseDto`** (`studentName`/`cashierName`, empty-string-fallback join fields, same shape `PendingUpcomingInvoiceResponseDto` already establishes) and **`ReceiptListResponseDto`** (`{items, total}` envelope). **A real, deliberate Swagger-schema choice, not previously needed anywhere else in this codebase**: since `GET /payments/receipts` now returns either a bare `ReceiptResponseDto[]` (studentId/sessionId branches) OR the `ReceiptListResponseDto` envelope (global branch) depending on runtime query params — a genuine polymorphic response shape for one route — the `@ApiResponse` decorator uses a real `oneOf` schema (`@ApiExtraModels(ReceiptListResponseDto)` + `getSchemaPath()`), the first use of this pattern anywhere in this codebase (confirmed by grep before adding it — no precedent existed). Verified this generates correctly in the live fetched spec (see Contracts regen below) and that `packages/contracts`' zod-schema codegen (which source-scans `*.dto.ts` files directly via `class-validator` reflection, entirely independent of how a controller's `@ApiResponse` references a DTO — confirmed by reading `generate-zod-schemas.ts` directly before assuming this would "just work") picked up both new DTO classes regardless.

### Slice 7 — frontend: extended `ReceiptsTable` + the new `/billing/receipts` screen

Read `receipts-table.tsx`'s two existing call sites (`students/[id]/page.tsx`'s Receipts card, `payments/page.tsx`'s "this session's receipts" card — both bare unbounded arrays, client-side `<DataTable>` pagination, no `serverPagination`) in full first, confirming changes could stay additive.

### Closing summary — the full 4-part Slice 8 "Billing Invoice Lifecycle" feature, end to end

This dispatch closes out all 7 slices of the plan (`docs/phase-6/PROGRESS.md`'s own `tidy-puzzling-snowflake.md` plan document), delivered across 4 separate dispatches over one day. For anyone reading this later without wanting to piece it together from 4 separate part-sections, here is what the whole feature delivers, in the order a user actually walks through it:

1. **Generate** (Part 1, Slices 0–2) — a new bulk "Generate Invoice" screen (`/billing/generate`): pick an academic year + term, a grade, one or more fee categories via an always-visible chip picker, then a checkbox grid of that grade's active students — submits to a new `POST billing/invoices/bulk-generate` endpoint that generates ONE invoice per distinct due-date group per student (reusing the existing, already-tested `InvoicingService.generateInvoice()`/`.postInvoice()` verbatim, zero new invoice-creation logic), with an optional "collect from student wallet" checkbox that sequentially calls the existing single-invoice wallet transfer endpoint per succeeded invoice. This dispatch also built the sidebar's first-ever expand/collapse nav group mechanism, which every later part simply extended.
2. **See what's owed** (Part 2, Slices 3–4) — two new due-date-driven list screens, "Pending Invoices" (`/billing/pending`, already overdue) and "Upcoming Invoices" (`/billing/upcoming`, not yet due), backed by a new paginated, student-joined `BillInvoiceRepository.findOpenPaginated()` query — each row's "Collect" action links into Part 3's flow with the student/invoice pre-filled.
3. **Collect, directed** (Part 3, Slice 5) — a cashier can now check exactly which of a student's several open invoices a payment should apply to (`/billing/collect`, one shared `CollectFeesFlow` component reached both bare from the nav and pre-filled from any Pending/Upcoming row), via a new optional `invoiceIds?` field on `CaptureReceiptDto`/`AllocationService.resolveAllocations()` that narrows the existing FIFO-by-due-date allocation loop to a caller-picked subset — the unscoped, "apply across ALL open invoices" behavior every other existing caller (cheques, suspense, M-Pesa, bulk allocation, the plain cashier capture form) relies on stays byte-for-byte unchanged when `invoiceIds` is omitted.
4. **See the breakdown, and see everything** (Part 4, Slices 6–7, this section) — a captured receipt's own detail page now shows the REAL invoice number for each allocation (not a generic label) and calls out an overpayment/prepayment row with a distinct badge instead of blending it in as a plain row; and a new, separately-permissioned (`payments:receipt:view-all`) global Receipts screen (`/billing/receipts`) lets an authorized user see every receipt across every student, paginated and filterable by date range/cashier/method — completing the "Generate → Collect → Receipt" cycle the whole feature set out to build, and completing the Billing nav dropdown at exactly 6 children with no more planned.

Every slice reused existing, already-tested backend primitives wherever one existed (`InvoicingService`, `AllocationService`, `BillInvoiceRepository`, the existing `pay_receipt_allocation` table, `resolveGrantedPermissions()`) rather than inventing parallel mechanisms — the only genuinely new pieces of infrastructure across all 4 parts were the nav dropdown mechanism itself (Part 1), the `invoiceIds` directed-allocation scoping (Part 3), and the `payments:receipt:view-all` permission (Part 4, this dispatch). Zero new DB migrations were needed for 6 of the 7 slices — the one exception is this dispatch's own `0230`, seeding exactly one new permission row.

A new shared `<StkStatusPanel>` polls the new GET endpoint, gates a "Resend" behind a live 60s countdown, and offers a "Check now" Daraja status-query nudge — mounted in `SplitRow`'s new `MPESA_STK` branch (Collect Fees) and in place of `StkInitiateForm`'s old manual "check for receipt" button. Parts B/C/D (search UX, chip picker polish, per-student item-based invoicing) are explicitly OUT of scope for this dispatch — `domains/billing`/`features/billing` were not touched.

Read `split-row.tsx`/`stk-initiate-form.tsx`/`collect-fees-flow.tsx`/`capture-form-state.ts`/`use-mpesa.ts`/`mpesa.api.ts` in full first, confirming the method-conditional extra-fields pattern and the existing `useInitiateStk()`/API-call conventions before extending them. `capture-form-state.ts`'s `selectedInvoiceIds` mechanism itself was NOT touched — only read, from `collect-fees-flow.tsx`, exactly as scoped.

**New `apps/web/src/features/payments/components/stk-status-panel.tsx`** (`<StkStatusPanel transaction onResend>`) — given the transaction `initiateStk()` just returned, polls `GET payments/mpesa/:id` via `useMpesaTransaction()` (new hook, `use-mpesa.ts`) whose `refetchInterval` is a function of the CACHED data's own `state` (react-query v5's `(query) => number|false` form — `3000`ms while `INITIATED`/`PENDING`, `false` the instant a terminal state (`CONFIRMED`/`FAILED`/`TIMEOUT`/`REVERSED`) lands, no separate `enabled` flag to keep in sync). A local `RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 60` countdown (`setInterval` ticking off `Date.now() - initiatedAt`) gates "Resend" until it reaches 0 or the transaction turns terminal (a terminal FAILED/TIMEOUT/REVERSED state enables Resend immediately — no point waiting out a countdown on an already-dead transaction). "Check now" calls the new `useQueryMpesaStatus()` mutation (`POST .../query-status`), writing straight into the SAME query-cache entry `useMpesaTransaction()` reads via `queryClient.setQueryData()` so the panel reflects the result instantly. "Resend" calls the caller-supplied `onResend()` (expected to be a fresh `initiateStk()` call with the same amount/msisdn/student/`invoiceIds`), then re-points the panel at the NEW transaction id and restarts its own countdown — a genuinely new `pay_mpesa_transaction`/`checkoutRequestId` each time, never a retry of the same one (Safaricom STK prompts are single-use). On `CONFIRMED`: a success `<Alert variant="success">` with a real `<Link href="/payments/receipts/{matchedReceiptId}">`. On `FAILED`/`TIMEOUT`/`REVERSED`: a `<Alert variant="destructive">` failure state with Resend enabled.

### Contracts regen sequence — a real deviation caught and self-corrected

Rebuilt `packages/server` (clean) → stopped `apps/api`'s process tree (PIDs `32900`/`22572`/`26928`) → restarted (`pnpm --filter @klickit/api run start:dev`, new PID `41408`) → confirmed clean boot, all 3 new/changed routes mapped in the live boot log → fetched the LIVE `GET /api/docs-json` → confirmed the new operations (`MpesaController_findOne`, `MpesaController_queryStatus`) and `InitiateStkDto.invoiceIds` present in the fetched JSON.

**A real mistake made and caught before it could silently ship**: the first `pnpm --filter contracts run generate` pass was run WITHOUT first writing the freshly-fetched spec into `packages/contracts/openapi.json` (the actual codegen input `generate-types.ts` reads from — its own doc comment states this plainly, re-confirmed by reading the script directly) — the fetched JSON had only been saved to a scratchpad file. `generate-zod-schemas.ts` (which source-scans `*.dto.ts` files directly, independent of `openapi.json`) correctly picked up `invoiceIds` regardless, but `generate-types.ts`'s output (`openapi-types.ts`, the typed `apiClient` paths the frontend calls through) was silently generated from the STALE pre-dispatch `openapi.json` still on disk — confirmed missing: `grep` for `payments/mpesa` in the regenerated `openapi-types.ts` showed only the pre-existing `stk`/`b2c` paths, NOT the 2 new ones. Caught before writing any frontend code that would have referenced the missing paths (`getMpesaTransaction()`/`queryMpesaStatus()` hadn't been written yet). Fixed by writing the fetched spec into `packages/contracts/openapi.json` (BOM-free) and re-running `generate` — confirmed both new paths present afterward, THEN wrote the frontend API wrappers against the corrected types.

`pnpm --filter contracts run generate` → **445 DTO classes, 2190 properties translated**, same 16 pre-existing duplicate-`operationId` disambiguations every prior regen has logged (unchanged) → `pnpm --filter contracts run build` clean → `pnpm --filter contracts exec jest --maxWorkers=2` → **891/891 passing**.

**Note on how this section came to be written**: the build agent dispatched for this part hit two consecutive infrastructure failures (a dropped connection, then a session-limit cutoff) right as it began its own verification/reporting phase — it never produced a self-report. Rather than risk a third interrupted attempt, I (the orchestrating session) independently investigated the actual state of the code directly — reading every changed file in full, confirming `tsc`/lint/tests myself, and cross-checking real residue left in the dev database from the agent's own interrupted verification run — before writing this section myself. Every claim below is something I personally confirmed by reading the real code or querying the live database, not a relayed agent report.

Real test residue (throwaway students `SL9-D1/D2/D3-msevqq2h` and `SL9-D1/D2/D3-msevutv2`, real `PAID`/`VOID` invoices `BIL-000110`–`BIL-000115`, real receipts `PAY-000073`/`PAY-000074`) was found already sitting in the dev DB — direct evidence the agent had reached real end-to-end testing of Part D (both same-due-date and different-due-date category groupings, one cohort per suffix) before being cut off.

Threaded through as an optional query param on `InvoicesController`'s pending/upcoming endpoints and `ReceiptsController.list()`'s global-mode branch.

Frontend: a search `<Input>` above each of the Pending/Upcoming table (`open-invoices-table.tsx`) and the global Receipts screen, wired to the new `q` param via `useDebouncedValue()`, firing only once 2+ characters are typed. `student-selection-grid.tsx` (bulk Generate Invoice) instead got a plain **client-side** `.filter()` over its already-fetched ≤200-row list — no network round trip, confirmed by reading the component (no new query, no debounce needed there).

`FeeCategoryChipPicker` (`features/billing/components/fee-category-chip-picker.tsx`) gained a `FILTER_THRESHOLD = 12` constant: at or below that option count, it renders the exact same unadorned `flex flex-wrap` chip row as before (confirmed by reading the code — an early `return` preserves the original markup byte-for-byte for the common case).
