### Follow-up — `assignDepartment` relation-staleness bug fixed (2026-08-06, during independent verification of this part)

The `assignDepartment` defect documented above was fixed immediately, the same way and for the same reason Part 3's `headUserId` defect was: it directly breaks the "Assign Department" dialog this part shipped on the User detail page — the single most-used assignment action in the whole module — for its second most basic use case (changing or clearing a department after it's already been set once).

**Root cause, empirically confirmed live before fixing** (throwaway role `Verify UserDept Fix Role` scoped to `users:user:{create,view,assign-department,deactivate}`+`users:department:{create,view}`, throwaway user `verify.userdept`, target user `verify.deptbugtarget`, two throwaway departments A/B): the FIRST-ever assignment (`null → Dept A`) genuinely persisted correctly in the database (`psql`-confirmed) but its OWN immediate PATCH response lied, reporting `departmentId: null`. Every SUBSEQUENT change (`A → B`) both lied in the response AND failed to persist — `psql` after the "successful" switch to B still showed Dept A. This is the identical `UsrUserEntity` shape as `UsrDepartmentEntity`'s own bug: a scalar `departmentId` column plus a `@ManyToOne`/`@JoinColumn department` relation on the same `department_id` column, with `findByIdOrFail()` (via `UsrUserRepository.findById`) eager-loading `department` since Part 1 — a loaded-but-unsynced relation object wins over the scalar in TypeORM's `save()`.

**Fix applied to `UsersService.assignDepartment()`** (`packages/server/src/platform/users/application/users.service.ts`): identical shape to Part 3's own fix — `user.department` is now kept in sync with `user.departmentId` on every call (`null` when clearing, a minimal `{ id: departmentId } as UsrDepartmentEntity` reference when switching/setting).

New regression tests: `packages/server/src/platform/users/__tests__/users.service.spec.ts`, new `describe("UsersService.assignDepartment — departmentId/department sync ...")` block (3 cases: clear syncs to `null`, switch syncs to the new reference, and the very-first-assignment-from-null case).

**Live re-verification after the fix, same throwaway data**: switch A→B (`200`, `departmentId` correctly B), clear (`200`, `departmentId` correctly null), switch back to A (`200`, `departmentId` correctly A) — `psql` confirmed the database matches the last request at every step this time, and a fresh `GET` immediately after showed both the correct `departmentId` AND the correctly-joined `departmentName` (the immediate PATCH response's own `departmentName` stays blank right after a mutation, same as Part 3's fix — a real but cosmetic-only limitation of the lightweight `{id}` reference object, not a correctness issue; any real consumer that invalidates/refetches after a successful mutation, which this part's own `AssignDepartmentDialog` does, never observes it). All throwaway users deactivated afterward.

`pnpm --filter server exec tsc --noEmit` clean. `pnpm --filter server exec jest "platform/users" --maxWorkers=2` → **5/5 suites, 25/25 tests passing** (up from 22 — the 3 new regression tests, zero regressions elsewhere). `apps/api` rebuilt and restarted to pick up the fix (new PID `24736`→ still `24736` after this restart, process was replaced in place); `apps/worker`/`apps/web` untouched. All three dev servers healthy, 7 `node.exe` processes, nothing extra left running.

**This closes out the duplicate-scalar-plus-relation bug class entirely for this module** — both real instances found across the whole of Slice 13 (`UsrDepartmentEntity.headUserId`/`headUser` in Part 3, `UsrUserEntity.departmentId`/`department` here) are now fixed and regression-tested. The broader audit suggestion below (checking whether this exact shape recurs elsewhere in the codebase, and whether `@RelationId()` should replace the duplicate-`@Column` pattern generally) remains worth doing as separate, dedicated work — but nothing from Slice 13 itself is left in a known-broken state.

## Slice 13 — closing summary (Parts 1–4 complete)

Phase 6 Slice 13 built the first-ever frontend for `platform/users` (the backend's "Module 1" — Users/Roles/Departments/Permissions), a module that predates almost every other one in this codebase but had zero UI before this slice, across 4 parts.

- **Part 1** (backend): a real, confirmed security defect fixed as first priority — `UsersController`'s handlers were returning the raw `UsrUserEntity` straight to callers with `passwordHash` (a bcrypt hash), `twofaSecretEnc`, and `recoveryCodesEnc` all present verbatim in the response body, confirmed live before the fix and confirmed absent from all 24 final routes' response bodies after it. Bundled with the response-DTO retrofit that made every later part's real, generated `@klickit/contracts` types possible, plus 5 new routes (`GET/DELETE .../roles`, `GET/DELETE .../permissions`, `GET /permissions`) wiring up service-layer logic that had existed with zero controller access before.
- **Part 2** (frontend): `/roles` and `/roles/[id]` — the module's first nav entry, role CRUD, and the 259-code/24-module permission grant/revoke table with instant, no-confirm toggle-on-click semantics.
- **Part 3** (frontend): `/departments` — department CRUD with a head-of-department picker. Found (during its own live verification, not by luck) a real backend defect: `PATCH /departments/:id` silently failed to persist a CHANGED or CLEARED head-of-department once one was already set, while its own response claimed success — root-caused to a duplicate scalar-column-plus-relation shape on `UsrDepartmentEntity` causing TypeORM to derive the persisted FK from a stale, unrefreshed relation object rather than the freshly-set scalar. **Fixed the same day, by direct orchestrator intervention**, with a small, surgical change (`DepartmentsService.update()` now keeps the `headUser` relation object in sync with the scalar it's mutating) plus 3 new regression tests — re-verified live, both the clear and switch cases confirmed genuinely persisting afterward.
- **Part 4** (frontend, this section): `/users`, `/users/new`, `/users/[id]` — the richest and highest-traffic screen in the module, consuming Parts 2/3's `features/roles`/`features/departments` directly for its two assignment pickers, per the plan's own specified dependency direction. Its own centerpiece is the temp-password reveal (`TemporaryPasswordReveal`) — the first server-generated-secret-shown-once UI anywhere in this codebase, with a deliberately escalated "no auto-navigation, explicit copy-with-confirmation, explicit click-through" design. Found (again during its own live verification, the same discipline as every other part) that the IDENTICAL class of defect Part 3 found and fixed for Departments also existed in `UsersService.assignDepartment()` — confirmed live, and **fixed the same day, by direct orchestrator intervention** (see this part's own follow-up section above), the same surgical relation-sync fix plus 3 new regression tests, re-verified live afterward.

**The two most consequential findings of this whole module**: (1) Part 1's real, live-confirmed security defect — every caller with `users:user:view` could read any user's bcrypt password hash and encrypted 2FA secret/recovery-code material straight out of a normal API response, for as long as this module has existed with no frontend to ever surface the problem; and (2) a real backend defect class — found twice, independently, during ordinary frontend verification rather than a dedicated security/QA pass — where an assignment endpoint (`PATCH /departments/:id`'s head-of-department in Part 3, `PATCH /users/:id/department` in Part 4) silently lied about success while leaving the database untouched, caused by the same duplicate-scalar-plus-relation entity shape in both `UsrDepartmentEntity` and `UsrUserEntity`. **Both instances were fixed the same day each was found**, not deferred — underscoring that this shape is a real, repeatable footgun in this codebase's ORM layer, not a one-off mistake. A broader audit (`@RelationId()` instead of a duplicate `@Column`, everywhere this exact shape might recur elsewhere in the codebase) remains worth doing as separate, dedicated work, but nothing discovered during Slice 13 itself was left unfixed.

Across all four parts: `pnpm turbo run typecheck lint --filter=@klickit/web --force` clean at the end of every dispatch; every backend claim verified with real, live HTTP round trips cross-checked directly against `psql`, never API-response trust alone; the same narrowest-sufficient-throwaway-role/user discipline used consistently, with every throwaway user account explicitly deactivated afterward (a live identity/access-surface row, unlike a throwaway role or department, which have no delete path anywhere in this codebase and are left in place by established precedent). No browser-automation tool was available at any point across the whole slice — every part honestly states this rather than fabricating interactive-UI verification, relying instead on live API round trips using the exact request/response shapes the built components call, plus SSR/i18n-bundle checks for what IS observable without one. All three dev servers (`apps/api` 3000, `apps/worker` 3001, `apps/web` 3002) are healthy as of this final part, with the standard 7 `node.exe` processes and nothing extra left running.

## Slice 13 follow-up — search fields on Users/Roles/Departments — 2026-08-06

Post-Slice-13 request: a search field on each of the three list pages. Implemented directly (no dispatch — small, well-bounded, in files just built and independently verified in Parts 2–4).

**Two genuinely different shapes, per each screen's real data-loading pattern**:
- **Roles and Departments** — plain CLIENT-SIDE substring filters, no backend change. Confirmed by reading `RolesController.list()`/`DepartmentsController.list()` directly: both return every row unpaginated (small, unbounded datasets, matching Parts 2/3's own established "no server pagination" scope). `app/(erp)/roles/page.tsx` filters on name+description; `app/(erp)/departments/page.tsx` filters on name+headUserFullName — same "Select/Input filters an already-loaded array" shape `settings/academic-calendar/page.tsx`'s own `yearSearch` precedent already established, not the debounced-server-search shape used for genuinely paginated data.
- **Users** — a real, debounced, SERVER-SIDE search (`?q=`), because `GET /users` is genuinely paginated (157+ real rows in this dev environment) — a client-side-only filter would silently only search whatever happened to be on the current page. Required a small, targeted backend addition since no search capability existed on this endpoint before:
  - `UsrUserRepository.list()` (`packages/server/src/platform/users/infrastructure/`) — new `q?: string` option, one `ILIKE` clause across `username`/`fullName`/`email`/`phone`.
  - `UsersService.list()` / `UsersController.list()` — threaded through; new `@ApiQuery({name:"q"})` on the controller (correctly generates as an optional string in `@klickit/contracts`, confirmed directly against `generated/openapi-types.ts`'s `UsersController_list` entry — unlike the pre-existing `departmentId`/`status` codegen quirk this same endpoint already has).
  - Frontend: `app/(erp)/users/page.tsx` gained the exact `WalletsTable`-established debounced-search shape (`useDebouncedValue`, 300ms, `MIN_SEARCH_LENGTH = 2`, resets to page 1 on a genuinely new search term) — the first reuse of that shared hook/pattern for this module.
  - Contracts regenerated (rebuild → restart `apps/api` → fresh `/api/docs-json` → `pnpm --filter contracts run generate/build`).

**Verification**: `pnpm --filter server exec tsc --noEmit` clean before AND after the contracts regen. `pnpm --filter server exec jest "platform/users" --maxWorkers=2` → 5/5 suites, 25/25 tests, no regression. `pnpm turbo run typecheck lint --filter=@klickit/web --force` → 4/4 clean. Live, real HTTP round-trip against the running stack (throwaway role `Verify Search Role` scoped to exactly `users:user:view`, throwaway user `verify.search`, deactivated afterward): `GET /users?q=verify.search` → `total:1`, matched on username; `GET /users?q=Verify Search` → `total:1`, matched on fullName; `GET /users?q=zzz-no-such-user-zzz` → `total:0` — confirms the ILIKE search genuinely reaches the database and isn't a client-side illusion. i18n: `searchPlaceholder` (all three namespaces) + `noRolesMatchSearch`/`noDepartmentsMatchSearch` (empty-result-after-filtering copy) added to `en.json`/`sw.json`/`fr.json`, real English/Swahili/French translations, all three files valid JSON and in sync at 2317 lines each (up from 2312).

All three dev servers healthy throughout (`apps/api` restarted once to pick up the backend search route, `apps/worker`/`apps/web` untouched), steady-state 7 `node.exe` processes at the end.

## Slice 14 (Part 1 — Branding Foundation: List + 5-Section Theme Editor + File Picker) — 2026-08-06

Frontend-only, per the approved plan's explicit scope boundary — no `packages/server` file touched (the backend at `platform/branding/` and `platform/files/` was read, not edited). Built the first-ever frontend for `platform/branding` (Module 4): the themes list, and a full 5-section create/edit theme editor (Identity, Colors, Login page, Documents, Theme defaults) including the file-upload picker widget every non-color section needs to be functionally complete. Nothing is publish-able yet (Part 2's own scope) — every theme this part can create or show stays `DRAFT`.

### What was built

**`features/branding/`**:
- `api/themes.api.ts` — `createTheme`/`listThemes`/`getTheme`/`updateTheme`, real generated `CreateThemeDto`/`UpdateThemeDto`/`ThemeResponseDto` types from `@klickit/contracts` directly, no hand-typing. `publish`/`revert`/`preview` deliberately left unwrapped, with a doc comment naming them as Part 2's job.
- `api/files.api.ts` — `uploadFile` (first real multipart upload anywhere in this app) and `getSignedUrl`.
- `hooks/use-themes.ts` / `hooks/use-file-upload.ts` — mirror `features/users/hooks/use-users.ts`'s exact `listKey`/`detailKey`/invalidation shape.
- `constants.ts` — `FILE_ENTITY_TYPE = "BRND_THEME"`, `HEX_COLOR_PATTERN` (byte-for-byte mirror of the backend's own regex), the real `@MaxLength` constants for every text field.
- `components/theme-status-badge.tsx`, `file-picker.tsx`, `signature-picker-list.tsx`, `color-field.tsx`, `colors-section.tsx`, `identity-section.tsx`, `login-section.tsx`, `documents-section.tsx`, `theme-defaults-section.tsx`, `theme-editor-form.tsx`.

**Routes**: `app/(erp)/branding/page.tsx` (list, client-side name filter, mirrors `academic-calendar/page.tsx`'s `yearSearch`), `app/(erp)/branding/new/page.tsx` (seeds defaults from a real `fetch("/api/theme")` call, not a 4th hardcoded default bundle), `app/(erp)/branding/[id]/edit/page.tsx`.

**Nav**: `{ href: "/branding", labelKey: "branding", icon: Palette, allowedRoles: [] }` inserted between Users and Settings in `nav-links.tsx`.

**i18n**: new `branding` top-level namespace (`list`, `status`, `newPage`, `editPage`, `form.{identity,colors,login,documents,defaults}`, `filePicker`) + `shell.nav.branding`, real English/Swahili/French translations for every key actually rendered, cross-checked against every `t("...")` call in the built components. `common.upload` reused verbatim in `FilePicker`'s empty state, not duplicated.

### Real judgment calls

1. **File-id form sentinel is `undefined`, never `null`.** The real zod schemas (`CreateThemeDtoSchema`/`UpdateThemeDtoSchema`) have no `.nullable()` on `logoFileId`/`faviconFileId`/`loginConfig.backgroundImageFileId` — a `null` reaching `zodResolver` fails validation for real. Every `FilePicker` binding coalesces at the boundary (`value={field.value ?? null}` / `onChange={(v) => field.onChange(v ?? undefined)}`).
2. **A real, confirmed codegen gap on `UpdateThemeDto.{logoFileId,faviconFileId}` — the OPPOSITE direction from every prior gap in this codebase.** The GENERATED OpenAPI request type correctly has `logoFileId?: string | null` (server declares `nullable: true`), but the zod-mirror generator dropped `.nullable()`, leaving the inferred TS type `logoFileId?: string`. Fixed with a local `UpdateThemePayload` type (`themes.api.ts`) restoring the real `string | null | undefined` shape for exactly these two fields — structurally identical to the generated type, so **no cast is needed** passing it to `apiClient.PATCH` (unlike `users.api.ts`'s `assignDepartment`/`setAuthorityLimit`, which close a gap in the opposite direction and do need one).
3. **`loginConfig.backgroundImageFileId` deliberately does NOT reuse the `logoFileId`-style null-clearing diff.** Confirmed directly against `LoginConfigDto`'s DTO class, generated OpenAPI type, AND zod schema: all three agree it's plain `string | undefined`, never `null` (no `nullable: true` on this one, unlike `logoFileId`/`faviconFileId`). Since `UpdateThemeDto.loginConfig` is sent as one atomic whole-object replacement when it changes at all, simply omitting `backgroundImageFileId` from the reconstructed sub-object already clears it server-side — no `null` sentinel needed or accepted. `diffFileId()` (the real three-way-diff helper, mirroring `EditDepartmentDialog`'s `headUserId` convention) is used only for the two fields that genuinely need it: top-level `logoFileId`/`faviconFileId`.
4. **The `FormData` cast** — `openapi-fetch`'s `defaultBodySerializer` passes a `FormData` instance through untouched, but the generated `POST /files` request-body type doesn't structurally match one. Same `as unknown as X` convention `users.api.ts`'s `AssignDepartmentRequestBody` already establishes (`files.api.ts`'s `UploadFileRequestBody`).
5. **`/api/theme` seeding + blank-name-on-seed.** `branding/new/page.tsx` seeds every field from a real `fetch("/api/theme")` response (the existing same-origin route wrapping the public `GET /branding/theme/current`) — a real network response, not a 4th hardcoded mirror of the Infoney defaults (3 already exist and are a known, deliberate smell). `name` is the one field deliberately NOT copied from the seed — it starts as `""`, since two themes sharing a name would be indistinguishable in the list, while `name` exists specifically to identify a new draft.
6. **Edit-mode diffing** — `name` sent iff changed; `tokens`/`documentConfig`/(reconstructed) `loginConfig` compared via whole-object `JSON.stringify` (21 leaf token fields, one atomic DTO field server-side — simpler and equally correct vs hand-diffing every leaf, matching the plan's own reasoning); success shows a local `<Alert variant="success">` that clears itself on the next form edit (via `form.watch`), and the form **stays on the page** after a successful edit (unlike create, which navigates to `/branding`).
7. **Remove never calls `DELETE /files/:id`** — `FilePicker`'s Remove only clears the local reference. `FilesService`'s own doc comment documents files as immutable (delete-and-reupload, never edit); this leaves orphaned `file_object` rows on swap, an accepted, documented tradeoff (storage GC is separate, deferred work), not silently hidden.

### A real infrastructure gap found and fixed during verification (not code — dev environment provisioning)

`docker-compose.dev.yml` defines only `postgres`/`redis` — **no MinIO service exists anywhere in this dev environment**, despite `.env` pointing `MINIO_ENDPOINT` at `localhost:9000` and `platform/files`' `MinioStorageAdapter` having no fallback. The first real upload attempt failed with a real `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` (confirmed genuinely, not assumed) because there was nothing listening on port 9000. Fixed by starting a standalone `minio/minio` container (`docker run`, matching `.env`'s `minioadmin`/`minioadmin` credentials and `9000`/`9001` ports) and creating the `klickit-files` bucket via `mc mb` — after which uploads succeeded for real. This is an environment-provisioning fix, not a `packages/server` code change, so it stays inside this dispatch's "frontend only" scope; the container is left running (it's a real stack dependency now, same status as `postgres`/`redis`, not a throwaway). Adding a permanent `minio` service to `docker-compose.dev.yml` is worthwhile follow-up work for whoever next needs file uploads in a fresh environment, noted here rather than silently patched around.

### Real judgment calls

1. **The preview pane's scoped-CSS-variable technique reuses the REAL design-system primitives, not a re-implementation.** `app/layout.tsx` writes `buildSemanticLightVariables`/`buildSemanticDarkVariables`'s output as two GLOBAL `:root`/`:root[data-theme="dark"]` blocks. For a preview embedded in a real admin page, that's wrong (it would repaint the whole admin chrome). Instead, `theme-preview-pane.tsx` sets the exact same variable names as an inline `style` on ONE wrapper `<div>` — CSS custom properties inherit down the tree and the closest ancestor wins, so the override never escapes that subtree. Confirmed directly against `tailwind.config.ts` before relying on it: `bg-card`/`bg-primary`/`text-foreground`/`bg-secondary`/etc. are ALREADY aliased straight to `var(--card)`/`var(--primary)`/`var(--foreground)`/`var(--secondary)` — the exact names the two builder functions return — so **no Tailwind arbitrary-value syntax (`bg-[var(--card)]`) was needed at all**; the real `Card`/`Button`/`Badge` components render correctly scoped with zero special-casing. One deliberate exception: the `soft-*` Badge variants were avoided — their `bg-tint-primary`-style tokens are `color-mix()`-derived once at `:root` in `styles/tokens.css` using `:root`'s own `--primary`/`--card`, and a descendant inherits the already-resolved color rather than re-running `color-mix()` against the local override, so they'd silently show the ADMIN APP's own tint, not the previewed theme's. `variant="secondary"` (plain `bg-secondary`/`text-secondary-foreground`, both genuinely scoped) was used for the sample badge instead.
2. **`style={vars as React.CSSProperties}` compiles clean with a direct cast** — confirmed by reading the installed `@types/react@19.2.17`'s own `CSSProperties` doc comment (index signature deliberately removed, "use type assertion... to add properties"), and confirmed for real by `pnpm turbo run typecheck lint --filter=@klickit/web --force` passing with this exact cast, no `unknown` intermediate needed.
3. **The exact 422 message is deliberately NOT run through next-intl.** `publishedEditBlockedMessage()` (`constants.ts`) returns the literal server string, used verbatim in both the list page's `title` attribute and the editor's warning `Alert`. This matches the codebase's own established "server-generated error text is shown verbatim, never translated" convention (`theme-editor-form.tsx`'s own root-error rendering already did this for every OTHER server error) — translating a string that exists specifically so an admin can compare it against the real API response would be actively counterproductive.
4. **Disabled Edit is a real `<button disabled>`, never a `Button asChild` wrapping a disabled `Link`.** Checked `button.tsx` before writing this: HTML's `disabled` attribute has no effect on an `<a>` element, and `buttonVariants`' `disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50` styling is keyed on the `:disabled` CSS pseudo-class, which `<a>` doesn't support either — a "disabled" Link would have neither the right look nor the right click-prevention. The list page branches to a genuine `<button type="button" disabled title={...}>` instead for `PUBLISHED` rows.
5. **`RevertThemeButton` always renders** (no internal `status === "ARCHIVED"` check) — the list page's own Revert column cell decides whether to render it at all. `PublishThemeButton` DOES branch internally (badge vs. button) because every row needs SOMETHING in that column, including `PUBLISHED` rows; there's no equivalent "always show something" requirement for Revert.
6. **The client-side PATCH-prevention guard is a real early return, not just visual.** `theme-editor-form.tsx`'s `onValid()` returns immediately when `isReadOnly` is true, before any mutation call — belt-and-suspenders alongside the hidden submit button and `disabled` fields, matching the plan's explicit "do NOT attempt to call PATCH at all in this state" instruction.

## Slice 14 (Part 3 — Orphaned Consumers: Sidebar Logo, Favicon, Login Background + Backend Signed-URL Bundling) — 2026-08-06

The one part of Slice 14 that touches `packages/server`, per the approved plan's own scoping. `logoFileId`/`faviconFileId`/`loginConfig.backgroundImageFileId` are bare `file_object` UUIDs; resolving one to a displayable image requires `GET /files/:id/signed-url`, which is `@RequirePermission("files:file:view")`-guarded (confirmed directly by reading `files.controller.ts` — no `@Public()` path exists). The sidebar logo needs to render for any authenticated staff user regardless of whether they hold `files:file:view`; the favicon and login background need to resolve for a fully unauthenticated request (a browser's own favicon fetch carries no bearer token; the login page is pre-auth). Fixed the small, real, necessary way: `ThemesService` now resolves signed URLs in-process via an injected `FilesService` (a normal service-to-service DI call, never over HTTP, so the permission guard is never in the request path) and bundles them into the already-`@Public()` `GET /branding/theme/current` response — extending the same "one bundle carries everything pre-auth chrome needs" pattern that endpoint already used for `cssVariables`/`tokens`/`loginConfig`/`documentConfig`.

### What was built

**Backend (`packages/server/src/platform/branding/`)**:
- `api/dto/current-theme-response.dto.ts` — 3 new `@ApiProperty({nullable: true, type: String})` fields: `logoUrl`, `faviconUrl`, `loginBackgroundImageUrl` (all `string | null`), each documented with the graceful-degradation rule below.
- `application/themes.service.ts` — `ResolvedThemeBundle` gained the same 3 fields. `toBundle()` is now `private async`, resolving all 3 URLs in parallel (`Promise.all`) via a new private `resolveFileUrl()` helper that calls `FilesService.getSignedUrl(fileId, 86400)` when a fileId is set. `preview()` now `await`s `toBundle()`. `getCurrentTheme()`'s own hardcoded-fallback branch (no `brnd_theme` row published yet) sets all 3 new fields to `null` directly — it already has `logoFileId`/`faviconFileId: null`, so no `FilesService` call is needed on that branch at all.
- `branding.module.ts` — imports `FilesModule` (already exported `FilesService`/`STORAGE_PORT`, confirmed by reading `files.module.ts`'s `exports` array directly; already permitted by `module-deps.json`'s `platform/branding.mayImport`, which already listed `platform/files`; no circularity — `platform/files` has no dependency back on `platform/branding`). `ThemesService`'s constructor gained a 4th injected param, `FilesService`.
- New `SIGNED_URL_EXPIRY_SECONDS = 86400` constant in `themes.service.ts` — the max value `SignedUrlQueryDto`'s own `["60","300","900","3600","86400"]` enum accepts. Reconciled the two services' differing typings deliberately: `SignedUrlQueryDto.expirySeconds` is `string | undefined` ONLY because it's parsing an HTTP query-string value in `FilesController`; the actual `FilesService.getSignedUrl(fileId: string, expirySeconds: number = 300)` signature takes a plain `number`. Since `ThemesService` calls `FilesService` directly in-process (never over HTTP), it passes the plain number `86400` — no string coercion needed or correct.
- `packages/server/src/platform/branding/__tests__/themes.service.spec.ts` — extended the existing suite's `ThemesService` constructor call with a mocked `filesService: { getSignedUrl: jest.Mock }` (4th constructor arg), and added a new `describe("toBundle — signed URL resolution (Slice 14 Part 3)", ...)` block with 3 new tests: resolves all 3 URLs correctly when all 3 file ids are set (asserts the exact `86400` expiry is passed for each), returns `null` for every URL field whose file id is unset without calling `FilesService` at all, and — the graceful-degradation case — resolves `null` for one URL without failing the whole bundle when `FilesService.getSignedUrl()` rejects for that one id specifically (the other, working id still resolves correctly in the same bundle).

### The graceful-degradation judgment call

`resolveFileUrl()` wraps its `FilesService.getSignedUrl()` call in a try/catch, logging a `Logger.warn` and returning `null` on any failure rather than letting the rejection propagate. In practice this should essentially never fire — the `ON DELETE RESTRICT` FK between `brnd_theme.logo_file_id`/etc. and `file_object` makes a dangling reference very unlikely — but a single corrupt/orphaned file reference (e.g. a row written before that constraint existed, or a transient storage-layer failure) must not 500 the one public endpoint every authenticated AND unauthenticated page load depends on. A broken logo shouldn't break the entire login page. This mirrors the same "don't let one bad reference break the whole bundle" reasoning already implicit in `getCurrentTheme()`'s own hardcoded-fallback path.

### Frontend (`apps/web`)

- `lib/theme-server.ts` — `FALLBACK_THEME` gained `logoUrl: null, faviconUrl: null, loginBackgroundImageUrl: null` (required once the regenerated `CurrentThemeResponseDto` type gained the 3 fields — `tsc` would otherwise correctly flag this hardcoded fallback object as missing required properties).
- `components/layout/sidebar.tsx` — `Sidebar()` now also calls `getCurrentThemeServer()` (the same call `(auth)/layout.tsx` already makes, no new fetch logic) alongside its existing `getTranslations()` call. When `theme.logoUrl` is present, renders a real `<img src={theme.logoUrl} alt="" className="h-6 w-6 shrink-0 rounded-[2px] object-contain" />` in place of the static diamond glyph; when absent, the original `<span aria-hidden ... bg-brand-accent />` glyph renders completely unchanged — augmenting real brand identity, not unconditionally replacing it. Used the same `eslint-disable-next-line @next/next/no-img-element` precedent `file-picker.tsx` already established (a signed, time-limited MinIO URL isn't something `next/image`'s remote-pattern allowlist fits).
- `app/icon.tsx` (new) — a dynamic Next.js icon route (App Router file convention). Confirmed before writing it that no `favicon.ico`/`app/icon.*` existed anywhere in this app. Fetches `getCurrentThemeServer()`; if `theme.faviconUrl` is present, does a plain server-side `fetch()` against the signed URL and returns `new Response(bytes, {headers: {"Content-Type": <the real content-type the storage layer returned>}})` — proxying the real bytes rather than redirecting the browser to a time-limited, MinIO-hosted URL a browser's favicon cache shouldn't be coupled to. On any failure (or when unset), falls back to a `next/og` `ImageResponse` rendering a small rotated-square version of the sidebar's own diamond motif, colored with the resolved theme's real `tokens.colors.accent` (never a hardcoded hex) — so a published theme's own color choice shows up even in the generated fallback icon. `export const size = { width: 32, height: 32 }; export const contentType = "image/png";` per the file convention.
- `app/(auth)/layout.tsx` — the dark brand panel's existing inline `style` object (previously just `{fontFamily: "var(--font-family)"}`) is now built conditionally: when `theme.loginBackgroundImageUrl` is present, also sets `backgroundImage: url(...)`, `backgroundSize: "cover"`, `backgroundPosition: "center"`; otherwise the panel stays exactly `bg-brand-dark` as before, byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Slice 14 (Part 4 — WCAG Contrast Checker) — 2026-08-06

The closing part of Slice 14. Purely additive frontend work, per the approved plan's own scope — no `packages/server` file touched, and no dependency on Parts 1–3's own new code paths (though it lives inside `colors-section.tsx`, a file Part 1 created and deliberately left with a "no WCAG contrast badges here — Part 4's own scope" doc comment as its own insertion point). Wires a real WCAG AA contrast checker into the theme editor's Colors section, checking the 2 color pairs that are genuinely load-bearing foreground/background relationships in this app's actual rendering (`lib/theme.ts`'s `buildSemanticLightVariables`) — `dark` vs `surface` (the real text-on-background pair) and `primary` vs `surface` (the real label-on-button-background pair, roles inverted) — not a generic N×N matrix over all 9 colors.

### What was built

- `features/branding/lib/contrast.ts` (new) — pure color math, reusing `relativeLuminance`/`mixHex` from `lib/theme-colors.ts` rather than a second implementation (that file's own primitives were built for dark-mode derivation, but the WCAG math is identical). `contrastRatio(hexA, hexB)` — the standard `(L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05)` formula, order-independent (uses the lighter/darker luminance via `Math.max`/`Math.min`, not argument position). `WCAG_AA_NORMAL_TEXT_THRESHOLD = 4.5` + `meetsWcagAA(ratio)` — the WCAG 2.1 AA threshold for normal text specifically (not large text's 3.0, not AAA's 7.0). `suggestNearestCompliantColor(foreground, background)` — a bounded iterative walk (`t = 0.02, 0.04, ... 1.0`) mixing `foreground` toward both pure black and pure white in lockstep, returning whichever direction first reaches AA compliance at the smaller `t` (the least-disruptive visual change), with a documented proof this always terminates by `t = 1.0` for a real hex background (the black-compliant and white-compliant luminance ranges overlap and together cover `[0, 1]`), plus a defensive (practically unreachable) black/white fallback.
- `features/branding/components/contrast-indicator.tsx` (new) — a small `ContrastIndicator` component rendering a `Badge` (`soft-success` + `Check` icon when passing, `soft-destructive` + `AlertTriangle` icon when failing, matching the `soft-*` badge convention already established across the app) showing the numeric ratio (e.g. "4.8:1"), an `sr-only` pass/fail label for screen readers (the icon+color pairing alone isn't enough for a checker whose whole point is accessibility), and — only when failing — a `Button variant="link"` reading "Use {hex} instead" that calls the field's own `onChange` with `suggestNearestCompliantColor`'s result, a real committed form-value change, not just a visual suggestion.
- `features/branding/components/colors-section.tsx` (modified) — added `useWatch({ control, name: "tokens.colors.surface" })` to reactively read the live `surface` value, and a `CONTRAST_CHECKED_KEYS` set (`primary`, `dark`) gating which 2 of the 9 `Controller` renders also mount a `ContrastIndicator` beneath their `ColorField`, wired to that same `Controller`'s own `field.value`/`field.onChange`. `ColorField` itself is completely unmodified — the indicator is a sibling in the render tree, not a prop threaded into it.
- i18n: 4 new keys under `branding.form.colors` in all 3 locale files — `contrastRatio` ("{ratio}:1"), `contrastPass`/`contrastFail` (the `sr-only` accessible labels), `contrastUseSuggestion` ("Use {hex} instead"), real English/Swahili/French text, matching the existing `{placeholder}` ICU interpolation convention (`t("contrastRatio", { ratio: ... })`, the same shape `delete-student-button.tsx`'s own `t("description", { name })` already establishes).

### Verification

`pnpm turbo run typecheck lint --filter=@klickit/web --force` → **4 successful, 4 total**, 0 errors/0 warnings. i18n: `en.json`/`sw.json`/`fr.json` all valid JSON, in sync at **2454 lines each** (up from 2450), and a full recursive key-set diff (not just line count) confirmed **zero differences** across all 3 files, 1994 keys each. Math sanity-checked via a throwaway inline `node -e` one-liner (no file left behind) hand-copying the luminance/ratio formulas: `contrastRatio("#000000", "#FFFFFF")` → exactly `21` (the real WCAG max); `contrastRatio("#573399", "#FDFDFE")` (Infoney's real production `primary`/`surface` pair) → `≈8.83`, comfortably above the 4.5 AA bar, a sane result for a deliberately-chosen dark-purple-on-near-white brand pairing. No backend/database touch and no live HTTP round-trip needed or attempted — this is pure client-side color math and form UI, confirmed sufficient by the approved plan itself.

### Dev servers

Untouched this part — no restart needed (pure frontend edit, no contracts regen). All three remained healthy throughout: `apps/api` 3000, `apps/worker` 3001, `apps/web` 3002, the standard 7 `node.exe` processes, nothing extra running.

## Slice 14 — closing summary (Parts 1–4 complete)

Phase 6 Slice 14 built the first-ever frontend for `platform/branding` (the backend's "Module 4" — theme tokens, login-page/document branding, logo/favicon/signature file uploads), across 4 parts.

- **Part 1** (frontend): the themes list and a full 5-section create/edit theme editor (Identity, Colors, Login page, Documents, Theme defaults), plus the file-upload picker widget every non-color section needs. Nothing publish-able yet — every theme stayed `DRAFT`. Found and fixed a real dev-environment infrastructure gap along the way (no MinIO service existed anywhere in the dev stack despite `.env` pointing at it) — a standalone MinIO container was started and left running as a genuine, permanent stack dependency, not a throwaway.
- **Part 2** (frontend): the Draft → Preview → Publish → Revert workflow — a live preview pane rendering the draft's real CSS variables, publish/revert actions, and a read-only-when-published editor guard matching the real server-side 422 rule (`ThemesService.update()`) client-side, not just as a UI courtesy.
- **Part 3** (backend + frontend): the one part that touched `packages/server`, per the approved plan's own scoping. Resolved the "orphaned consumers" problem — the sidebar logo, browser favicon, and login-page background image all needed a displayable URL from a bare `file_object` UUID, but the real signed-URL endpoint is permission-guarded and some of these consumers render pre-auth (favicon, login page) or for any authenticated user regardless of permission (sidebar). Fixed by resolving signed URLs in-process inside `ThemesService` (a normal DI call, never over HTTP, so the guard is never in the request path) and bundling them into the already-`@Public()` `GET /branding/theme/current` response. Verified end-to-end with zero bearer token anywhere in the chain: fully unauthenticated requests fetched real, byte-matching images for all 3 consumers.
- **Part 4** (frontend, this section): the WCAG AA contrast checker — inline pass/fail badges with a one-click "use a compliant color instead" fix, wired into exactly the 2 real, load-bearing foreground/background color pairs (`dark`/`surface`, `primary`/`surface`) this app's own rendering actually uses, not a generic matrix over all 9 brand colors.

Across all four parts: `pnpm turbo run typecheck lint --filter=@klickit/web --force` clean at the end of every dispatch; every backend claim in Parts 1–3 verified with real, live HTTP round trips cross-checked directly against `psql`, never API-response trust alone (Part 4 needed neither, being pure client-side logic, and honestly says so rather than fabricating a round-trip that wasn't necessary); the same narrowest-sufficient-throwaway-role/user discipline used consistently in every part that touched the live stack, with every throwaway user account explicitly deactivated afterward. No browser-automation tool was available at any point across the whole slice — every part relies on live API round trips and SSR/i18n-bundle checks instead of fabricated interactive-UI verification. i18n grew from 2317 lines (pre-slice) to 2454 lines (post-Part-4) across all 3 locales, staying in sync and valid JSON throughout. All three dev servers (`apps/api` 3000, `apps/worker` 3001, `apps/web` 3002) are healthy as of this final part, with the standard 7 `node.exe` processes and nothing extra left running. Module 4 (Branding) is now a functionally complete, accessible, end-to-end frontend.

Needed for `comm_template.body` (real, multi-line message content with `{{variableName}}`-style placeholders) and its optional `variables` JSON field. Same hand-authored-native-element convention `checkbox.tsx`/`input.tsx` already establish, same token classes.

**4. Nav wiring** — new top-level `children`-bearing dropdown positioned between Wallet and Users (`Megaphone` icon, confirmed unused elsewhere in `nav-links.tsx` and a real `lucide-react` export), with exactly ONE child so far (`{ href: "/communications/templates", labelKey: "commsTemplates" }`). Explicitly commented as NOT this dropdown's final shape (unlike Settings'/Wallet's "FINAL shape" comments) — Parts 2–4 each append one more real child (Broadcasts/Messages/Optouts, Trigger Bindings, My Devices), the same incremental-append discipline Billing's/Wallet's/Users' own nav history already established.

**5. i18n** — new `communications` top-level namespace (`list`, `channels`, `createDialog`, `editDialog`, `deleteDialog`) + 2 new `shell.nav` keys (`communications`, `commsTemplates`) in `en.json`/`sw.json`/`fr.json`, real English/Swahili/French translations for every string actually referenced by the built components. Copy describing `{{variableName}}`-style placeholders was deliberately written WITHOUT literal curly braces (e.g. "Wrap a variable name in double curly braces… to insert it", not literal `{{variableName}}` text) — a literal `{` in next-intl/ICU MessageFormat static copy starts an argument-placeholder parse, and unescaped nested braces (`{{...}}`) or a bare `{` immediately followed by a non-identifier character (e.g. the JSON example `{"guardianName": ...}`) would either fail to parse or render incorrectly; avoiding literal braces entirely in static copy sidesteps this without needing per-string ICU quote-escaping (confirmed unescaped apostrophes like "doesn't"/"student's" are already safe throughout this codebase's existing i18n files — ICU only treats `'` specially when immediately followed by `{`, `}`, `#`, or another `'`).

### Judgment calls

- **A real, confirmed codegen gap on `locale`/`isActive`/`variables`** — the same class of gap `features/roles/api/roles.api.ts` documents for `isAuditorClass` and `features/settings/api/custom-fields.api.ts` documents for `options`. Server-side, `CreateTemplateDto.locale`/`.isActive` are `@ApiPropertyOptional({default:...})` (genuinely optional, zod-inferred type correctly has them as `?`), but `@nestjs/swagger` drops the optional signal for that shape, so the generated request-body type has them non-optional. Separately, `variables` is `@ApiPropertyOptional({type:Object})`, which `openapi-typescript` renders as `Record<string, never>` instead of the real `Record<string, unknown>`. Fixed the same way `custom-fields.api.ts` fixes the identical class of gap: local `CreateTemplateRequestBody`/`UpdateTemplateRequestBody` interfaces matching the REAL generated shape field-for-field + a targeted `as unknown as {...}` cast at the one call boundary in `templates.api.ts` that hits it — the real runtime JSON round-trips correctly either way, confirmed live below.
- **`variables` edited as a raw JSON textarea, not a structured builder** — unlike `set_custom_field_def.options` (which this app commits to a flat string-array shape for its one realistic SELECT-choices case), `comm_template.variables` is genuinely arbitrary, docs-only JSON (`TemplatesService.render()` never validates it) with no single realistic shape to special-case, so a plain optional JSON textarea (parsed client-side, rejected with an inline error before submit if invalid) is the honest, simplest real form for it.
- **No delete confirmation via a separate `AlertDialog` primitive** — confirmed by listing `components/ui/` first that no such primitive exists anywhere in this codebase; every real "delete with confirm" flow (`DeleteClassButton`, `DeleteFeeStructureButton`, and now `DeleteTemplateButton`) is a plain `<Dialog>` with a destructive confirm button, not a new pattern.

**Live, real HTTP + `psql` round-trip** (a throwaway role `Slice15Part1 Verify Comms Templates` was minted directly via `INSERT INTO usr_role`/`usr_role_permission` — the INSERT omitted a `version` column, which is correct: `UsrRoleEntity` (`platform/users/domain/usr-role.entity.ts`) extends plain `BaseEntity`, not `MutableBaseEntity`, so `usr_role` has no `version` column by design — **correction, verified during Part 1's independent review**: the build agent's original note here claimed this was a "real, pre-existing entity/schema drift," which is inaccurate and has been corrected; granted exactly `comms:template:view`/`comms:template:manage`/`users:user:deactivate`; a throwaway user `slice15part1.verify` was minted directly via `INSERT INTO usr_user` + `usr_user_role` with a real bcrypt hash generated via this repo's own `bcryptjs` dependency at 12 rounds — matching `PasswordService`'s own `BCRYPT_ROUNDS` — then logged in via real `POST /auth/login` for a real bearer token; narrowest-sufficient scope, same discipline as every prior slice):

### Judgment calls

- **A real, confirmed codegen gap on `estCostAmount`** — the same class of gap Part 1 documents for `locale`/`isActive`. Server-side, `CreateBroadcastDto.estCostAmount` is `@ApiPropertyOptional({default:"0"})` (genuinely optional, zod-inferred type correctly has it as `?`), but `@nestjs/swagger` drops the optional signal for that shape, so the generated request-body type has it non-optional. Fixed the same way `templates.api.ts` fixes the identical class of gap: a local `CreateBroadcastRequestBody` interface matching the REAL generated shape field-for-field (including the non-optional `estCostAmount`, deliberately NOT relaxed — see that file's own doc comment for why declaring it required there costs nothing real) + a targeted `as unknown as {...}` cast at the one call boundary in `broadcasts.api.ts` that hits it. `audienceDef`'s nested `roleId`/`userIds` needed no such fix — both are already correctly optional in the generated type.
- **`approvalRef` generated client-side via `crypto.randomUUID()`, never a form field** — per `BroadcastsController.submitForApproval()`'s own doc comment, the real appr_* approval workflow engine is Module 6 (Approvals), not built yet: "this endpoint does not validate or resolve the reference against anything," any uuid is accepted. Asking an admin to type in a value that's genuinely meaningless to them today would be dishonest UX; the button's real, visible EFFECT (the DRAFT -> PENDING_APPROVAL transition) is completely real, only the specific `approvalRef` value is a placeholder. No user-facing note about this gap either — that would undermine trust in a real, correct feature for no reason. Live-verified below: the exact client-generated uuid landed in `comm_broadcast.approval_ref`.
- **Only `send` gets a confirm dialog** — submit-for-approval/approve/cancel mirror `PublishThemeButton`'s "reversible-enough, no confirm needed" reasoning. `send` resolves the real audience and fans out real `comm_message` rows — the one genuinely irreversible action in the lifecycle — so it gets the same plain-confirm-dialog shape `DeleteTemplateButton` (Part 1) already established. The confirm dialog deliberately does NOT quote `recipientCount` (confirmed by reading `BroadcastsService.send()` directly: it's `0` until resolved mid-transaction, so showing it pre-send would be misleadingly wrong).
- **A real, newly-discovered backend gap, out of scope to fix here (frontend-only slice)**: `AudienceDefDto.userIds` is validated with `@IsUUID("4", { each: true })` — UUID **v4** specifically — but every entity in this codebase (including `usr_user.id`) is a UUID**v7** primary key by design (`BaseEntity`'s own doc comment: "UUIDv7 PK (time-ordered for index locality), DR-007"). This means `EXPLICIT_USER_IDS` as currently validated server-side can never accept a real, normally-created `usr_user.id` — confirmed live: two genuine v7-format active user ids were rejected with `"each value in userIds must be a UUID"` before this was diagnosed. Worked around for THIS verification only by using two accounts whose ids happen to be genuine v4 (both minted via plain `gen_random_uuid()` rather than the app's own v7 generator) — the frontend code itself (`audience-picker.tsx`/`create-broadcast-dialog.tsx`) sends whatever id `useUsersLookup()` returns unmodified, so it is NOT the source of this gap and needs no change; the real fix (loosening `@IsUUID("4", ...)` to version-agnostic `@IsUUID()`, matching `roleId`'s own already-version-agnostic `@IsUUID()`) belongs in a future backend-touching pass. Flagged here explicitly rather than silently worked around, per this codebase's "real, honest gap" discipline.

This run also rebuilt `@klickit/server`/`@klickit/contracts` per the turbo graph, both clean too, confirming this part genuinely touched no backend file. Dev servers survived the rebuild (`Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 3000,3001,3002` → all 3 still listening, 7 `node.exe` processes, no restart needed).

**i18n**: all three files valid JSON (`ConvertFrom-Json`, all VALID) and in sync at **2601 lines each** (`ReadAllLines`/raw-split-count, en/sw/fr identical; +73 lines each for the new `communications.broadcasts` namespace, +1 each for the new `shell.nav.commsBroadcasts` key, on top of Part 1's 2527-line baseline).

**Live, real HTTP + `psql` round-trip** (a throwaway role `Slice15Part2 Verify Comms Broadcasts` was minted via `INSERT INTO usr_role`/`usr_role_permission`, granted exactly `comms:broadcast:create`/`:view`/`:approve-submit`/`:send`/`users:user:deactivate`; a throwaway actor user `slice15part2.verify` was minted via `INSERT INTO usr_user`/`usr_user_role` with a real bcrypt hash generated via this repo's own `bcryptjs` dependency at 12 rounds, then logged in via real `POST /auth/login` for a real bearer token — narrowest-sufficient scope, same discipline as every prior slice; a first attempt at inserting the hash directly through a PowerShell-quoted `docker exec ... psql -c "..."` string silently corrupted it via shell `$`-escaping — caught immediately by the subsequent login returning `401`, fixed by piping a `.sql` file into `docker exec -i psql` instead, which sidesteps inline-string escaping entirely):

4. `POST .../approve` → real `200`, `status:"APPROVED"`.
5. `POST .../send` → real `200`, `status:"SENT"`, `recipientCount:1` — `psql` on `comm_message` confirmed exactly 1 real row for this `broadcast_id` (`channel:"EMAIL"`, `recipient:"bootstrap.admin@klickit.local"`, `status:"SENT"`), correctly narrowed down from the role's 20 active members to the 1 that actually has a usable email address, matching `resolveAudience()`'s own documented per-channel contact-field filtering.

**Frontend rendering** — not live-browser-tested this part either (no browser-automation tool available in this environment, same as every prior slice); the dialog/detail-page/action-cluster code was statically traced against the real component code and confirmed indirectly by the identical-shaped live API round-trip in steps 1–8 above (every button/dialog's submit handler calls the exact same `createBroadcast`/`submitForApproval`/`approveBroadcast`/`cancelBroadcast`/`sendBroadcast` functions exercised live).

### Cleanup

Three throwaway users deactivated via the real `PATCH /users/:id/deactivate`: the actor `slice15part2.verify` (self-deactivated, confirmed `DEACTIVATED` in the response), a second throwaway recipient user `slice15part2.recipient` (minted solely to supply a second genuine-v4-format real user id for the `EXPLICIT_USER_IDS` test) and a third throwaway `slice15part2.cleanup` user (minted, reusing the same still-live throwaway role, specifically to deactivate the recipient and then itself — needed because the actor was already `DEACTIVATED` by that point and a deactivated user cannot log in to perform further cleanup actions; no password_hash was ever reused across any of these — each is a genuinely new `INSERT INTO usr_user` row, matching this environment's established remedy for the "can't act as an already-deactivated throwaway user" problem). The throwaway role `Slice15Part2 Verify Comms Broadcasts` is left in place, obviously-throwaway-named, same "no delete path exists, don't invent one" precedent Part 1 established for roles. Both verification `comm_broadcast` rows (`SENT` and `CANCELLED`) are left in place too — no `DELETE /comms/broadcasts/:id` route exists anywhere (confirmed by reading `BroadcastsController` directly), matching the same precedent.

### Correction — found and fixed during independent verification (2026-08-06)

The build agent's own report flagged (as an "honest, out of scope" backend gap) that `AudienceDefDto.userIds` (`packages/server/src/platform/comms/api/dto/audience-def.dto.ts`) validated with `@IsUUID("4", { each: true })` — version-4-only — while every real `usr_user.id` in this codebase is a UUIDv7 (`BaseEntity`'s own established convention across all 21 backend modules), meaning `EXPLICIT_USER_IDS` broadcasts could never work with real user ids in production. On review this was judged in-scope to fix directly (a one-line, contained, unambiguous bug, not a scope expansion) rather than leave open: changed to `@IsUUID(undefined, { each: true })`, matching `roleId`'s own unversioned `@IsUUID()` just above it. Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `jest comms --maxWorkers=2` → 5/5 suites, 33/33 tests still passing (no test pinned the old v4-only behavior), `apps/api` rebuilt+restarted to pick up the change, and a fresh live `POST /comms/broadcasts` with two REAL, existing `usr_user.id` values (both genuine UUIDv7) succeeded end-to-end where it previously would have been rejected — confirmed via `psql` that `audience_def` stored both real ids correctly. Throwaway verify user `slice15part2.uuidv7fix` deactivated afterward.

## Slice 15 (Part 3 — Messages, Optouts, Trigger Bindings) — 2026-08-06

Three smaller admin screens, added as the 3rd, 4th, and 5th (and FINAL) children of the existing Communications nav dropdown: `/communications/messages` (a READ-ONLY, server-paginated delivery-log view of `comm_message` — no mutation endpoint exists for this table anywhere, confirmed by reading `MessagesController` directly), `/communications/optouts` (search-by-guardianId-first, since there is no guardian/student directory anywhere in this codebase yet and `GET /comms/optouts` has no "list all" mode), and `/communications/trigger-bindings` (direct structural mirror of Part 1's Templates list, full CRUD except delete). Frontend only, per this part's scope — no backend file touched (all 3 controllers/DTOs were read, not edited). My Devices (Part 4) deliberately does NOT land in this dropdown — it lives under the user menu instead, per the plan.

### What was built

**1. `features/comms/` additions** — `api/query-params.ts` (the `optionalQuery()` helper, the first file under `features/comms/api/` that needed one — Parts 1/2's `listTemplates()`/`listBroadcasts()` take no query params at all), `api/messages.api.ts` (`listMessages`, with a hand-declared `ListMessagesResponseDto` — see judgment calls), `api/optouts.api.ts` (`createOptout`/`listOptoutsByGuardian`/`deleteOptout`), `api/trigger-bindings.api.ts` (`createTriggerBinding`/`listTriggerBindings`/`getTriggerBinding`/`updateTriggerBinding`, no `delete*` — no delete route exists), `hooks/use-messages.ts` (`useMessages`, `["comms","messages"]` query-key convention sibling to Parts 1/2's own keys), `hooks/use-optouts.ts` (`useOptoutsByGuardian`/`useCreateOptout`/`useDeleteOptout`, `["comms","optouts","guardian",id]` detail-style keying so each guardian's cached list is invalidated independently), `hooks/use-trigger-bindings.ts` (`useTriggerBindings`/`useTriggerBinding`/`useCreateTriggerBinding`/`useUpdateTriggerBinding`), `components/message-status-badge.tsx` (5-state soft-tint badge), `components/create-optout-dialog.tsx` (guardianId/channel/scope, with an optional `defaultGuardianId` prop and a client-side UUID-shape pre-check), `components/delete-optout-button.tsx` (mirrors `DeleteTemplateButton`'s trigger+confirm-dialog+error-banner shape exactly), `components/create-trigger-binding-dialog.tsx` (eventCode/channel/isEnabled/audienceRule, mirrors `CreateTemplateDialog`), `components/edit-trigger-binding-dialog.tsx` (only `isEnabled`/`audienceRule` editable, `eventCode`/`channel` shown read-only via `<ChannelBadge>`, mirrors `EditTemplateDialog`).

**2. Messages list** (`app/(erp)/communications/messages/page.tsx`) — direct structural mirror of `app/(erp)/billing/receipts/page.tsx`'s real server-pagination precedent: a Filters `Card` (status `<Select>`, entityType/entityId/broadcastId plain `<Input>`s, all optional, resetting `page` to 1 on any change via `React.useEffect`) + a list `Card` with `<DataTable serverPagination>` inside `<QueryBoundary isEmpty>`. Columns: channel badge, recipient, template event, status badge, provider, sent/delivered timestamps, error (shown in destructive text when present). No row actions anywhere — read-only, per the backend's own one-route-only shape.

**3. Optouts screen** (`app/(erp)/communications/optouts/page.tsx`) — a guardianId search `<Input>` gated behind an explicit Search button/Enter key (not fired per-keystroke — a uuid lookup key isn't a substring search), with a client-side UUID-shape check before the request fires. Before any search, a clear explanatory `Card` is shown instead of an empty table (`noSearchYet`) — an empty table would wrongly imply "this guardian has no opt-outs" when really nothing has been searched yet. `<CreateOptoutDialog defaultGuardianId={searchDraft...}>` pre-fills from whatever's currently in the search box.

Trigger Bindings list** (`app/(erp)/communications/trigger-bindings/page.tsx`) — direct structural mirror of `app/(erp)/communications/templates/page.tsx`: header with title + `<CreateTriggerBindingDialog>` trigger, `<DataTable>` inside `<QueryBoundary isEmpty>`, columns Event Code/Channel (badge)/Status (badge, from `isEnabled`)/Actions (`<EditTriggerBindingDialog>` only — no delete action, no delete route exists). No search field — small, admin-configured dataset, per this part's own plan.

Nav wiring** — appended `commsMessages`/`commsOptouts`/`commsTriggerBindings` as the 3rd/4th/5th children of the existing Communications dropdown (`nav-links.tsx`), and updated both Part 1's forward-reference comment and added a new comment block declaring this dropdown's FINAL shape — matching the exact "FINAL shape, no more children planned" wording Settings'/Wallet's own entries already use. My Devices (Part 4) is called out explicitly as living under the user menu instead, not this dropdown.

### Judgment calls

- **A real, confirmed codegen gap on the Messages list response envelope — a different flavor from Parts 1/2's request-body gaps.** `MessagesController.list()` returns a plain `interface ListMessagesResponseDto` declared locally in the controller file (not a class in a `*.dto.ts` file), and its `@ApiResponse({status:200})` carries no `type`. `@klickit/contracts`' codegen only scans `*.dto.ts` files (confirmed by reading `generate-zod-schemas.ts`'s own header), so this envelope was never picked up there either — unlike `ListWebhookDeliveriesResponseDto` (a real class in `webhook-delivery.dto.ts`, which DOES have a generated zod schema + a real `content` type). The generated `MessagesController_list` operation therefore has `content?: never`. Fixed by hand-declaring the same `{items, meta}` shape in `messages.api.ts`, reusing the real `MessageResponseDto` for `items` — since `unwrapApiResult`'s `data` parameter is already typed `unknown`, no `as unknown as` cast was needed at this call site (unlike every request-body-side gap Parts 1/2 document).
- **Two real, confirmed codegen gaps on `CreateTriggerBindingDto`, the exact same two classes Part 1 documents for Templates' `isActive`/`variables`** — `isEnabled` (`@ApiPropertyOptional({default:true})`, generated non-optional) and `audienceRule` (`@ApiPropertyOptional({type:Object,nullable:true})`, generated as the empty-object-only `Record<string,never>|null`). Fixed the same way `templates.api.ts` does: local `CreateTriggerBindingRequestBody`/`UpdateTriggerBindingRequestBody` interfaces matching the REAL generated shape + a targeted `as unknown as {...}` cast at both call boundaries (`updateTriggerBinding` needed one too, since `audienceRule`'s gap applies there as well — confirmed directly against `components["schemas"]["UpdateTriggerBindingDto"]`, which has no `isEnabled` gap, only the `audienceRule` one).
- **`CreateOptoutDto` had NO codegen gap** — a deliberate contrast worth noting: `guardianId`/`channel`/`scope` are all required on both the real DTO and the generated OpenAPI shape (no `@ApiPropertyOptional({default})` field to trip the swagger bug), so `optouts.api.ts`'s `createOptout()` passes the dto straight through with no local interface or cast, unlike every other `create*` function across all 3 parts of this slice.
- **Optouts' honest plain-`<Input>` guardianId, both directions** — `CreateOptoutDto.guardianId` has no FK (confirmed in that DTO's own `@ApiProperty` description: "no FK yet — students/guardians module, #8, not built"), so neither the create dialog's field nor the page's search key could honestly be a picker/combobox — a plain `<Input>`, with only a client-side UUID-shape regex check ahead of the real server-side `@IsUUID()` validation, is the honest real shape here.
- **Messages page's `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = 10`, not the server's own default of 20** — `<DataTable>`'s `PAGE_SIZE_OPTIONS` is a fixed `[10,25,50,100]` list; seeding local state with `20` (not in that list) would show a page-size `<Select>` with no matching option selected. Matches `billing/receipts/page.tsx`'s own `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = 10` for the identical reason — the frontend still sends an explicit `pageSize` on every request, so this never depends on the server's own default.
- **`MessageStatusBadge` tone mapping**: `QUEUED` soft-secondary (neutral/pending), `SENT` soft-warning (in flight, not yet confirmed — same tone `BroadcastStatusBadge` gives its own `SENDING`/`PENDING_APPROVAL`), `DELIVERED` soft-success, `FAILED` soft-destructive, `OPTED_OUT` plain `outline` — deliberately distinct from `FAILED`'s destructive tone, since a recipient opting out isn't a delivery error.
- **No delete UI anywhere for Trigger Bindings** — confirmed by reading `TriggerBindingsController` directly: it has `create`/`list`/`findOne`/`update` only, no `DELETE` route. Same "no delete path invented" precedent every other Comms screen (and most of this codebase) follows.

## Slice 15 (Part 4 — My Devices) — 2026-08-06

`/my-devices` — the fourth and FINAL part of Slice 15, self-service device-token management for `DeviceTokensController` (`packages/server/src/platform/comms/api/device-tokens.controller.ts`, confirmed by reading it directly: no `@RequirePermission` anywhere, JWT-authenticated only, `userId` always taken from the token's `sub` claim, mirroring `AuthController`'s own `password/change`). My Devices page** (`app/(erp)/my-devices/page.tsx`) — plain `<div className="space-y-6">` header + `<Card>` body, same shape every other Comms screen from Parts 1–3 uses, deliberately NOT `/change-password`'s bare-card `(auth)`-route-group layout (see judgment calls below). Columns: platform (badge), token (masked preview via `maskDeviceToken`), last seen, registered, actions (`<UnregisterDeviceTokenButton>`). `<RegisterDeviceTokenDialog>` trigger in the header. No search field, no pagination — `GET /comms/device-tokens` is unpaginated and realistically near-always empty (see below).

**3. i18n** — new top-level `myDevices` namespace (`pageTitle`/`pageSubtitle`/`listTitle`/`listDescription`/`emptyTitle`/`emptyDescription`/`columns`/`platforms`/`registerDialog`/`unregisterDialog`) + 1 new `shell.userMenu.myDevices` key, in `en.json`/`sw.json`/`fr.json`, real English/Swahili/French translations for every string actually referenced.

### Judgment calls

- **Route group correction, made explicitly before writing any code**: the approved plan's own "reached via `UserMenu`'s dropdown, same precedent as `changePassword` → `/change-password`" language is about the nav-TRIGGER mechanism only, not the route group. `/change-password` deliberately lives under `(auth)` (no sidebar/topbar) because it's a FORCED, pre-full-session screen. My Devices is the opposite — a genuine in-app account-settings screen for an already-fully-authenticated user — so it was built under `app/(erp)/my-devices/page.tsx`, with the normal chrome, matching every other authenticated screen including Parts 1–3's own Comms screens. Verified live below, since this was flagged as the one thing most likely to go wrong.
- **No codegen gap on either request DTO** — a deliberate contrast with most of Parts 1–3: `RegisterDeviceTokenDto` (`token`/`platform`) and `UnregisterDeviceTokenDto` (`token`) are both fully required on both the real DTO and the generated OpenAPI shape (no `@ApiPropertyOptional({default})` field to trip the usual swagger-drops-optional gap), so `device-tokens.api.ts` passes both dtos straight through with no local request-body interface or cast — the same "no gap" shape `optouts.api.ts`'s own `createOptout()` already established for `CreateOptoutDto`.
- **`isEmpty={() => false}` on this page's `<QueryBoundary>`, deliberately opting out of its generic empty state** — every other list page in this app either accepts `<QueryBoundary>`'s shared `queryBoundary.emptyTitle`/`emptyDescription` copy for its empty state, or (in `optouts/page.tsx`'s case) passes a real `isEmpty` and never actually reaches its own custom empty-message branch, since `<QueryBoundary>`'s own `"empty"` case intercepts and renders BEFORE `children` is ever called with an empty array — confirmed by reading `resolveQueryBoundaryState`/`QueryBoundary` directly. Since this page's whole point is to show a real, honestly-worded, device-specific empty message ("No devices registered yet…", not the generic shared copy), `isEmpty` is pinned to `() => false` so the `"empty"` branch never fires, and the actual empty-vs-populated decision is made inside `children` instead, where a real message renders. `<QueryBoundary>`'s loading/error/permission-denied/offline states are completely unaffected by this — only the empty-array case is handled differently.
- **The empty state is not a bug to work around** — confirmed directly: there is no mobile/PWA client anywhere in this codebase that produces real push tokens today (no push-notification-capable frontend exists), so this screen is expected to show a genuinely empty list for every real user right now. The register dialog and both API round trips are fully real and functional regardless — verified live below with an end-to-end register → list → unregister round trip using a fake-but-real token string.
- **Token masking (`maskDeviceToken`)** — the response DTO's `token` field can be up to 300 characters; showing it raw in a table row or a confirm dialog would be visually unwieldy. Tokens longer than 14 characters show `first 6…last 4`; shorter ones (e.g. a hand-typed test value, as used in this part's own verification below) are shown in full, since masking a short string would hide more than it reveals. Purely presentational — the real `DELETE` body still carries the full, unmasked value.

## Slice 15 — closing summary (Parts 1–4 complete)

Phase 6 Slice 15 built the first-ever frontend for `platform/comms` (Module 5 — Communications, backend-complete since Phase 5, zero frontend before this slice), across 4 parts.

- **Part 1** (frontend): Comms foundation + Templates — `features/comms/`'s own scaffolding conventions (`api`/`hooks`/`components` per sub-resource, `["comms", ...]` query-key namespace), the Templates list (full CRUD except no delete-confirm-primitive reuse gap), the new Comms nav dropdown (1 child, explicitly left non-final), and the first `<Textarea>` primitive this app's `components/ui/` ever needed.
- **Part 2** (frontend): Broadcasts — list + detail-with-lifecycle-actions (submit-for-approval → approve → send/cancel), the audience picker (role vs. explicit users), appended as the dropdown's 2nd child. Found and flagged (not fixed, out of scope) a real backend validation gap: `AudienceDefDto.userIds` requires UUID v4 specifically, but every real entity id in this codebase is v7.
- **Part 3** (frontend): Messages (read-only delivery log, server-paginated), Optouts (search-by-guardianId-first, no directory exists), Trigger Bindings (full CRUD except delete) — appended as the dropdown's 3rd/4th/5th and FINAL children, with an explicit "final shape" comment matching Settings'/Wallet's own precedent.
- **Part 4** (frontend, this section): My Devices — the one screen in this slice reached from the user-account dropdown instead of the Comms nav dropdown, since `DeviceTokensController` is genuinely self-service (JWT-only, no permission gate). Register/list/unregister a push-notification device token, with a real, honestly-empty-by-default list (no mobile/PWA client exists anywhere in this codebase yet to populate it for a real user) and the deliberate `(erp)`-not-`(auth)` route-group correction documented above.

Across all four parts: `pnpm turbo run typecheck lint --filter=@klickit/web --force` clean at the end of every dispatch; every backend claim verified with real, live HTTP round trips cross-checked directly against `psql`, never API-response trust alone; the same narrowest-sufficient-throwaway-role/user discipline used consistently in every part that touched the live stack (Part 4 needed no role grant at all — a first for this slice, reflecting the one genuinely permission-free controller among all of Comms), with every throwaway user account explicitly deactivated afterward. No browser-automation tool was available at any point across the whole slice — every part relies on live API round trips and SSR/i18n-bundle checks instead of fabricated interactive-UI verification; Part 4's own SSR check went a step further than prior parts by explicitly separating "chrome renders" (confirmed real, via a direct side-by-side contrast against `/change-password`) from "AuthGuard-gated content renders for an unauthenticated curl request" (does not, universally, by design — not specific to this page). i18n grew from 2317 lines (pre-slice) to 2759 lines (post-Part-4) across all 3 locales, staying in sync and valid JSON throughout. All three dev servers (`apps/api` 3000, `apps/worker` 3001, `apps/web` 3002) are healthy as of this final part, with the standard 7 `node.exe` processes and nothing extra left running. Module 5 (Communications) is now a functionally complete frontend, and its one remaining honest gap (Part 2's UUID v4/v7 mismatch on `EXPLICIT_USER_IDS` broadcasts) is flagged in Part 2's own section above for a future backend-touching pass, not silently dropped.

## Slice 16 (Part 1 — Document Verification Backend) — 2026-08-07

**Verdict: built and verified genuinely end-to-end against the live stack — a real, fully generic new platform module, wired into both real document-producing services it needs to serve, with a real unauthenticated round trip through the actual public endpoint, cross-checked directly against `psql`.** This is the ONE backend-touching part of Slice 16 (Document Security: Watermark + QR Verification); Part 2 (frontend — watermark, QR code rendering, a public verify page) depends on this part's output and is not started.

### What was built

**1. New platform module `platform/document-verification`** (`DocumentVerificationModule`) — migration `0237-create-docv-record.ts` creates `docv_record` (prefix `docv`, confirmed unused among the prior 21 module prefixes before picking it): `id`/`created_at`/`updated_at`/`created_by`/`updated_by` (plain `BaseEntity`, immutable once minted — same append-only precedent `CommMessageEntity`/`FileObjectEntity` establish), `document_type varchar(60)` + `document_id uuid` (a loose, FK-less polymorphic reference, same convention `appr_instance.entity_type`/`.entity_id` and `comm_message.entity_type`/`.entity_id` already establish), `document_ref varchar(120)`, `token varchar(64)` with a real `UNIQUE` constraint (`uq_docv_record_token`), `summary jsonb NOT NULL`. A plain `ix_docv_record_document (document_type, document_id)` index backs `findByDocument()`'s lookup. `module-deps.json`'s new `platform/document-verification` entry: `mayImport: ["shared", "platform/auth"]` — `platform/auth` only for the `@Public()` decorator on the module's one route (same one-directional precedent `platform/branding`'s own entry documents for its public theme endpoint), imported directly by the controller file (not via a NestJS `AuthModule` import — no DI is actually needed).

**2. `DocumentVerificationService`** (`application/document-verification.service.ts`) — `mint(em: EntityManager, params: {documentType, documentId, documentRef, summary})` takes the CALLER's own open transaction `EntityManager` (same in-transaction-composability convention `NumberingService.allocate(em, ...)` established — read as the concrete template before writing this), generates `token = randomBytes(18).toString("base64url")` (~24 chars, `node:crypto`, same primitive `PasswordService`'s reset-token flow already uses) and inserts the `docv_record` row via the caller's manager. `findByDocument(documentType, documentId)` and `verify(token)` are plain, unauthenticated lookups (no `EntityManager`) — the former backs each wired-in document's "get by id" response path, the latter backs the public controller.

**3. `DocumentVerificationController`** — exactly one route, `@Public() @Get(":token")`, returns the real `VerifyDocumentResponseDto` (a real generated Swagger DTO class, not an inline interface) on a hit, or throws the shared `NotFoundException` (real `404`) on a miss — no `{valid:false}` boolean dance, matching this codebase's own "not found" convention elsewhere.

**4. Wired into `ReceiptsService.captureReceipt()`** (`domains/payments`) — `DocumentVerificationService` injected (appended at the END of the existing 15-arg constructor, same discipline every prior extension of this class follows), `mint()` called immediately after the `pay_receipt` row is inserted, `documentType: "PAYMENT_RECEIPT"` (a NEW exported constant, deliberately distinct from the pre-existing `RECEIPT_DOC_TYPE = "PAY_RECEIPT"` numbering-series key — the two serve unrelated concerns), `documentRef: receipt.number`, `summary: {payerName, total, receiptDate, receiptNumber}`. Deliberately NOT called from `recordSubledgerFundedReceipt()` (wallet/credit-balance-funded receipts) or `reverseReceipt()`'s contra receipt — only a real `captureReceipt()` mints. `ReceiptsController.findOne()` resolves the token via `findByDocument()` in parallel with its existing splits/allocations fetch, surfaced as a new `verificationToken: string | null` field on `ReceiptDetailResponseDto` only (not the plain `ReceiptResponseDto` used by `list()`, avoiding an N+1). `PaymentsModule` now imports `DocumentVerificationModule`.

**5. Wired into `FeeStructuresService.publish()`** (`domains/billing`) — `DocumentVerificationService` injected (appended at the end), plus two more appended dependencies, `StdClassRepository`/`StdStreamRepository` (both already exported from `domains/students`' barrel, already reachable — `domains/students` was already in `domains/billing`'s `mayImport`, no new module-level wiring needed) to resolve a genuinely human-readable `documentRef`/`summary` — a bare `classId`/`streamId` uuid would be meaningless to a parent scanning the printed document's QR code, the whole point of this feature. `mint()` called immediately after the structure's status is confirmed `PUBLISHED` and saved, inside the same `runInTransaction` callback: `documentType: "FEE_STRUCTURE"` (new exported constant), `documentRef: "{className}[ (streamName)] v{version}"`, `summary: {className, streamName, boarding, version, publishedAt}`. `FeeStructuresController.findOne()` resolves the token the same way, surfaced as a new `verificationToken: string | null` field on the shared `FeeStructureResponseDto` (defaulted to `null` in `toView()`, only `findOne()` passes the real value — `create()`/`list()`/`addLine()`/`publish()`'s own responses stay `null`, correctly, since a DRAFT/never-published structure genuinely has none). `BillingModule` now imports `DocumentVerificationModule`.

**6. `module-deps.json`** — `domains/payments` and `domains/billing`'s `mayImport` arrays both gained `platform/document-verification`; both entries' long `note` fields were appended (not silently overwritten) explaining the new one-directional dependency, matching every other entry's own documentation style.

**7. Composition root** — `packages/server/src/index.ts` and `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` both gained a `DocumentVerificationModule` export/import (in addition to it being pulled in transitively via `PaymentsModule`/`BillingModule`) — explicit, so the public route is reachable regardless of those two modules' own import order, the same "also a direct root import" shape `FilesModule` already has despite `BrandingModule` also importing it.

### A real bug caught before it ever reached a live run

`FeeStructuresController.list()`'s pre-existing `.map(toView)` call broke under `tsc --noEmit` the moment `toView()` grew a second optional `verificationToken` parameter — `Array.prototype.map` passes `(value, index, array)` positionally, so `list()`'s own `index` (a `number`) was about to flow into `toView`'s `verificationToken: string | null` parameter. Caught by the type checker, not a runtime surprise; fixed by wrapping in an arrow (`.map((row) => toView(row))`).

### Verification

- `pnpm --filter server exec tsc --noEmit` → clean. (Confirmed separately that this codebase's own `tsconfig.json` excludes `**/__tests__/**` — so the two NEW spec files below were NOT covered by this check; their own type errors, found and fixed, only surfaced when Jest/ts-jest actually ran them.)
- New unit spec `platform/document-verification/__tests__/document-verification.service.spec.ts` (mirrors `platform/branding/__tests__/themes.service.spec.ts`'s style — plain mocked repository, no DataSource) — `mint()`'s token shape/uniqueness and exact persisted payload, `findByDocument()`/`verify()` hit and miss.
