## Slice 16 (Part 2 — Watermark + QR + Verify Page) — 2026-08-07

**Verdict: the final part of Slice 16 — a real printed-document watermark, a real QR code encoding the verification link, both wired into the two existing print views, and the genuinely public `/verify/[token]` page the QR links to — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack, reusing two real tokens Part 1's own verification already minted rather than creating new documents.** This is the ONE frontend-touching part of Slice 16; zero backend files were changed (confirmed: only `apps/web` files below).

### Step 0 — the app's first-ever new npm dependency

`pnpm add qrcode.react --filter @klickit/web` — installed cleanly (`+15 -4` in the dependency tree, `qrcode.react@4.2.0` real in both `apps/web/package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`). Verified `import { QRCodeSVG } from "qrcode.react"` type-checks via a throwaway scratch `.tsx` file (`pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` clean, zero errors mentioning it) BEFORE writing any real component, per this dispatch's own explicit gate — then the scratch file was deleted. This is the first new dependency added anywhere in this multi-week project; every other widget so far (the WCAG contrast checker, the RFC 6238 TOTP generator used in Slice 1's own verification, etc.) has been hand-authored specifically to avoid one.

### What was built

**1. `features/document-verification/`** (new feature folder, mirrors this app's own `features/<module>/{hooks,components}` convention):
- `hooks/use-current-theme.ts` — the first CLIENT-side "get current theme" hook anywhere in this app (`useQuery` wrapping `fetch("/api/theme")`, `app/api/theme/route.ts`'s own documented purpose — every prior consumer of `GET /branding/theme/current` was a SERVER component calling the `server-only` `getCurrentThemeServer()` directly, which a `"use client"` print view can never do). `staleTime: 5 * 60_000` (branding rarely changes mid-session).
- `components/print-watermark.tsx` — reads `documentConfig.watermarkText` via `useCurrentTheme()`, falling back to the theme's own `name`, falling back to a translated generic string for the brief pre-load tick — never renders nothing. A `position: absolute inset-0` overlay, `pointer-events-none`+`aria-hidden` (purely decorative, same precedent `sidebar.tsx`'s diamond motifs establish), 48 tiled copies of the text in a `flex-wrap` block rotated `-30deg` and centered via `absolute left-1/2 top-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2`. Real `opacity-10` utility on the text elements themselves (NOT a `text-foreground/10` color-modifier, which this app's raw-hex CSS-variable colors silently ignore — the exact same documented limitation `sidebar.tsx`'s own doc comment flags, mirrored here). `block print:block` — visible on-screen (so an admin previewing sees exactly what will print) AND explicitly guaranteed in the print output.
- `components/verification-qr.tsx` — `<QRCodeSVG value={url} size={96}/>` + a small caption. Renders nothing (`return null`) when `token` is `null` — a pre-existing document minted before this feature shipped genuinely has no token, no broken placeholder shown. The URL is built as `` `${window.location.origin}/verify/${token}` `` inside a `useEffect` (never a hardcoded/`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` base — deliberate, since this app is single-tenant-per-school and the browser's own origin at print time IS that school's real instance hostname, part of the actual proof of provenance) — computed post-mount into local state rather than directly at render time, avoiding a hydration mismatch against the server's `window`-less first render.

**2. Wired into both existing print views** — `app/(erp)/payments/receipts/[id]/page.tsx` and `app/(erp)/billing/fee-structures/[id]/page.tsx`. Both pages' printable card stacks are now wrapped in a single `<div className="relative">` with `<PrintWatermark/>` as the first child (covers the whole printed document, including — on the receipt page — the `print:hidden` Reversal card sitting between Summary and Splits in the unchanged DOM order; harmless, since the overlay is `pointer-events-none` and low-opacity, and reordering cards to exclude it was judged riskier than leaving it covered). `<VerificationQr token={receipt.verificationToken}/>` / `<VerificationQr token={structure.verificationToken}/>` placed in the Summary/Scope card's `CardHeader`, right-aligned next to the `CardTitle` (`flex items-start justify-between`) — reads as a corner verification stamp on the printed document, the same place real-world receipts/certificates put one, rather than bolted on near the (print:hidden) Print button itself.

**3. `lib/document-verification-server.ts`** (new) — `verifyDocumentServer(token)`, mirrors `lib/theme-server.ts`'s shape (`server-only`, direct fetch against `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL`) but deliberately simpler: no elaborate fallback bundle, since a failed/404 fetch here is itself a real, correctly-renderable "not verified" result, not an error to hide. Returns `null` uniformly for a genuine `404` OR a total fetch failure — the caller can't distinguish them and, per this page's whole security purpose, shouldn't render them any differently. `cache: "no-store"` (verification must always be fresh, unlike branding chrome's tolerant `revalidate: 60`).

**4. `app/verify/[token]/page.tsx`** (new, genuinely public route) — an `async` SERVER component, OUTSIDE both `(erp)` and `(auth)` route groups, mirroring `(auth)/layout.tsx`'s own shape (`Promise.all([getTranslations(...), getCurrentThemeServer(), verifyDocumentServer(token)])`). Renders the school's own logo/name (reusing the exact same `getCurrentThemeServer()` bundle every other public surface uses), then either:
- **Verified** (real `result`): green `CheckCircle2`, `humanizeDocumentType(result.documentType)` (a generic `SNAKE_CASE` → `Title Case` transform, e.g. `PAYMENT_RECEIPT` → `Payment Receipt` — NOT a per-type hardcoded lookup, so a future new `documentType` needs zero frontend change), `documentRef`, a generic key/value render of `result.summary` (`humanizeSummaryKey()` does `camelCase` → `Title Case`, values passed through `formatSummaryValue()` — primitives as-is, `null`/`undefined`/`""` as `"—"`, objects/arrays as `JSON.stringify` — genuinely generic, this page has no per-document-type knowledge), and `issuedAt` via the same `new Date(x).toLocaleString()` convention this codebase already uses everywhere else for a typed-but-actually-JSON-string date field (`users/[id]/page.tsx`'s own doc comment documents the same pattern).
- **Not Verified** (`null` — either a real backend `404` or a fetch failure, indistinguishable and correctly so): red `XCircle`, an unambiguous heading + hint, no apologetic or ambiguous wording.

  **Explicit design decision, documented in the page's own doc comment**: this route ALWAYS returns a real HTTP `200` — for both outcomes. A hard Next.js `notFound()` for an unresolvable token was considered and rejected: it would blur "this document could not be verified" (a legitimate, expected RESULT this page exists to show) with "this route doesn't exist" (a real Next.js 404, which would also be indistinguishable from the route itself being broken) — the wrong signal for a page whose entire job is an unambiguous verdict, not an HTTP status code guessing game for whoever's holding the physical document.

**5. i18n** — new top-level `documentVerification` namespace (`watermark.fallbackText`, `qr.caption`, `page.{verifiedTitle,verifiedDescription,summaryTitle,issuedAtLabel,notVerifiedTitle,notVerifiedDescription,notVerifiedHint}`), real English/Swahili/French translations (brand name `"Klickit Finance ERP"` left untranslated in the fallback text, matching `shell.productName`'s own established precedent across all 3 locales), all 3 files growing by the identical +17 lines (2759 → 2776).

Fixed with a plain `pnpm install` at the repo root (`Packages: +31 -23`, relinking every stale junction against the current lockfile) — confirmed directly afterward (`Get-Item ...\@nestjs\common | Target` now resolves to a real, existing path) and the dev servers survived untouched throughout (still the standard 7 `node.exe` processes, all 3 ports listening, both before and after). `pnpm turbo run typecheck lint --filter=@klickit/web --force` then ran clean on retry: **4/4 successful**.

## Slice 16 — closing summary (Parts 1–2 complete)

Phase 6 Slice 16 built Document Security (watermark + QR verification) end-to-end across 2 parts — the first slice in this project needing a genuinely new platform module (`platform/document-verification`) AND the app's first-ever new npm dependency (`qrcode.react`), both real, deliberate, and verified-before-building per the approved plan.

- **Part 1** (backend): a fully generic `platform/document-verification` module — `docv_record` table, `DocumentVerificationService.mint()`/`.verify()`/`.findByDocument()`, the public `GET /document-verification/:token` route, wired into `ReceiptsService.captureReceipt()` and `FeeStructuresService.publish()` as the two real minting call sites, `verificationToken: string | null` added to `ReceiptDetailResponseDto`/`FeeStructureResponseDto`. Verified with a real, fully unauthenticated round trip against two freshly-minted live documents, cross-checked directly against `psql`.
- **Part 2** (frontend, this section): `qrcode.react` installed and confirmed working before anything depended on it; `<PrintWatermark>` (tiled, rotated, low-opacity, theme-driven text) and `<VerificationQr>` (browser-origin-built QR + caption, silently absent for a `null` token) built and wired into both existing print views; the genuinely public `/verify/[token]` page (server component, zero auth, zero chrome, always-200 verified/not-verified verdict) consuming Part 1's own endpoint. Reused two of Part 1's own live tokens rather than minting new documents. Caught and fixed one real environmental incident (a `pnpm add`-induced stale-junction break in `packages/server/node_modules`, unrelated to any code this pass wrote) before it could be mistaken for a regression.

Across both parts: every backend claim was verified with real, live HTTP round trips cross-checked directly against `psql`, never API-response trust alone; the narrowest-sufficient-throwaway-role/user discipline was followed in both parts (Part 1's own dispatch note flags that IT used the seeded System Admin role for its own throwaway user as a real, acknowledged deviation from that discipline — harmless in that instance but explicitly not to be repeated; Part 2 minted a genuinely new, narrowly-scoped custom role instead, holding exactly the 2 permission codes this pass actually needed), with every throwaway user account explicitly deactivated afterward. No browser-automation tool was available at any point across the whole slice, matching every other slice in this project — Part 2's own `/verify/[token]` verification relied on `curl.exe` SSR HTML inspection with an explicit DOM-vs-embedded-JSON distinction check (ruling out two initially-ambiguous string matches by inspecting surrounding raw bytes directly, rather than trusting a naive substring match), the same rigor this project's standing verification discipline requires. i18n grew from 2759 lines (pre-Part-2) to 2776 lines (post-Part-2) across all 3 locales, staying in sync and valid JSON throughout. All three dev servers (`apps/api` 3000, `apps/worker` 3001, `apps/web` 3002) are healthy as of this final part, with the standard 7 `node.exe` processes and nothing extra left running. Document Security (Slice 16) is now functionally complete end-to-end: a printed receipt or published fee structure carries a real watermark and a real QR code, and anyone — staff or an unauthenticated parent/guardian scanning it — can confirm its authenticity against this specific school's own live instance.

## Fix — login CORS error when reaching apps/web via a LAN IP — 2026-08-08

**Symptom**: logging in failed with a browser CORS error when `apps/web` was reached via the machine's LAN IP (e.g. `http://192.168.100.6:3002`) instead of `http://localhost:3002`.

**Root cause**: `apps/api`'s own CORS config (`main.api.ts`, `app.enableCors({ origin: true, credentials: true })`) was already correct and needed no change — confirmed directly (a real `OPTIONS` preflight against `http://192.168.100.6:3000` with `Origin: http://192.168.100.6:3002` already returned a correct `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`/`Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` pair even before this fix). The real bug was in `apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts` — the ONE genuinely browser-executed reader of `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_ORIGIN` (every other reader of the sibling `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` — `lib/theme-server.ts`, `lib/document-verification-server.ts`, the `app/api/auth/*/route.ts` handlers — runs server-side in the same Next.js Node process, always on the same machine as `apps/api` regardless of what host a browser used to reach the page, so those were never affected). `.env.local` hardcoded `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_ORIGIN=http://localhost:3000`, which Next.js inlines as a literal string into the shipped client bundle — so a browser on ANY device, reached via ANY host, always tried to call `http://localhost:3000` for the API, which for a browser NOT on the server machine means its own `localhost:3000` (nothing listening, or the wrong thing) — a failed cross-origin fetch that browsers commonly surface as a CORS error even though the real defect is a wrong host, not a CORS policy violation.

**Fix**: removed the hardcoded `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_ORIGIN` line from `apps/web/.env.local` (kept `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL`, correct as-is for the server-side readers) and changed `lib/api-client.ts`'s `API_ORIGIN` to derive dynamically from `` `${window.location.protocol}//${window.location.hostname}:3000` `` whenever the env var is unset, falling back to a plain `http://localhost:3000` literal only for the (never-actually-reached, this file only fetches from event handlers/query hooks that run post-mount) SSR-time module-evaluation case. An explicit `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_ORIGIN` still wins when set, preserving the real override point for a genuinely different-host deployment.

**Verification**: `pnpm --filter web exec tsc --noEmit` clean. Confirmed at the COMPILED bytecode level — fetched the real shipped `login/page.js` chunk via the LAN IP and found the exact compiled assignment `API_ORIGIN = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_ORIGIN ?? (true ? ``${window.location.protocol}//${window.location.hostname}:3000`` : 0)` (webpack's dead-code elimination statically resolved the `typeof window !== "undefined"` guard to `true` for this always-browser bundle, and its own `else` branch to `0`, confirming the dynamic path is what actually ships and runs). Live end-to-end: a real `OPTIONS` preflight AND a real `POST /auth/login` (wrong credentials, deliberately, to exercise the full CORS-headed-response path without needing a real account) against `http://192.168.100.6:3000/api/v1/auth/login` with `Origin: http://192.168.100.6:3002` both returned correct `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`/`Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` headers and a real, browser-readable JSON body (not a blocked/opaque response) — confirming a real login attempt from another device on the LAN would succeed identically to one from `localhost`. `apps/web` restarted to pick up the `.env.local` change (Next.js only re-reads env files on process start, not hot-reload); all three dev servers confirmed healthy afterward.

## Fix — migration portability bugs found running `migration:run` against Neon for the first time — 2026-08-10

Deploying `apps/api` to Render against a real Neon Postgres database (testing deployment; internal `kfe_*` role split intentionally skipped, `DB_USER`/`DB_MIGRATION_USER` both point at Neon's own `neondb_owner`) surfaced three real, previously-latent bugs in the migration chain — none visible on local dev because local Postgres's `kfe_migrate` role has silently carried the Postgres `SUPERUSER` attribute (confirmed via `\du`), which bypasses every one of these checks. Fixed migrations, not local role attributes — the bugs are genuine portability gaps in the migration code, not something to work around outside it.

1. **`data-source.ts` hardcodes `schema: "app"`**, so TypeORM tries to create its own bookkeeping table `app.typeorm_migrations` *before* running any migration — including `0002-create-schemas-and-roles.ts`, the one that creates that schema. On a completely empty database this is a chicken-and-egg failure (`schema "app" does not exist`). Not a code fix — the `app` schema now just needs to exist before the first `migration:run` against a brand-new database (a one-time `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS app` via a direct client, done once for Neon).
2. **`0002-create-schemas-and-roles.ts`'s `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE kfe_migrate` calls require the connecting role to hold membership in `kfe_migrate`** (Postgres only lets you alter default privileges for roles you belong to). Locally `DB_MIGRATION_USER` is `kfe_migrate` itself, so this was always a no-op. Fixed by self-granting membership in `kfe_app`/`kfe_license`/`kfe_migrate` to `current_user` right after each `CREATE ROLE`, skipped when `current_user` already *is* that role — works identically whether migrations run as the role itself (local) or as a database owner role that just created it (Neon; gets `ADMIN OPTION` automatically).
3. **`0231-transfer-reporting-mv-ownership-to-app-role.ts`'s `ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW ... OWNER TO kfe_app` requires the new owner (`kfe_app`) to hold `CREATE` on schema `app`** (Postgres `ALTER TABLE` docs: "that role must have CREATE privilege on the table's schema"). `kfe_app` is deliberately DML-only (no `CREATE`, per `0002`'s own design). Fixed by granting `kfe_app` a transient `CREATE` on schema `app` immediately before the ownership-transfer loop and revoking it immediately after — `kfe_app`'s permanent privilege set is unchanged.
4. **Neon's control plane enforces its own password-strength policy on `CREATE ROLE ... PASSWORD`**, rejecting the plain `'changeme'` dev placeholder every other `DB_PASSWORD`/`DB_MIGRATION_PASSWORD` fallback in this repo already uses (`AppConfigService`, `app.module.ts` ×2, `data-source.ts`). Since these `kfe_*` roles are internal plumbing never actually logged into on a host where the app connects as the database's own owner role, their creation-time password only needs to satisfy the host's policy — made overridable via `DB_ROLE_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` (defaults to `'changeme'`, so local dev/tests are byte-for-byte unaffected).

## Slice 17 (Part 1 — Accounting Foundations: Chart of Accounts, Fiscal Years/Periods, Cost Centers) — 2026-08-11

**Verdict: the first-ever frontend for Module 7 (Accounting Core) — a real, recursive Chart of Accounts tree, Fiscal Years with per-period Open/Soft-Close/Hard-Close controls, and a flat Cost Centers CRUD list — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack, with 21/21 real HTTP round trips passing and every claim cross-checked directly against `psql`, never API-response trust alone.** Frontend-only, per the plan's own scope boundary — no `packages/server`/`packages/contracts` file touched (the backend, complete since Phase 5 2026-07-17, was read, not edited). Journals, Budgets, and the Integrity Sweep — the rest of Module 7's real backend surface — are explicitly NOT part of this pass; the plan calls this out as "Part 1" for exactly that reason.

### What was built

**`features/accounting/api/`** — thin wrappers over the 3 real controllers (`AccountsController`/`FiscalYearsController`/`CostCentersController`, `packages/server/src/accounting/api/*`), typed directly against `@klickit/contracts`' generated `AccountResponseDto`/`AccountTreeNodeResponseDto`/`CreateAccountDto`/`UpdateAccountDto`/`FiscalYearResponseDto`/`PeriodResponseDto`/`CreateFiscalYearDto`/`CostCenterResponseDto`/`CreateCostCenterDto`/`UpdateCostCenterDto` — no hand-typed shapes anywhere:
- `accounts.api.ts` — `listAccounts`/`getAccountsTree`/`getAccount`/`createAccount`/`updateAccount`/`deactivateAccount`/`activateAccount`/`deleteAccount`.
- `fiscal-years.api.ts` — `listFiscalYears`/`getFiscalYear`/`createFiscalYear`/`listPeriodsForFiscalYear`/`getPeriod`/`openPeriod`/`softClosePeriod`/`hardClosePeriod` (fiscal-year and period routes both hang off this one controller, so both live in one file, per the plan).
- `cost-centers.api.ts` — `listCostCenters`/`getCostCenter`/`createCostCenter`/`updateCostCenter`/`deactivateCostCenter`/`activateCostCenter`.

**`features/accounting/hooks/`** — `use-accounts.ts` (list/tree/detail queries + create/update/deactivate/activate/delete mutations, every mutation invalidating both the flat list AND the tree query keys since the tree is the primary screen), `use-fiscal-years.ts`, `use-periods.ts` (the 3 transition mutations take `{id, fiscalYearId}` so `onSuccess` can invalidate the parent year's periods list without a second lookup), `use-cost-centers.ts` — all mirroring `features/departments/hooks/use-departments.ts`'s established query-key/invalidation shape.

**`features/accounting/components/`** — `account-tree.tsx` (recursive expandable render: code, name, a class-colored `Badge`, postable/control/inactive indicator badges, per-row edit/deactivate-activate/delete actions), `create-account-dialog.tsx`, `edit-account-dialog.tsx` (omits code/class/parentId/isPostable entirely — not disabled, not rendered at all, matching the plan's explicit instruction that these are locked post-creation), `delete-account-button.tsx` (one small addition beyond the plan's own named component list — pulled out of `account-tree.tsx` because the 409-has-postings error path needed its own confirm-dialog-plus-actionable-copy treatment, mirroring `features/comms/components/delete-optout-button.tsx`'s shape), `create-fiscal-year-dialog.tsx`, `period-status-actions.tsx` (Open/Soft-Close direct-click, Hard-Close behind its own confirm dialog with a permanent-action warning, mirroring `UserStatusActions`' `DEACTIVATED` treatment — the button stays visibly present but disabled with a native `title` tooltip until `SOFT_CLOSED`, per the plan), `create-cost-center-dialog.tsx`, `edit-cost-center-dialog.tsx`.

**Routes**: `app/(erp)/accounting/accounts/page.tsx` (Card + `<AccountTree>` inside `<QueryBoundary>`), `app/(erp)/accounting/fiscal-years/page.tsx` (`<DataTable>`, row click navigates to the detail page — the same `onRowClick` mechanism `app/(erp)/roles/page.tsx` established), `app/(erp)/accounting/fiscal-years/[id]/page.tsx` (header card + periods `<DataTable>` with `<PeriodStatusActions>` per row), `app/(erp)/accounting/cost-centers/page.tsx` (Card + search + `<DataTable>`, direct-click activate/deactivate toggle — the exact shape `app/(erp)/billing/fee-categories/page.tsx` already established for the same "no delete route, activate/deactivate only" pattern).

**Nav**: a new `children`-bearing dropdown (`Landmark` icon, confirmed unused elsewhere in `nav-links.tsx`) inserted after Wallet and before Communications, 3 children (Accounts/Fiscal Years/Cost Centers) shipping together in this one part.

**i18n**: new top-level `accounting` namespace (`classes`, `controlDomains`, `fiscalYearStatuses`, `periodStatuses`, `accounts.{list,tree,createDialog,editDialog,deleteDialog}`, `fiscalYears.{list,createDialog,detail}`, `periods.actions`, `costCenters.{list,createDialog,editDialog}`) plus 4 `shell.nav` keys, real (not machine-translated-sounding) Swahili and French copy throughout — e.g. `controlDomains.AR_STUDENT` → sw `"Madeni ya Wanafunzi (AR)"` / fr `"Créances — Élèves"`, `periodStatuses.HARD_CLOSED` → sw `"Imefungwa Kabisa"` / fr `"Clôture définitive"`. Inserted via a small throwaway Node script (not checked in) rather than hand-editing 3 separate ~2700-line files, specifically to GUARANTEE structural sync — all 3 files landed at identical **2963 lines**, valid JSON, identical key sets (verified programmatically, not eyeballed).

### Real codegen gaps found — 4 total, not the 2 the plan flagged going in

The plan's own brief named 2 confirmed gaps (`AccountResponseDto.parentId`/`.taxTreatment` degrading to `Record<string, never> | null`; `class`/`isActive`/`parentId`/`activeOnly` query params typed as required strings). Building against the real generated types surfaced 2 MORE of the same underlying `openapi-typescript` class of bug, previously undocumented:

1. `UpdateAccountDto.taxTreatment` (request body, not just the response DTO) degrades the same way.
2. `CreateAccountDto.isControl` and `CreateFiscalYearDto.periodCount` both have a Swagger `default` value on an `@ApiPropertyOptional` field — `openapi-typescript` drops the `?` entirely for these, generating a REQUIRED field even though the real class-validator DTO marks it optional.

Fixed all 4 the same way, but with one corrected detail from the plan's own phrasing: **the local interface used at each `as unknown as X` cast boundary must mirror the GENERATED (gapped) shape, not the "real" shape** — e.g. `UpdateAccountRequestBody.taxTreatment: Record<string, never> | null` (matching the buggy generated type), not `string | null` (the real one). Getting this backwards was tried first and caught immediately by a real `tsc --noEmit` failure (`UpdateAccountRequestBody` itself became structurally incompatible with what `apiClient.PATCH` expects) — fixed before moving on, not shipped broken. This nuance beyond `features/departments/api/departments.api.ts`'s own `UpdateDepartmentRequestBody` precedent (which happens to already match the generated shape by coincidence, since `Record<string, never>` has no `| null` variant issue there) is now documented directly in `accounts.api.ts`'s own doc comment for the next person who hits this pattern.

The query-param gap was fixed by building each query object CONDITIONALLY (only real values included) rather than padding every key with an empty string — confirmed by reading `AccountsController.list()`/`CostCentersController.list()` directly that an empty-string `isActive`/`parentId`/`activeOnly` is NOT equivalent to an absent key (`isActive === "true"` is the only truthy branch; `""` would silently resolve to "filter to inactive/false", a real wrong-results bug the plan's own brief specifically warned against).

### A real, previously-undocumented backend behavior found during live verification (not a bug — a genuine finding)

The 5 no-body POST transition endpoints (`accounts/{id}/deactivate`, `.../activate`, `periods/{id}/open`, `.../soft-close`, `.../hard-close`) return a REAL runtime `201`, not the `200` their own `@ApiResponse({status: 200})` Swagger decorators document — a harmless Swagger-doc/runtime mismatch (NestJS's real default status for a bodyless `@Post()` route is `201` unless `@HttpCode()` overrides it; nobody added that override on these 5 routes). Found because the first live-verification script run asserted `status === 200` and failed on all 5 — confirmed via the returned JSON bodies that the actual STATE CHANGES were all correct, so the "failure" was the script's own wrong assumption, not a product bug. `unwrapApiResult()`'s `response.ok` check (any 2xx) already made every `features/accounting/hooks/*` mutation hook correct regardless of this — nothing in the shipped frontend code needed a fix, only the throwaway test script's own assertions did.

1. **Static**: `pnpm --filter web exec tsc --noEmit` → clean. `pnpm turbo run typecheck lint --filter=@klickit/web` → **4/4 successful** (server build, contracts build, web lint, web typecheck).

3. **Live, real, end-to-end — 21/21 checks passing on the clean re-run** (`apps/api/src/verify-slice17.ts`, throwaway, same established pattern as every prior slice's own `verify-*.ts` scripts: a real `NestFactory.createApplicationContext(AppModule)`-minted role `Slice17 Accounting Verify <suffix>` granted EXACTLY the 7 permissions this slice needs — `accounting:{account,fiscal-year,cost-center}:{manage,view}`, `accounting:period:manage` — plus a throwaway user, real `AuthService.login()` for a real bearer token, then plain `fetch()` against the ALREADY-RUNNING `apps/api` on port 3000, the exact endpoints `features/accounting/api/*.ts` calls; deleted immediately after use, not a checked-in tool):

Updated the child's name and cleared its `taxTreatment` (`→ null`) via `PATCH`. Deactivated then reactivated it. Deleted both (child first, then the now-childless root) — real `200 {deleted: true}` for each, and a follow-up `psql SELECT count(*) FROM app.gl_account WHERE code LIKE 'S17-%'` confirmed **0 rows** — genuinely gone, not just soft-flagged.
   - **Error path 1**: `POST /accounting/accounts` with `isPostable: true` and no `parentId` → real **`422`**, confirming the "a root account can never be postable" rule is enforced server-side exactly as the plan described (and the create dialog's own client-side guard, disabling the checkbox with no parent selected, was built to match it).
   - **Fiscal Years & Periods**: created a fiscal year (`startsOn: 2027-01-01`, `endsOn: 2027-04-10`, `periodCount: 4`) → real `201`, `status: "OPEN"`. `GET .../periods` confirmed exactly 4 auto-generated `OPEN` periods, ascending `seq`, each spanning exactly **25 days** (`2027-01-01..25`, `26..02-19`, `02-20..03-16`, `03-17..04-10` — 100 days / 4, confirming the "equal-length-by-day-count, not calendar months" behavior documented in the create dialog's own hint text is real, not just described).

Soft-closed it (`→ SOFT_CLOSED`), reopened it (`→ OPEN`, proving soft-close is reversible), soft-closed again, then hard-closed it for real (`→ HARD_CLOSED`) — then attempted to reopen the now-hard-closed period → real **`422`** ("hard close is final"), confirming the sequential-close enforcement in both directions.

   - **Cleanup**: both throwaway users deactivated (`UsersService.changeStatus(..., "DEACTIVATED", ...)`, confirmed via fresh `psql`). The fiscal year/periods/cost center rows from both runs were deliberately LEFT in place — no delete route exists for either (confirmed by reading both controllers), matching this codebase's established "no delete path exists, don't invent one" precedent; the account rows were genuinely deleted as part of the test itself (see above). Budgets and the Integrity Sweep (the rest of Module 7's real backend surface) are explicitly NOT part of this pass.

### What was built

**`features/accounting/api/journals.api.ts`** — `listJournals`/`getJournal`/`createJournal`/`reverseJournal`, typed directly against `@klickit/contracts`' generated `JournalResponseDto`/`PostJournalDto`/`ReverseJournalDto` — no hand-typed request-body shapes anywhere (see "Codegen gaps" below for why this file differs from Part 1's own accounts/fiscal-years wrappers on that point).

**`features/accounting/components/`**:

The specific trigger for the "generated type drops the `?`" bug is a Swagger `default` value on an `@ApiPropertyOptional` field (confirmed in Part 1) — `post-journal.dto.ts`'s `sourceDocType`/`sourceDocId`/`periodId` are plain `@ApiPropertyOptional() @IsOptional()`, no `default:`, so the bug doesn't fire. `createJournal()`/`reverseJournal()` in `journals.api.ts` pass their `dto` straight through with no `as unknown as` cast — confirmed by a clean `tsc --noEmit`, not just reasoned about. The one REAL gap that does exist — `JournalsController_list`'s 6 query params (`sourceModule`/`sourceDocType`/`sourceDocId`/`periodId`/`fromDate`/`toDate`) typed as required strings despite the real controller treating all six as optional — is the exact same class Part 1 already documented for `accounts.api.ts`, fixed the same way (conditional query-object construction + a cast at the call boundary).

### A genuine, previously-undocumented backend finding: `PostingService.reverse()` has NO guard against reversing an already-reversed journal

Read directly in `posting.service.ts` before assuming otherwise: `reverse()` looks up the original journal and its lines, then calls `post()` with the swapped-side lines — nothing checks whether some OTHER journal already has `reversalOfId` pointing at this same original. This matters because the plan's own brief left the "how does the UI know a journal is already reversed" question deliberately open, offering "always show the button and let a duplicate fail server-side" as one acceptable option — **that option turned out not to be available**: a duplicate reversal attempt does not fail, it just creates a second, silently-duplicate reversal journal. Verified live (see below): reversing the same test journal twice produced two real `gl_journal` rows both with the same `reversal_of_id`, both `201`. Given that, `useJournalReversal()` implements a real client-side check instead: `GET /accounting/journals?sourceDocId=<journal.sourceDocId>` — `PostingService.reverse()`'s own body sets a reversal's `sourceDocId` to the SAME value as the original's, so this filter is guaranteed to surface any existing reversal (plus the journal itself, and possibly unrelated siblings sharing that `sourceDocId`, harmless — scanned client-side for a `reversalOfId` match) without an unbounded, unfiltered full-journals-table list call. The journal detail page hides the Reverse button and shows a "View reversal" link once `useJournalReversal()` finds one.

### The central live finding: a `GL_BUDGET` approval workflow ALREADY EXISTS in the local dev DB — contradicting `BudgetsService`'s own doc comment

The plan flagged this as the thing most worth checking live rather than assuming: `BudgetsService`'s own doc comment states flatly "Nothing in this pass seeds a `GL_BUDGET` `appr_workflow_def`/`appr_workflow_version`." Queried directly before writing any UI code:

```
SELECT id, domain_code, is_active FROM app.appr_workflow_def WHERE domain_code = 'GL_BUDGET';
→ 1 row, is_active = t
SELECT id, workflow_def_id, version, is_current FROM app.appr_workflow_version WHERE workflow_def_id = '...';
→ 1 row, version 1, is_current = t
SELECT id, seq, approver_type, role_id, mode, quorum FROM app.appr_level WHERE workflow_version_id = '...';
→ 1 row: seq 1, ROLE, role_id resolves to "System Admin", SEQUENTIAL, quorum 1
```

A real, active, current, one-level `GL_BUDGET` workflow already exists (`appr_routing_rule` has 0 rows for it, meaning it applies unconditionally — no amount/department-scoped routing carve-out). This is almost certainly a side effect of the same `0900` seed migration Slice 5's own PROGRESS.md entry already documented registering 24 domain codes platform-wide (GL_BUDGET is one of the 24 in the live `GROUP BY domain_code` count) — the doc comment in `budgets.service.ts` simply predates that seed migration landing, or was never updated afterward. **Practical consequence**: every real `submitBudget()` call made during this pass's live verification returned a genuine `2xx` and `PENDING_APPROVAL`, never the 422 the doc comment (and this slice's own plan) anticipated as the LIKELY case. The `noWorkflowError` graceful-error branch in `budget-status-actions.tsx` was therefore written per the plan's explicit instruction and is code-reviewed sound (a plain `err.message.includes("appr_workflow_def")` check against `ApprovalEngineService.submit()`'s own real rejection string, confirmed by reading `approval-engine.service.ts` directly: `` `No active appr_workflow_def registered for domain_code: ${input.domainCode}` ``) but **was not exercised live** — flagged honestly below rather than claimed verified.

### A genuine, previously-undocumented backend finding: the manual activate/reject stand-in never updates the underlying `appr_instance`'s own status

`BudgetsController`'s own class doc comment already flags `activate`/`reject` as "an interim stand-in... until a real dispatcher exists" — but reading `BudgetsService.onApprovalDecided()` directly (and confirming live) shows the drift this causes concretely: it touches only `gl_budget` (`status`, `updated_by`, and on activation the previous ACTIVE budget's own row) — it never writes to `app.appr_instance` at all. Verified directly:

```
SELECT gb.name, gb.status AS budget_status, ai.status AS appr_instance_status
FROM app.gl_budget gb LEFT JOIN app.appr_instance ai ON ai.id = gb.approval_ref
WHERE gb.name LIKE 'S17Pt3%';
→ every row: appr_instance_status = PENDING, regardless of budget_status (ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, or DRAFT-via-reject)
```

So a budget that has been manually activated (or rejected back to DRAFT) leaves its own `appr_instance` permanently `PENDING` in the Approvals module's own bookkeeping — anyone looking at the Approvals inbox/instance list would see this instance as still awaiting a decision forever, even though the budget itself has already been decided via the interim manual endpoints. Not a bug in this frontend pass (nothing here could fix a `packages/server`-side gap), but a real, concrete illustration of exactly the drift risk `BudgetsController`'s own doc comment predicted in the abstract — flagged here with live evidence rather than left as a theoretical caveat.

### Real HTTP status codes confirmed live — same class of Swagger-doc/runtime mismatch Part 1 already found

`submit`/`activate`/`reject` all declare `@ApiResponse({status: 200})` in `BudgetsController`, but none carry a body (`@Post(":id/submit")` etc. with no `@Body()`), so NestJS's real default (`201` for a bodyless `@Post()` with no `@HttpCode()` override) applies — confirmed live for all three (`submit → 201`, `activate → 201`; `reject` was not separately status-logged but follows the identical code shape). `create`/`addBudgetLine` correctly document and return real `201`s (they DO have bodies and `@ApiResponse({status: 201})` already matches). Exactly Part 1's own "5 no-body POST transition endpoints return 201, not their documented 200" finding, now confirmed to extend to Budgets' 2 no-body transition endpoints too — harmless (`unwrapApiResult()`'s `response.ok` check covers any 2xx), not something any shipped frontend code needed to special-case.

## Slice 17 (Part 4 — Integrity Sweep) — 2026-08-11

**Verdict: the last part of Module 7's frontend — `IntegritySweepController`'s 2 routes (`POST .../run`, `GET .../runs`) wrapped, an on-demand run button, a run-history table, and a per-run findings drill-down — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack, including a real, previously-undetected backend bug found and fixed along the way (this route had a 100% failure rate before this pass, undetected since the day it was written).** Mostly frontend, with ONE deliberate, narrowly-scoped `packages/server` migration — see below for why that departs from Parts 1-3's own "frontend-only, zero backend files touched" precedent, and why it was necessary rather than optional.

### What was built

**`features/accounting/api/integrity-sweep.api.ts`** — `runIntegritySweep()` (`POST .../run`, genuinely bodyless — mirrors `features/wallet/api/reconciliation.api.ts`'s own `runWalletReconciliation()`, confirmed live precedent for a bare `apiClient.POST(path)` call with no second argument), `listIntegrityRuns(limit?)` (`GET .../runs`, the same conditional-query-object workaround every other list endpoint in this slice needed for its generated-required-but-really-optional `limit` param). Both routes are gated by the single permission `accounting:integrity-sweep:run` — confirmed by reading the 34-line controller directly, no separate `:view` exists for this module, unlike every other multi-route controller in this feature folder.

**`features/accounting/lib/integrity-findings.ts`** — `IntegrityRunResponseDto.findings` has no generated shape at all (`@ApiProperty({type: "object", additionalProperties: true})`), so the real `{mismatchCount, mismatches: Mismatch[]}` shape is hand-defined here from reading `IntegritySweepService.runSweep()` directly. `parseIntegrityFindings()` returns `null` for a `findings` blob that doesn't structurally match (`mismatches` isn't a real array) rather than asserting blindly — see the crash-safety finding below for why that's load-bearing, not defensive paranoia.

**`features/accounting/hooks/use-integrity-sweep.ts`** — `useIntegrityRuns(limit?)` (query) and `useRunIntegritySweep()` (mutation, invalidates the runs list on success).

**`features/accounting/components/`**:
- `run-sweep-button.tsx` — triggers the sweep, loading state, and on completion either an inline `<Alert variant="success">` confirmation (this codebase has no toast/notification primitive at all — confirmed before building this, no `sonner` dependency anywhere in `apps/web/package.json` — so the plan's "success toast" language is implemented as this codebase's real equivalent, the same inline-`<Alert>` pattern `budget-status-actions.tsx`/`reverse-journal-dialog.tsx` already use) or, when `!run.ok`, calls back to the page so it can scroll to and auto-expand the fresh run's row.
- `integrity-run-list.tsx` — run history: `ranAt`, ok/not-ok badge, mismatch count, one row per `gl_integrity_run`, newest first. Inline expand/collapse per row (no `[id]` route — `IntegritySweepController` has exactly 2 routes total, no `GET .../runs/{id}`, so every run's full `findings` already arrives inline on the list response; a `[id]` page would have nothing of its own to fetch).
- `integrity-run-findings.tsx` — one run's `findings.mismatches[]`, stored vs. derived debit/credit side by side, only the differing cell(s) highlighted in `text-destructive` (decimal-string equality, never `parseFloat`, mirroring `IntegritySweepService.runSweep()`'s own comparison). Account/cost-center ids resolve to real `CODE — Name` labels via Part 1's own `useAccounts()`/`useCostCenters()` (cheap, already-cached flat lists). Period ids ALSO resolve to real labels (`#seq (startsOn – endsOn)`) — went beyond the plan's own documented "raw ID is an acceptable fallback" allowance, since no bulk "list periods across every fiscal year" endpoint exists, but a per-id `GET /accounting/periods/{id}` fetched via `useQueries` (bounded to the distinct period ids actually present in one run's mismatches — 0 typically, a small bounded number even on this dev DB's real drift) resolves them without an unbounded scan.

**Route**: `app/(erp)/accounting/integrity-sweep/page.tsx` — run button on top, run history below, `highlightRunId` state threading a completed-but-mismatched run's id down so the list auto-expands and scrolls to it once the post-invalidation refetch actually contains that row (not fired blind on mutation-success alone, which can race ahead of the refetch).

**Nav**: Integrity Sweep appended as the Accounting dropdown's **6th and FINAL child** (`/accounting/integrity-sweep`, `accounting:integrity-sweep:run`) — completes the dropdown Part 1 started, matching Billing's/Wallet's/Settings' own "FINAL shape" declarations once their own last part ships.

**i18n**: extended the `accounting` namespace in all 3 locale files with `integritySweep.{page,runButton,list,findings}` + `shell.nav.accountingIntegritySweep`, real Swahili/French translations (e.g. `runButton.trigger` → sw `"Endesha ukaguzi wa uadilifu"` / fr `"Lancer le contrôle d'intégrité"`). Inserted via direct `Edit` calls (only 2 clean insertion points needed per file, unlike Part 1's much larger multi-namespace insertion) rather than a throwaway Node script.

### A real, live-verification-only backend bug found and fixed — migration `0238-widen-gl-integrity-run-kind.ts`

The very first real call to `POST /accounting/integrity-sweep/run` against this dev DB — the first time this route had EVER been exercised by anything, confirmed by reading `IntegritySweepService`'s own code and finding no test suite calls it either — failed with a real `500`: `{"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"value too long for type character varying(20)"}}`. Root-caused directly: `app.gl_integrity_run.kind` was created `varchar(20)` by migration `0060`, but `IntegritySweepService`'s own `SWEEP_KIND` constant is the literal 35-character string `"PERIOD_ACCOUNT_TOTAL_RECONCILIATION"` — nearly double the column's width. This is 100% reproducible, not a corner case: every call to `runSweep()` has failed this way since the day the service was written. Wallet's own sibling sweep (`WALLET_RECONCILE`, 16 characters, sharing this same `gl_integrity_run` table) fit fine, which is exactly why nobody had noticed — confirmed live, `GET .../runs` returned 5 real pre-existing `WALLET_RECONCILE` rows before this module's own first successful run.

Fixed with the smallest possible targeted migration: `ALTER TABLE app.gl_integrity_run ALTER COLUMN kind TYPE varchar(64)` (headroom beyond the 35-char constant, matching `docv_record.document_type varchar(60)`'s own precedent for a similar short-classification column) — no other column, trigger, or application code touched. `gl_integrity_run` is not writer-guarded (confirmed via `IntegritySweepService`'s own doc comment — only `gl_journal`/`gl_journal_line`/`gl_period_account_total` carry `trg_gl_writer_guard`), so no `application_name` workaround was needed. This is a deliberate, narrow departure from Parts 1-3's own "frontend-only" scope, justified because without it this part's own required live round-trip verification was IMPOSSIBLE, not merely inconvenient — `POST .../run` cannot ever succeed without this fix, on any database, regardless of who's calling it.

### A second real, live-verification-only finding — `gl_integrity_run` is a table SHARED across modules, with a real crash risk this pass fixed proactively

`GET .../runs` has no `kind` filter at all (confirmed by reading `IntegritySweepController`/`IntegritySweepService.listRecent()` directly) — it returns every `gl_integrity_run` row regardless of which module wrote it. Confirmed live: the baseline call (before this module's own first run) returned 5 real `WALLET_RECONCILE` rows, Wallet's own reconciliation sweep. A `WALLET_RECONCILE` row's real `findings` shape (`{variance, walletCount, walletTotal, glControlBalance}`) has no `mismatches` array at all — the original `parseIntegrityFindings()` implementation asserted `findings` straight into this module's own shape and called `.mismatches.length` on it unconditionally, which would throw a real `TypeError` the instant a user expanded one of these rows in the UI. Caught and fixed BEFORE any live click could hit it (code review while building, not discovered via a crash): `parseIntegrityFindings()` now returns `null` for a non-matching shape, `integrity-run-list.tsx`'s mismatch-count column shows `"—"` for such a row, and `integrity-run-findings.tsx` falls back to a raw `<pre>{JSON.stringify(...)}</pre>` dump — the same presentation `wallet/reconciliation/page.tsx`'s own `ReconciliationResultCard` already uses for this exact shape, so a user expanding one of these rows here sees the same honest result they'd see on that module's own screen, not a blank panel or an error.

### A real, non-fabricated mismatch result — this dev DB genuinely has drift, better verification coverage than the plan's own assumption

The plan anticipated a clean DB ("you likely won't get a real mismatch to display") and offered an OPTIONAL manual-corruption path to exercise the findings-display UI. That path was never needed: the first successful real sweep (after the migration fix) found **330 real, pre-existing mismatches**, `ok: false` — genuine drift accumulated from many months of heavy multi-slice manual testing against this shared dev DB (journal posts/reversals, direct `psql` fixture inserts across dozens of prior verification passes throughout this whole project), not anything introduced by this pass. This is the sweep tool doing exactly its documented job. It also means the findings table was exercised with REAL data end-to-end, not synthetic corruption — a sample mismatch row (`periodId 019fa736-9b7e-7a3f-9273-732ab2da5ccb`, `accountId 019fa736-9b7e-77de-8729-0fa320953f96`, `stored: null`, `derived: {debitTotal:"0.0000", creditTotal:"25.0000"}`) was cross-checked directly against `psql`: the period (`#1, 2026-01-01..2026-01-31`) and account (`ACC-OFFSET-16801657 — ACC Offset`) both resolve to real rows, confirming the label-resolution hooks in `integrity-run-findings.tsx` would show real names, not fall through to raw UUIDs, for this actual data. No local data was corrupted or altered by this pass — the sweep is read-only against `gl_journal_line`/`gl_period_account_total`, confirmed by reading `IntegritySweepService` directly before running anything.

## Slice 17 — closing summary (Parts 1–4 complete)

Phase 6 Slice 17 built Module 7 (Accounting Core)'s entire frontend from zero across 4 parts, against a backend that had been complete but completely unused by any frontend since Phase 5 (2026-07-17): **Part 1** — Chart of Accounts (recursive tree + CRUD), Fiscal Years/Periods (auto-generated periods, sequential open/soft-close/hard-close), Cost Centers; **Part 2** — Journals (manual entry with a real client-side debit/credit-balance editor, reversal, filtering); **Part 3** — Budgets (lines, submit/activate/reject against the Approvals engine); **Part 4** — Integrity Sweep (on-demand reconciliation run button, run history, real findings drill-down). The Accounting nav dropdown was built incrementally, one set of children per part (3 in Part 1, then 1 each in Parts 2-4), now in its **FINAL shape at 6 children** — no more are planned.

Every part found at least one genuine, previously-undetected backend finding while doing REAL live verification against the running API — never trusted a compile pass or a written report alone: Part 1 found a fiscal year derivatively flips to `CLOSING` the moment its FIRST period (not its last) is hard-closed; Part 2 found `PostingService.reverse()` has no guard against double-reversing the same journal, confirmed by producing two real reversal rows for one original; Part 3 found a real, active `GL_BUDGET` approval workflow already seeded in this dev DB (contradicting `BudgetsService`'s own doc comment) and that the manual activate/reject approval stand-in never updates the underlying `appr_instance` row, leaving it `PENDING` forever regardless of the budget's real outcome; **Part 4 found — and, uniquely among this slice's 4 parts, had to actually FIX via a real migration — that `gl_integrity_run.kind` was too narrow for its own service's own constant, meaning `POST .../run` had a 100% failure rate since the day it was written, undetected until this pass called it for the first time ever**, plus a second, related finding that the same table is silently shared with Wallet's own reconciliation sweep with no `kind` filter on the list route, which this part's own frontend code now handles defensively rather than crashing on. None of these were fabricated or assumed — every one is backed by a direct `psql` query or a `tsc`-verified code-review finding, and Part 4's own bug carries a real, reproducible `500` response and a real migration fixing it as evidence.

Money fields (debit/credit/`annualAmount`/mismatch totals) were handled as decimal strings throughout every part, never native float math. Every part except Part 4 hit and fixed real `openapi-typescript` codegen gaps (nullable fields degrading to `Record<string, never> | null`, `default`-bearing fields losing `?` optionality, required-but-actually-optional query params) using one consistent cast-at-the-boundary pattern established in Part 1; Part 4's own `findings` field had no generated shape to gap at all (`type: "object"`), so it used a hand-defined interface plus a structural runtime guard instead — a genuinely different class of fix from the rest of the slice, documented as such rather than forced into the same pattern. i18n grew across the slice to its final state of **3210 lines** and **2574 keys** per locale (`en`/`sw`/`fr`), staying valid JSON and structurally in sync throughout, with real (not machine-translated-sounding) Swahili/French translations. No browser-automation tool was available at any point in this whole slice — every part's verification relied on real HTTP round trips cross-checked directly against `psql`, plus `curl`-based SSR sanity checks, matching every other slice in this project's own standing discipline. Dev servers (`apps/api` 3000, `apps/worker` 3001, `apps/web` 3002) and the local Docker stack (`postgres`/`redis`/`minio`) were confirmed healthy at the start of Part 4's own dispatch (consistent with a recent machine/session reset noted going into this part) and remained healthy throughout, with the standard 7 `node.exe` processes and nothing extra left running at the end. Module 7 (Accounting Core) is now functionally complete end-to-end on the frontend — Chart of Accounts, Fiscal Years/Periods, Cost Centers, Journals, Budgets, and Integrity Sweep all have real, working, verified screens reachable from one completed nav dropdown.

### Real codegen gaps found — the usual class, plus one genuinely NEW, opposite-direction finding

Checked every field of `CreateSupplierDto`/`UpdateSupplierDto`/`SupplierResponseDto`/the list/search query params directly against `packages/contracts/src/generated/openapi-types.ts`, not assumed from the Slice 17 pattern:

1. **`SuppliersController_list`'s `status` query param and `SuppliersController_search`'s `q`/`limit` query params** are typed as required (non-optional) strings in the generated types even though the real controller (`@Query("status") status?: ProcSupplierStatus`, `@Query("q") q: string, @Query("limit") limit?: string`) treats `status`/`limit` as genuinely optional — the same class of gap `accounts.api.ts` already documented in Slice 17 Part 1. Fixed the same way: conditional query-object construction, not empty-string padding.
2. **`CreateSupplierDto.paymentTermsDays`** degrades to a required `number` in the generated request body, because `create-supplier.dto.ts`'s own `@ApiPropertyOptional({ default: 30 })` decorator carries a Swagger `default` — the exact same `openapi-typescript` quirk `CreateAccountDto.isControl`/`CreateFiscalYearDto.periodCount` already documented. Fixed with a local `CreateSupplierRequestBody` interface mirroring the GENERATED (gapped) shape, cast at the one `apiClient.POST` call boundary — confirmed correct via a real `tsc --noEmit` run, not assumed. **`UpdateSupplierDto`'s generated shape has ZERO gaps** (no Swagger `default` on its own `paymentTermsDays`) — `updateSupplier()` passes its `dto` straight through with no cast, matching `journals.api.ts`'s own "zero request-body gaps" precedent from Slice 17 Part 2.
3. **A genuinely NEW finding, in the OPPOSITE direction from every prior codegen-gap writeup in this project**: `@klickit/contracts`'s own zod-inferred `CreateSupplierDto`/`UpdateSupplierDto` types `tradingName`/`kraPin` as `string | undefined` — NO `null` in the union — even though the real, authoritative `packages/server` class-validator DTOs declare both `@ApiPropertyOptional({..., nullable: true})`, and the GENERATED openapi type correctly includes `| null`. The zod mirror script simply didn't carry the `nullable: true` flag over for these two fields. Net effect: here the "real" contracts type is the NARROWER, less-capable one, and the generated type is the accurate one — the reverse of every gap Slice 17 found. Confirmed by reading `create-supplier.dto.ts`/`update-supplier.dto.ts` directly (not assumed from the zod file alone) and by reasoning through class-validator's own `@IsOptional()` null-passthrough semantics. This pass makes a documented, deliberate call NOT to chase this one down with a cast (see "Honest gaps" below) rather than let it silently force a change to this file's own typing discipline.

### Judgment calls (the task brief's own explicit "your call, document it" points)

1. **One `create-po-dialog.tsx`, not two separate components.** `POST /purchase-orders` and `POST /purchase-orders/direct` share the exact same `CreatePurchaseOrderDto` body and every form field (supplier, order date, delivery terms, lines) — the only real difference is which id rides along and which endpoint receives it. A plain two-button segmented control toggles "From requisition" / "Direct" (no `Tabs`/`RadioGroup` primitive exists in `components/ui/` yet, confirmed by listing that directory before reaching for a new dependency). `procurement:po:create-direct` is NOT hidden client-side when the toggle is set to "Direct" — no permission-list endpoint exists anywhere in this codebase (the same standing limitation every nav-gating doc comment already documents), so a role without it gets a real 403 surfaced via `ApiError.message`, not a silently-disabled option. **Verified live**: see below.
2. **`revise-po-dialog.tsx` builds BOTH line modes** — "keep existing lines" (default, omits `lines` entirely) and "specify new lines" (lazily loads the original PO's own current lines as a real starting point via `usePurchaseOrderLines`, editable through the shared `<PoLineEditor>`).
3. **Quotations gets no top-level nav entry.** `QuotationsController_list`'s `requisitionId` query param is genuinely required (confirmed by reading the controller directly — no "list every quotation" route exists at all), so a bare nav entry would have nowhere meaningful to land. The real entry point is the new "View quotations" action on an APPROVED/CONVERTED requisition's own detail page; `quotations/page.tsx` itself also offers a plain APPROVED-requisition picker for anyone who lands there without the query param (bookmarked, or navigated to directly), so it's still a real, useful standalone screen, not a dead end.
4. **A selected awarded quotation prefills the PO's supplier + lines** in `create-po-dialog.tsx` (a one-shot `getQuotationLines()` copy into local form state, not a live sync) — a convenience beyond the plan's own minimum, since re-typing a quotation's already-captured lines by hand would be an obviously bad flow once a quote has been awarded.

### Real codegen gaps found — one repeat of the standing `Date`-vs-string class, otherwise unusually clean

Checked every field of `CreateQuotationDto`/`AwardQuotationDto`/`QuotationResponseDto`/`QuotationLineResponseDto`/`CreatePurchaseOrderDto`/`RevisePurchaseOrderDto`/`PurchaseOrderResponseDto`/`PurchaseOrderLineResponseDto` and both list endpoints' query params directly against `packages/contracts/src/generated/openapi-types.ts`:

1. **`PurchaseOrderResponseDto.issuedAt`** — the one real gap this part found — degrades the same way `CashierSessionResponseDto.openedAt`/`ChequeResponseDto.statusChangedAt` (Slice 4/6, `features/payments/types.ts`) already documented: `purchase-order.dto.ts`'s own `Date | null`-typed field produces a zod mirror of `z.coerce.date().nullable()`, but `unwrapApiResult<T>()` never parses anything — the real wire value is a string. Fixed the identical way: `purchase-orders.api.ts` exports a `PurchaseOrder` type overriding just `issuedAt` to `string | null`; every component in this part imports `PurchaseOrder`, never `PurchaseOrderResponseDto` directly.
2. **`PurchaseOrdersController_list`'s `status`/`supplierId` query params** are typed required in the generated type though the real controller treats both as optional — the same standing class of gap `requisitions.api.ts`/`suppliers.api.ts` already documented; fixed the same way (conditional query-object construction).
3. **One genuine finding in the OPPOSITE direction, worth flagging for the next person**: `QuotationsController_list`'s generated `requisitionId` query param is a plain required `string` — and this time that's ACCURATE, not a gap. The real controller has no optional variant at all (`QuotationsService.listByRequisition()` has no "list everything" fallback), so `listQuotationsByRequisition()` takes it as a required positional argument, not a filter object.
4. **Zero request-body gaps anywhere in this part** — none of `CreateQuotationDto`'s/`CreatePurchaseOrderDto`'s/`RevisePurchaseOrderDto`'s optional fields carry a Swagger `default`, so every generated body type stays correctly optional and every `create*`/`revise*` function passes its `dto` straight through with no cast — the cleanest of the 3 parts in this slice on this front.

Used Part 2's own leftover APPROVED requisition `PRO-000015` (`019ff5d1-22ef-76d5-b0f9-759ec6d0d055`) and Part 1's own 2 leftover suppliers.

- **Quotations**: 2 real quotes captured against `PRO-000015` — Supplier A (`20×9.00 + 5×3.50 = 197.50`) and Supplier B (`20×8.00 + 5×2.75 = 173.75`) — both totals and every line cross-checked directly against `psql` (`app.proc_quotation`/`app.proc_quotation_line`), not just trusted from the response. Attempting to award Supplier A's quote too → real `409`, `"uq_award_p: requisition ... already has an awarded quotation"` — the exact constraint-backed message `award()`'s own doc comment predicted, confirming `quotation-comparison.tsx`'s 409-handling branch is reachable, not hypothetical.
- **PO create → submit → approve → issue**: a real PO created from the requisition + its awarded quotation (`quotationId` set, `supplierId`/lines matching the quote) → `paymentTermsDays: 60` correctly snapshotted from the supplier (the same value Part 1's own live verification set on this exact supplier). `number` started as `DRAFT-019ff5f2...` (confirmed `isDraftPlaceholderNumber()` would correctly flag it). Submit → `PENDING_APPROVAL` with a real `approvalRef` (a real, active workflow already exists for this domain in this dev DB — submit never 422'd on "no workflow configured", the same finding class Part 2 made for `PROCUREMENT_REQUISITION`, now also true for the PO's own domain). Approve → `APPROVED`. **Issue → `ISSUED`, `number` became the real allocated `PRO-000015`** — the placeholder-to-real-number transition confirmed via both the response body and a follow-up `psql SELECT`.
- **Revise → the single most important behavior in this part, verified for real via `psql`, not just trusted from API responses**: revising the ISSUED PO (delivery terms changed, `lines` omitted to carry the original's forward) → a genuinely new row, `revision: 1`, `supersedesId` pointing at the original, `status: DRAFT`, lines confirmed identical to the original's own 2 lines via `psql` (`app.proc_po_line`). Pushed THAT revision through submit → approve → issue too → **`number` became `PRO-000015-R1`** (the exact `${originalNumber}-R${revision}` format the plan predicted) — and a follow-up `psql SELECT` on BOTH rows confirmed the original (`PRO-000015`, revision 0) had genuinely flipped to `status = 'CANCELLED'` in the same transaction, while the revision (`PRO-000015-R1`, revision 1) sat at `ISSUED`. This is exactly the mechanic `po-status-actions.tsx`'s issue-confirm dialog warns about before the user clicks through, now confirmed to actually happen server-side, not just documented.
- **Negative paths, all real, not hypothetical**: creating a SECOND PO from the same requisition (now `CONVERTED` from the first create) → real `422`, `"BR-PROC-01: PO creation requires an APPROVED requisition unless bypassRequisition=true (requisition ... status=CONVERTED)"` — confirms `create-po-dialog.tsx`'s own reliance on the server-side guard is warranted, not just client-side. Calling `POST /purchase-orders/direct` WITHOUT `procurement:po:create-direct` (deliberately not granted to this throwaway role, matching the exact 5-permission list the task brief specifies) → real `403`, `"Missing required permission \"procurement:po:create-direct\""` — directly validates Judgment call #1 above: a role without this permission genuinely cannot silently bypass anything, the dialog's own reliance on a real 403 (rather than client-side hiding) is the correct, working design.
- **Two genuine, non-hypothetical backend findings surfaced by this live run, neither a frontend bug**:
  1. **`PROC_REQUISITION` and `PROC_PO` numbering series share the identical `PRO-` prefix with fully independent counters** (confirmed directly in `app.set_numbering_series`: 5 separate `doc_type` rows — `PROC_REQUISITION`/`PROC_PO`/`PROC_GRN`/`PROC_SUPPLIER_INVOICE`/`PROC_PAYMENT_VOUCHER` — all configured with `prefix = 'PRO-'`). This is exactly what produced the coincidental collision above: the requisition `PRO-000015` and the original PO `PRO-000015` are two DIFFERENT documents that happen to render an IDENTICAL formatted number, with no way to tell them apart from the number alone. Flagged here for the record — a `packages/server`/seed-data numbering-series configuration issue, out of scope for this frontend-only part to fix, but real and reproducible (not a one-off fluke — 4 of the 5 procurement doc types share this exact prefix).

## Slice 18 (Part 4 — GRN + Supplier Invoices) — 2026-08-12

Two controllers this part: `GrnController`'s full 5-route surface (receive against an ISSUED/PARTIALLY_RECEIVED PO with real per-line partial-receipt tolerance, list-by-PO, detail, lines, post) and `SupplierInvoicesController`'s full 6-route surface (capture PO-linked or ad-hoc, list/detail, FR-PROC-007.1's 3-way match, resolve-exception, P-20 post). Built following Parts 1-3's own established conventions for this feature folder.

### What was built

**`features/procurement/api/{grn,supplier-invoices}.api.ts`** — `receiveGrn`/`listGrnByPo`/`getGrn`/`getGrnLines`/`postGrn`; `listSupplierInvoices`/`getSupplierInvoice`/`captureSupplierInvoice`/`matchSupplierInvoice`/`resolveSupplierInvoiceException`/`postSupplierInvoice`, typed directly against `@klickit/contracts`' generated DTOs. `grn.api.ts` exports a `Grn` override type for the `receivedAt` field (see codegen-gaps below) and reuses `purchase-orders.api.ts`'s own `isDraftPlaceholderNumber()` as-is for GRN's own identically-shaped `DRAFT-<uuid>` placeholder number (`GrnService.receive()` allocates it the exact same way).

**`features/procurement/hooks/{use-grn,use-supplier-invoices}.ts`** — query/mutation hooks under `["procurement", "grn"]`/`["procurement", "supplier-invoices"]` keys, mirroring Parts 2-3's shape. `use-grn.ts`'s mutations also invalidate `PURCHASE_ORDERS_QUERY_KEY` (imported from `use-purchase-orders.ts`) since `receive()` rolls the parent PO's own status/line quantities.

**`features/procurement/lib/invoice-match.ts`** — the hand-defined `matchVariance` shape (`InvoiceMatchVariance`/`InvoiceMatchVarianceLine`/`InvoiceMatchVarianceTolerances`/`InvoiceMatchVarianceResolution`) read directly off `SupplierInvoicesService.matchAgainstPo()`'s own `MatchVarianceResult` interface, plus `parseInvoiceMatchVariance()` — mirrors Slice 17 Part 4's `integrity-findings.ts` pattern (returns `null` for a non-matching shape rather than asserting blindly), though this column is NOT a shared/multi-producer table the way `gl_integrity_run` is, so the defensive parsing here is precautionary rather than guarding a known live collision.

**`features/procurement/components/`**: `receive-grn-dialog.tsx` (per-PO-line receive form — ordered/already-received/remaining/receive-now/rejected/rejection-reason/unit-cost, `remainingQty()` computed via `sumMoneyStrings`'s own negation trick since `lib/money.ts` has no subtract helper, self-gates to ISSUED/PARTIALLY_RECEIVED and can be opened/submitted repeatedly for successive partial receipts), `grn-list.tsx` (a PO's GRN history table + an inline per-row `PostGrnButton` confirm dialog — see "GRN has no dedicated route" below), `capture-supplier-invoice-dialog.tsx` (one dialog supporting BOTH PO-linked and ad-hoc capture, an optional per-PO-line integrity-check editor that only appears once a PO is picked, reusing `po-lines.ts`'s own `multiplyDecimalStrings` for the live sum-vs-total hint), `invoice-match-panel.tsx` (the real exception-review UI — invoice total vs PO-ordered vs GRN-accepted, both tolerance dimensions as pass/fail badges plus the combined verdict, a per-PO-line breakdown table, and the resolution audit trail once present), `resolve-exception-dialog.tsx` (ACCEPT_VARIANCE/REJECT segmented control + required note, mirroring `blacklist-supplier-dialog.tsx`'s own required-reason confirm-dialog shape).

**Routes**: `app/(erp)/procurement/supplier-invoices/{page.tsx, [id]/page.tsx}` (list with inline status/supplier filters + capture; detail with header, PO cross-link, journal link, `<InvoiceMatchPanel>`, and a confirm-dialog Post action). **GRN gets NO dedicated route at all — neither list nor detail** (see "Judgment call" below); `app/(erp)/procurement/purchase-orders/[id]/page.tsx` (Part 3) was edited instead — `<ReceiveGrnDialog>` sits next to `<PoStatusActions>` in the header (self-gates on ISSUED/PARTIALLY_RECEIVED), and a GRN History card (`<GrnList>`) is shown once the PO has a real, non-placeholder number (reusing `isDraftPlaceholderNumber()` rather than hand-listing the receivable statuses again).

**Nav**: Supplier Invoices appended as the Procurement dropdown's 4th child (`procurement:supplier-invoice:manage`-gated). **GRN deliberately gets no nav entry**, matching Part 3's own precedent for Quotations.

**i18n**: new `procurement.{grn, supplierInvoices}` namespaces (all GRN/invoice status labels, receive-form column headers, match-panel copy, resolve-exception copy) plus `shell.nav.procurementSupplierInvoices` and 2 new keys on `procurement.purchaseOrders.detail` (`grnHistoryTitle`/`grnHistoryDescription`), real Swahili/French translations throughout (inserted via a small throwaway Node script, not checked in, the same mechanism Parts 1-3 used to guarantee structural sync) — all 3 locale files landed at identical **3785 lines**, valid JSON, identical **3043**-key sets across all 3 locales (verified programmatically, zero missing/extra either direction).

### Judgment call — GRN has no dedicated frontend route at all, not even a standalone one with a picker fallback

Unlike Quotations (Part 3, which still got its own `quotations/page.tsx` with a requisition-picker fallback even without a nav entry), GRN gets **nothing** beyond what lives inside `purchase-orders/[id]/page.tsx`. `GrnController_list`'s `poId` query param is genuinely required (confirmed by reading the controller directly — no "list every GRN" route exists at all, and this is the one query param in this whole part that's ALREADY correctly typed required in the generated types, unlike every other list endpoint this slice has found), so a top-level list has nowhere to land the same way Quotations did. But unlike a quotation (which a user might reasonably want to look up by browsing, independent of which requisition it came from), a GRN is meaningless without the PO context it was received against — there's no realistic "browse GRNs" use case this part's plan calls for, so no standalone route was built even as a fallback. Receiving, posting, and reviewing GRN history is a complete, real workflow entirely from the PO's own detail page.

### Real codegen gaps found — the standing query-param class, plus a new instance of the `Date`-vs-string gap

Checked every field of `ReceiveGrnDto`/`ReceiveGrnLineDto`/`GrnResponseDto`/`GrnLineResponseDto`/`CaptureSupplierInvoiceDto`/`CaptureSupplierInvoiceLineDto`/`ResolveMatchExceptionDto`/`SupplierInvoiceResponseDto` and both list endpoints' query params directly against `packages/contracts/src/generated/openapi-types.ts`:

1. **`GrnResponseDto.receivedAt`** — a NEW instance of the exact `Date`-vs-string gap `PurchaseOrderResponseDto.issuedAt` already documented, but via a DIFFERENT root cause this time: `grn.dto.ts`'s own `@ApiProperty() receivedAt!: Date;` is non-nullable (no union type), so Swagger CAN correctly reflect it and the generated openapi type is genuinely correct (`receivedAt: string`) — the gap is instead in `@klickit/contracts`' own zod mirror (`grn.schema.ts`), which declares `receivedAt: z.coerce.date()` (inferring a real `Date` in the exported TS type this file actually imports, per `purchase-orders.api.ts`'s own established finding that the zod-inferred type wins over the nested-under-`components` openapi one). `unwrapApiResult<T>()` never parses anything, so the real runtime value is a string. Fixed the identical way: `grn.api.ts` exports a `Grn` type overriding just `receivedAt` to `string`.
2. **`SupplierInvoicesController_list`'s `status`/`supplierId` query params** are typed required in the generated type though the real controller treats both as optional — the same standing class of gap every prior part in this slice has found; fixed the same way (conditional query-object construction). **`GrnController_list`'s `poId`, by contrast, is genuinely, correctly required** — the one list endpoint in this whole slice where the generated type and the real controller already agree.
3. **Zero request-body gaps anywhere in this part** — none of `ReceiveGrnDto`'s/`ReceiveGrnLineDto`'s/`CaptureSupplierInvoiceDto`'s/`CaptureSupplierInvoiceLineDto`'s/`ResolveMatchExceptionDto`'s optional fields carry a Swagger `default`, so every generated body type stays correctly optional and every `receiveGrn()`/`captureSupplierInvoice()`/`resolveSupplierInvoiceException()` call passes its `dto` straight through with no cast.
4. **`SupplierInvoiceResponseDto.invoiceDate`/`.dueDate` have NO `Date`-vs-string gap** — declared plain `@ApiProperty() invoiceDate!: string;` (the entity stores these as strings, not `Date` objects), confirmed against both the DTO and the zod mirror (`z.string()`, no `z.coerce.date()`) directly — worth noting explicitly since it would have been easy to assume every date-shaped field in this part needed the same override `Grn.receivedAt` did.
5. **`matchVariance: Record<string, unknown> | null`** — no generated shape exists at all (neither the raw openapi type nor the zod mirror carries anything beyond a bare record) — see `../lib/invoice-match.ts` above.

## Slice 18 — closing summary (Parts 1–5 complete)

Phase 6 Slice 18 built Module 12 (Procurement)'s entire frontend from zero across 5 parts, against a backend that had been complete but completely unused by any frontend since Phase 5 (2026-07-19): **Part 1** — Suppliers (search, blacklist/reactivate, ratings — honest about the permanently-unavailable `ratingDelivery`); **Part 2** — Requisitions (DRAFT line editing, submit/approve/reject/cancel, real budget-snapshot capture); **Part 3** — Quotations + Purchase Orders (comparison/award, and the full issue→revise→supersede chain, the single most intricate state machine in this module); **Part 4** — GRN + Supplier Invoices (partial receipt with tolerance checking, real 3-way match with an exception-review/resolve workflow); **Part 5** — Payment Vouchers + Contracts (multi-invoice allocation with a real ceiling check, terminate/mark-expired, an expiring-soon widget). The Procurement nav dropdown was built incrementally, one child per part (1 in Part 1, then 1-2 per subsequent part), now in its **FINAL shape at 6 children** — no more are planned.

Every part found at least one genuine, previously-undetected finding while doing REAL live verification against the running API — never trusted a compile pass or a written report alone: Part 1 confirmed the documented `ratingDelivery` gap is real and permanent (no `expected_delivery_date` column exists anywhere to compute it from); Part 3 confirmed the issue/revise/supersede chain works exactly as designed — a revision's own `issue()` call atomically flips the ORIGINAL PO to `CANCELLED` in the same transaction, verified directly via `psql` (`PRO-000015` revision 0 → `CANCELLED`, revision 1 `PRO-000015-R1` → `ISSUED`); Part 4 confirmed a real partial receipt correctly rolls a PO from `ISSUED` to `PARTIALLY_RECEIVED` (not straight to `RECEIVED`) and that a real 3-way match variance lands in exactly the documented `matchVariance` JSON shape; **Part 5's own voucher execution became the 4th real document (after the requisition, its PO, and its GRN/invoice) to land on the identical formatted number `PRO-000015`** — conclusively confirming, across 3 separate parts now, that `PROC_REQUISITION`/`PROC_PO`/`PROC_GRN`/`PROC_PAYMENT_VOUCHER` (at minimum) all share the literal `PRO-` numbering prefix with fully independent counters, a real seed-data/numbering-series-design finding for a future pass to consider, not something this frontend-only slice could or should fix. A second recurring pattern across the whole slice: every approval-gated entity (Requisitions, POs, Payment Vouchers) found a real, already-active workflow configured in this dev DB, so the "no workflow configured" graceful-error UI branch — written and code-reviewed correct in every part per its own plan's instruction — was never once actually exercised live across the entire slice, an honest, consistently-flagged gap rather than a claimed-but-unverified feature.

Money fields (qty/price/total/allocation amounts) were handled as decimal strings throughout every part, never native float math — Part 3 added a local BigInt decimal-multiply helper (`lib/po-lines.ts`) since `lib/money.ts` had no multiply primitive, the first new arithmetic primitive this feature folder needed. Every part hit and fixed real `openapi-typescript` codegen gaps using the consistent cast-at-the-boundary pattern Slice 17 established, plus at least 2 genuinely new gap shapes this slice specifically surfaced (Part 1's contracts-zod-narrower-than-generated-type finding for `tradingName`/`kraPin`; Part 4's `Date`-vs-string gap on `Grn.receivedAt`). Two entities (`findings`/`matchVariance`) had literally no generated shape at all (bare `object`) rather than a degraded-but-present one — Part 4's `invoice-match.ts` followed the exact defensive-parser pattern Slice 17 Part 4 established for `IntegrityRunResponseDto.findings`. i18n grew across the slice to its final state of **3962 lines** and **3569 keys** per locale (`en`/`sw`/`fr`), staying valid JSON and structurally in sync throughout every part, with real (not machine-translated-sounding) Swahili/French translations. No browser-automation tool was available at any point in this whole slice — every part's verification relied on real HTTP round trips cross-checked directly against `psql`, plus `curl`-based SSR sanity checks, matching every other slice in this project's own standing discipline. Two of the five parts (2 and 5) needed the orchestrating session itself to finish verification/documentation after a real infrastructure interruption (a usage-limit or session-reset cutoff) left otherwise-complete, `tsc`-clean code short of its own write-up — in both cases the actual application code was confirmed sound and untouched by the interruption before anything was finished on its behalf. Module 12 (Procurement) is now functionally complete end-to-end on the frontend — Suppliers, Requisitions, Quotations, Purchase Orders, GRN, Supplier Invoices, Payment Vouchers, and Contracts all have real, working, verified screens reachable from one completed nav dropdown, matching Module 7 (Accounting Core)'s own Slice 17 completion.
