Inserted via a small throwaway Node script (not checked in), the same mechanism every prior slice's own i18n pass established to GUARANTEE structural sync — all 3 files landed at identical **4195 lines**, valid JSON, identical **3372**-key sets across all 3 locales (verified programmatically, `Object.keys()` diffed both directions, zero missing/extra).

### `<ItemCombobox>` — a new, generic, reusable picker, and the shared `<Combobox>` primitive's own first extension since it was built

Built on `components/ui/combobox.tsx` rather than a hand-rolled popover: that shared primitive gained one new, purely ADDITIVE, backward-compatible prop — `onQueryChange?: (query: string) => void` — which, when supplied, makes the component skip its own internal client-side substring filter and treat `items` as already-filtered by the caller (necessary for a trigram/fuzzy search result set, where a literal-substring re-filter would incorrectly hide a real fuzzy match). Every one of the ~15 pre-existing callers omits this prop and is completely unaffected (confirmed by the clean `tsc`/`eslint` run below). `<ItemCombobox>` itself is deliberately generic — `value`/`valueLabel`/`onSelect(item: {id,code,name} | null)` only, zero Inventory- or Procurement-specific logic — per the plan's own explicit requirement that it be usable from both this feature AND Procurement's line editors without modification.

### The item-picker retrofit — an additive-only change to already-shipped, already-verified code

`features/procurement/lib/po-lines.ts`'s `PoLineFormRow` gained two new optional fields (`itemId`, `itemLabel` — a client-only display cache, never sent to the server), `poLineRowsToDto()` now includes `itemId` in the wire shape only when set. `po-line-editor.tsx` (shared by `create-quotation-dialog.tsx`/`create-po-dialog.tsx`/`revise-po-dialog.tsx`) gained one new table column hosting `<ItemCombobox>`; `requisition-line-editor.tsx`'s Add/Edit line dialogs each gained one new optional field. In every case, selecting an item sets `itemId` and convenience-prefills the description/free-text field ONLY if it's still empty (never overwrites text already typed); leaving the combobox untouched preserves the EXACT prior behavior byte-for-byte (`itemId` stays unset, free text stays free text, `poLineRowsToDto()`/the requisition-line DTOs omit the key entirely). No Requisition/Quotation/PO submission logic, validation, or any other part of those flows was touched.

### Real codegen gaps found — including a genuinely NEW, more severe class beyond every prior slice's own findings

1. **A real schema-name COLLISION, not just a nullable-field/required-query-param quirk** — `packages/server/src/domains/expenses/api/dto/category.dto.ts` and `packages/server/src/domains/inventory/api/dto/category.dto.ts` both declare classes named `CreateCategoryDto`/`UpdateCategoryDto`/`CategoryResponseDto`. `@nestjs/swagger`'s schema registry collides on the shared name, so `packages/contracts/src/generated/openapi-types.ts`'s `components["schemas"]["CreateCategoryDto"]` reflects EXPENSES' much richer shape (`{name, parentId?, glExpenseAccountId: uuid (required), budgetRequired, isActive}`) everywhere that name is referenced — including inside the GENERATED request-body type for Inventory's own `POST /inventory/categories` route, even though the real, running route only ever reads `name`/`parentId`. `packages/contracts/src/index.ts`'s own generator already recognized this collision and re-exports Inventory's correct, narrow versions under a namespace (`domains_inventory_category_schema`) instead of a flat name — the SAME mechanism `features/wallet/api/wallets.api.ts`'s own `domains_wallet_wallet_transaction_schema` doc comment already established for a different collision, followed here rather than reinvented. `categories.api.ts` reaches the real types via that namespace, and casts request bodies through `CreateCategoryRequestBody`/`UpdateCategoryRequestBody` local interfaces mirroring the GENERATED (collided) shape at the `apiClient.POST`/`.PATCH` call boundary only — the extra `glExpenseAccountId`/`budgetRequired`/`isActive` fields the generated type demands are never actually populated or sent on the wire.
2. A second-order gap ON TOP of the collision: `UpdateCategoryDto.parentId` (expenses' own class field is typed `parentId?: string | null`, an explicit union) hits the familiar "nullable field without an explicit type hint" NestJS/Swagger reflection gap (`accounts.api.ts`'s own `taxTreatment` precedent) and degrades further to `Record<string, never> | null` — asymmetric with `CreateCategoryDto.parentId` (no explicit union on that class field), which stays plain `string | null`. Caught by a real `tsc --noEmit` failure, not assumed.
3. `CreateItemDto`/`UpdateItemDto`'s `uomConversions`/`barcode`/`preferredSupplierIds`/`glIncomeAccountId` all show the "opposite direction" gap Slice 18 Part 1 first found on `tradingName`/`kraPin` (generated type WIDER than the real one, adding `| null`) — `uomConversions` specifically forces a cast at the call boundary DESPITE having no UI field anywhere in this feature, because TypeScript checks whole-object structural assignability, not just the fields a given call site populates at runtime; confirmed by a real `tsc` failure before adding `CreateItemRequestBody`/`UpdateItemRequestBody`.
4. `Stores` had ZERO codegen gaps on either request body — `createStore()`/`updateStore()` pass their `dto` straight through with no cast, matching `journals.api.ts`'s own "zero gaps" precedent.
5. The now-familiar required-vs-actually-optional query-param gap recurred on all 3 controllers' list/search query params, fixed with the same conditional-query-object pattern every prior `*.api.ts` file in this codebase establishes.

### Two genuine, previously-undocumented backend findings from this part's own live verification

1. **A duplicate `name`/`code`/`barcode` on Categories, Stores, AND Items is rejected with a raw `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, not a clean 409/422** — confirmed live for all three (`duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uq_inv_category_name"` / `"uq_inv_store_name"` / `"uq_inv_item_code"`, each leaking verbatim in the response body), and confirmed by reading the code directly: `CategoriesService.create()`/`StoresService.create()`/`ItemsService.create()` have no try/catch around their respective unique-constraint violations, and `AllExceptionsFilter.mapException()` only special-cases `DomainException`/`HttpException` — a raw TypeORM `QueryFailedError` falls straight through to the generic 500 branch, with no Postgres-error-code (`23505`) sniffing anywhere in this codebase's exception pipeline. A real `packages/server` gap, out of scope to fix in this frontend-only part — `ApiError`'s generic `err.message` fallback still surfaces something to the user regardless of status code, just an unpolished raw-SQL message instead of a clean "name already in use."
2. **`ItemsController.findByBarcode()`'s "no match" `null` return does not actually serialize to a JSON `null` body on the wire** — confirmed by byte-inspecting a raw `curl` response (`Content-Length: 0`, zero bytes, not even the 4-byte string `null`). NestJS's Express adapter treats a controller method returning JS `null` identically to `undefined` for response purposes. `openapi-fetch` (confirmed by reading its own source directly) already handles a `Content-Length: 0` response defensively — short-circuiting to `{data: undefined, response}` without attempting a JSON parse that would otherwise throw on an empty body — so nothing crashes, but the value is `undefined`, not `null`. `findItemByBarcode()` explicitly coerces `undefined -> null` at this one call site so its own declared `Promise<ItemResponseDto | null>` return type is honestly true at runtime, not just a type annotation masking a real mismatch.

### A significant, previously-undetected backend finding — `POST /inventory/stock-takes` appears to have never successfully created a real row

While seeding test data for this part's own live verification (Stock Takes' `post()` is the only documented path to get real stock into a fresh item/store pair — see this slice's own plan document), a real `POST /inventory/stock-takes` call against a genuinely fresh item (zero prior balance history) failed with a raw `500`: `{"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')"}}`. Investigating further (not fixing — this is Stock Takes' own domain, Part 3's scope, not Part 2's):
- `StockTakesService.createSession()`'s own code (read directly) handles both the `"ALL"` and explicit-`itemIds` scope branches correctly, including a null-balance fallback (`balance?.qty ?? "0.0000"`) — the crash does not appear to originate in the service's own business logic.
- **`app.set_numbering_series` shows `INV_STOCK_TAKE`'s counter at `next_no=14` (13 numbers already allocated), but `app.inv_stock_take` has ZERO rows** — meaning every prior attempt to create a stock take in this dev database's entire history has failed the same way (`NumberingService.allocate()`'s own counter increments even when the surrounding transaction later rolls back, a correct anti-reuse property, but it means 13 silent prior failures, not 13 successes).
- `StockTakeScopeDto.itemIds` (`api/dto/stock-take.dto.ts:7-13`) carries **no runtime validation decorators at all** (`@IsArray`/`@IsUUID` are absent, only Swagger metadata) despite the outer `CreateStockTakeDto.scope` using `@ValidateNested()` + `@Type(() => StockTakeScopeDto)` — a plausible root cause (not confirmed) is `class-transformer`'s handling of a bare `string[] | "ALL"` union field without an explicit `@Type`/transform strategy on `itemIds` itself, potentially producing a malformed value by the time the controller hands `dto.scope` to the service.
- `StockTakesService`'s own unit test suite (`__tests__/stock-takes.service.spec.ts`) is part of the 846/846 passing this module reported in Phase 5 — but unit tests construct the service's input object directly in memory, bypassing the real HTTP DTO-transformation pipeline entirely, which is consistent with the service logic itself being correct while the real controller/DTO layer is broken.
- **This is flagged prominently for Part 3 (Stock Takes) to investigate and fix as its own first task** — Stock Takes cannot ship without `POST /inventory/stock-takes` genuinely working, and per this slice's own plan document, Stock Takes is also the *only* documented way to seed opening stock anywhere in this system, so this bug currently blocks not just its own module but full positive-path testing of Movements/Transfers too (see below).

## Slice 19 (Part 3 — Stock Takes) — 2026-08-13

The last part of Module 13's frontend: `StockTakesController`'s full create→count→submit→decide→post lifecycle. Leads with a real backend bug fix — the route this whole part depends on had never once successfully created a row in this database's history.

### Backend fix — `POST /inventory/stock-takes`'s 500, root-caused via the real server stack trace

Confirmed root cause (not guessed): the global `ValidationPipe` (`apps/api/src/app.module.ts`) runs with `whitelist: true`. `CreateStockTakeDto.scope` is validated via `@ValidateNested()` + `@Type(() => StockTakeScopeDto)`, so class-validator recurses into `StockTakeScopeDto` — but `itemIds` (`string[] | "ALL"`) carried **zero validation decorators**, and class-validator's own documented whitelist behavior silently **strips any property with no validators** before the transformed object ever reaches the controller. Every real `POST /inventory/stock-takes` call therefore hit `StockTakesService.createSession()`'s `input.scope.itemIds.length` check against `undefined`, crashing with exactly the reported `500`. Confirmed with `app.set_numbering_series.next_no` at 14 for `INV_STOCK_TAKE` against **zero** real `app.inv_stock_take` rows — every one of 13 prior attempts, across this database's entire history, had failed the identical way undetected.

**Fix**: `packages/server/src/domains/inventory/api/dto/stock-take.dto.ts` — a small custom `class-validator` constraint (`IsAllOrUuidArrayConstraint`, `@Validate(IsAllOrUuidArrayConstraint)` on `itemIds`) that accepts the literal `"ALL"` or a non-empty UUID array. Having ANY registered decorator stops the whitelist strip; the constraint also gives the field real validation instead of silently passing through malformed input. **Proactively found and flagged (not fixed, out of this part's scope) the identical bug shape** in `domains/fixed-assets/api/dto/verification.dto.ts`'s `FaVerificationScopeDto` (`assetIds: string[] | "ALL"`, also zero decorators) — a real, load-bearing note for whenever Module 17 (Fixed Assets) gets its own frontend pass.

**Verified live, independently, by me (the orchestrating session)**: `pnpm --filter server exec tsc --noEmit` clean; the exact previously-crashing call (`POST /inventory/stock-takes` with a real item id) now returns a real `201` with a genuine `app.inv_stock_take` row, confirmed via `psql`.

### What was built

`features/inventory/api/stock-takes.api.ts` (create/list/get/getLines/recordCounts/submit/decide/post, plus a small approvals-status helper); `hooks/use-stock-takes.ts`; components `create-stock-take-dialog.tsx` (store + ALL-vs-explicit-items scope), `stock-take-count-form.tsx` (snapshot/counted editor, batch submit), `stock-take-status-actions.tsx` — **Post is gated by the REAL underlying `appr_instance` status via `GET /approvals/instances/{approvalRef}`, never by the stock take's own `status` field**, since `inv_stock_take` has no `APPROVED` enum value at all (confirmed live below). Routes `app/(erp)/inventory/stock-takes/{page.tsx,[id]/page.tsx}`. Nav: **Stock Takes appended as the Inventory dropdown's 6th and FINAL child** — no more Inventory nav children planned, completing the dropdown Part 1 started. i18n: `inventory.stockTakes.*` (6 status labels, count-form copy) + 1 `shell.nav.*` key, real Swahili/French translations, all 3 locales structurally verified in sync (identical 4404-line counts).

**Process note, matching this slice's own recurring pattern (Parts 1-2 both hit this)**: this part's dispatch was interrupted mid-response (a connection failure) right as it was moving into final SSR verification — the backend fix AND all frontend code were already complete and `tsc`-clean at that point, confirmed by direct inspection. I (the orchestrating session) performed essentially all of the live verification described below myself, and am the author of this write-up.

### Verification — the real approval-status quirk, confirmed exactly as designed, plus Part 2's gap fully closed

A throwaway role/user (`Slice19Pt3 StockTakes Verify`, permissions: `inventory:stock-take:*`, `inventory:movement:{view,issue}`, `inventory:transfer:{issue,receive}`, `approvals:instance:{view,decide}`, `inventory:store:manage`) plus a SECOND user (found already created by the interrupted agent, holding the `System Admin` role — reused rather than duplicated) for the approval decision itself:

1. **Create**: real `201` against a real item+store (Part 2's own leftover `S19STK-...` item / `Slice19 Verify Store ...`), a real `app.inv_stock_take` row with a real snapshot line (`snapshot_qty: 25.0000`, the item's real balance at that point).
2. **Count**: `POST .../counts` with `countedQty: "30"` → real `201`, status auto-advanced `OPEN → REVIEW` (skipping the visible `COUNTING` step since this was a single batch covering the only line).

4. **The self-approval guard, confirmed for real**: attempting to decide as the SAME user who submitted → real `403`, `"BR-APPR-01: an initiator can never approve, reject, or return their own request, at any level"` — the same rule enforced everywhere else in this project, now confirmed for Stock Takes' `STOCK_ADJUSTMENTS` domain too.
5. **The core finding this part exists to verify**: decided `APPROVE` as the second (different) user via `POST /approvals/instances/{approvalRef}/decide` → the real `appr_instance` genuinely flips to `status: "APPROVED"` (a real decision `action` row, `decidedAt` set). **The stock take's own `GET .../{id}` response is re-checked immediately after and still reads `status: "PENDING_APPROVAL"`** — exactly the documented divergence: `inv_stock_take` has no `APPROVED` value in its own status enum, so the two states genuinely diverge, and only the approval instance ever reflects the real decision. Confirms the frontend's `Post`-button gating logic (checking `GET /approvals/instances/{approvalRef}`, not `stockTake.status`) is not just defensively cautious — it is the ONLY way the button could ever correctly enable.
6. **Post**: real `201`, `status → POSTED`. Cross-checked directly via `psql`: a real `app.inv_movement` `ADJUSTMENT` row exists (`qty: 5.0000`, referencing the stock-take LINE's own id as `ref_doc_id`, not the take's id — a real, correct distinction, not a query mistake left uncaught), `app.inv_stock_balance` now shows `qty: 30.0000` for that item+store. `journal_id` correctly stayed `null` — this item's `avg_cost` was `0` (never received with a real cost basis), so the variance's *quantity* was nonzero but its *value* was exactly zero, and per `StockTakesService.post()`'s own documented design ("if net variance is exactly zero ... no journal is posted, a legitimate outcome"), no P-24 journal was created. Confirmed this is correct behavior, not a bug, by reading the service code directly before accepting it.
7. **Part 2's own blocked gap, now fully closed**: with real positive stock (30 units) now existing, a real `POST /inventory/stock-movements/issue` (5 units) succeeded (`201`, balance → 25), and a real Transfer issue→receive round trip (10 units, Store A → Store B) succeeded end-to-end — `psql` confirms both stores' final balances are exactly correct (`15.0000` at the source, `10.0000` at the destination: `30 − 5 (issue) − 10 (transfer out) = 15`; `0 + 10 (transfer in) = 10`).
8. **Cleanup**: both throwaway users deactivated, confirmed via `psql`. The real test stock-take/movements/transfer/journal rows were left in place — no delete route exists for any of them (confirmed by reading every relevant controller), matching this codebase's established precedent.

## Slice 19 — closing summary (Parts 1–3 complete)

Phase 6 Slice 19 built Module 13 (Inventory)'s entire frontend from zero across 3 parts, against a backend that had been complete but completely unused by any frontend since Phase 5 (2026-07-19): **Part 1** — Categories, Stores, Items (with BR-INV-04's RESALE-only-fields enforcement), plus a reusable `<ItemCombobox>` retrofitted into 3 already-shipped Procurement screens (Requisitions/Quotations/POs), genuinely closing a gap Slice 18 had left open; **Part 2** — Stock Movements (balance/history reads, manual Issue) and Transfers (issue/receive/cancel); **Part 3** — Stock Takes (create/count/submit/decide/post), which also required fixing a real, previously-undetected backend bug that had silently broken stock-take creation since the feature was first built. The Inventory nav dropdown was built incrementally, one set of children per part (3 in Part 1, 2 in Part 2, 1 in Part 3), now in its **FINAL shape at 6 children** — no more are planned.

This slice found more genuine, previously-undetected backend issues than any prior slice — three real bugs, not stylistic nitpicks: (1) Part 1's schema-name collision between `domains/expenses` and `domains/inventory`'s generated `Create/Update/ResponseCategoryDto` names in the OpenAPI codegen output, requiring the namespaced export path; (2) Part 1's confirmed, reproducible raw-`500` on duplicate category/store/item names (no unique-constraint catch exists anywhere in that service layer — documented, not fixed, genuinely out of a frontend slice's scope); (3) Part 3's `ValidationPipe`-whitelist-silently-strips-undeclared-nested-properties bug in `POST /inventory/stock-takes`, root-caused via a real server stack trace and fixed with a minimal custom validator — plus a proactive flag of the identical bug shape already latent in Fixed Assets' own DTO, left for whenever that module gets its own frontend pass. Two more real, live-confirmed *behavioral* findings, not bugs: Part 2 confirmed there is genuinely no way to receive/seed stock via any HTTP route except Stock Takes (no `recordReceipt`/`recordSale`/`recordReturn` controller routes exist at all); Part 3 confirmed the stock-take approval-status divergence exactly as the slice's own plan predicted — `inv_stock_take.status` never reaches `APPROVED`, only the underlying `appr_instance` does, requiring the frontend to check the real approval instance directly rather than the entity's own status field.

Every part hit and fixed real `openapi-typescript` codegen gaps using the established cast-at-the-boundary pattern. Inventory introduced this project's first new decimal-precision discipline beyond the existing scale-4 `Money` type — `qty` (scale-4) and `avgCost`/`unitCost` (scale-6) fields, handled via a new small `lib/decimal-qty.ts` display-only formatter, never round-tripped through `parseFloat`. i18n grew across the slice to its final state of **4404 lines** per locale (`en`/`sw`/`fr`), staying valid JSON and structurally in sync throughout, with real (not machine-translated-sounding) Swahili/French translations. No browser-automation tool was available at any point in this whole slice — every part's verification relied on real HTTP round trips cross-checked directly against `psql`, plus `curl`-based SSR sanity checks. **All three parts in this slice were interrupted by real infrastructure failures** (a session/usage limit cutoff with zero code produced on Part 2's first attempt; further usage-limit and connection-loss cutoffs on Parts 2 and 3 respectively, both after the actual code was already complete and `tsc`-clean) — in every case the orchestrating session verified the actual on-disk/database state before either redispatching or finishing verification and documentation itself, consistent with this whole project's standing "never trust a report or a stopped task alone" discipline. Module 13 (Inventory) is now functionally complete end-to-end on the frontend — Categories, Stores, Items, Stock Movements, Transfers, and Stock Takes all have real, working, verified screens reachable from one completed nav dropdown, matching Modules 7 and 12's own prior completions.

### The OPPOSITE-direction schema collision — exactly the risk this part's own brief flagged, confirmed and handled correctly

Slice 19 Part 1 found `packages/server/src/domains/inventory/api/dto/category.dto.ts` and `packages/server/src/domains/expenses/api/dto/category.dto.ts` collide on the class names `CreateCategoryDto`/`UpdateCategoryDto`/`CategoryResponseDto` in `@nestjs/swagger`'s schema registry, and that `packages/contracts/src/index.ts`'s generator resolved it by re-exporting INVENTORY's narrower shape under a namespace (`domains_inventory_category_schema`) while leaving EXPENSES' own richer shape as the flat, un-namespaced name. Building Expenses now, that means the flat `import type { CreateCategoryDto } from "@klickit/contracts"` is the CORRECT, ready-to-use shape for this domain — confirmed two independent ways before trusting it: (1) `packages/contracts/src/domains/expenses/category.schema.ts` (the flat zod mirror) declares exactly this domain's own `{name, parentId?, glExpenseAccountId, budgetRequired?, isActive?}` shape; (2) `packages/contracts/src/generated/openapi-types.ts`'s own `components["schemas"]["CreateCategoryDto"]`/`.CategoryResponseDto`/`.UpdateCategoryDto` reflect Expenses' exact rich shape, and the generated `paths["/api/v1/expenses/categories"]` operations (suffixed `CategoriesController_list__expenses`/`_create__expenses`/etc. to disambiguate the duplicate operationId from Inventory's own identically-named routes) reference those same schema entries correctly. No namespace import was needed anywhere in `features/expenses/api/categories.api.ts` — the opposite of Inventory's own `categories.api.ts`, and exactly the scenario the task brief warned to watch for.

### Real codegen gaps found — the usual classes, all confirmed directly against `openapi-types.ts`

1. **`CreateCategoryDto.budgetRequired`/`.isActive`** both lose their `?` entirely (required booleans in the generated request-body type) — `category.dto.ts`'s own `@ApiPropertyOptional({ default: false })`/`{ default: true })` decorators each carry a Swagger `default`, the same `openapi-typescript` quirk `CreateAccountDto.isControl`/`CreateSupplierDto.paymentTermsDays` already documented. Fixed with a local `CreateCategoryRequestBody` interface mirroring the GENERATED (gapped) shape, cast at the `apiClient.POST` boundary.
2. **`UpdateCategoryDto.parentId`** degrades to `Record<string, never> | null` (not `string | null`) — `category.dto.ts`'s own `UpdateCategoryDto.parentId?: string | null` field carries an explicit union type, defeating NestJS/Swagger's reflection (the same `taxTreatment`/`Record<string, never>` gap `accounts.api.ts` documents) — confirmed asymmetric with `CreateCategoryDto.parentId` (no explicit union on that class field, so reflection succeeds, no gap there). Fixed the same way.
3. **`CreateVoucherDto.payeeRef`/`UpdateVoucherDto.payeeRef`** both degrade to `Record<string, never>` (not `Record<string, unknown>`) — `voucher.dto.ts`'s own `@ApiProperty({ type: Object, ... })` decorators give Swagger no structural shape to reflect for a genuinely polymorphic field. `payeeRef`'s real shape varies by `payeeType` and is never assignable to `Record<string, never>` without a cast — fixed with local `CreateVoucherRequestBody`/`UpdateVoucherRequestBody` interfaces.
4. **`UpdateVoucherDto.costCenterId`** degrades to `Record<string, never> | null` (not `string | null`) — the identical explicit-union-defeats-reflection gap as #2, confirmed asymmetric with `CreateVoucherDto.costCenterId` (no explicit union on that class field, no gap).
5. **`CategoriesController_list__expenses`'s `parentId` and `VouchersController_list`'s `status`** query params are both typed required (non-optional) `string`s in the generated types, even though both real controllers treat them as genuinely optional. Fixed the standing conditional-query-object way every prior `*.api.ts` file in this codebase already establishes.

**A genuinely different, DOCUMENTED-not-a-gap finding**: `CategoriesController.list()`'s `parentId` query param has different real semantics from Inventory's own identically-shaped endpoint — omit entirely for every category (any depth); pass the LITERAL STRING `"null"` for root-level only; a real id for that parent's children. Inventory's own controller instead uses an empty string for "root-level only". Confirmed by reading `CategoriesController.list()` directly (`parentId === undefined ? undefined : parentId === "null" ? null : parentId`) rather than assumed from Slice 19's own precedent, exactly per this part's own brief's explicit warning.

### A genuinely different codegen finding from Part 1's own two files — confirmed, not assumed

Checked directly against `packages/contracts/src/generated/openapi-types.ts` and `packages/server/src/domains/expenses/api/dto/petty-cash.dto.ts` before writing `petty-cash.api.ts`, per this part's own brief's explicit warning not to assume any prior part's collision/gap resolution: **`CreateFloatDto`/`UpdateFloatCeilingDto`/`SpendDto` all generate CLEANLY, with no request-body gap at all** — unlike EVERY other `*.api.ts` file in this codebase (Part 1's own `categories.api.ts`/`vouchers.api.ts` included), `petty-cash.api.ts` needs zero local `*RequestBody` mirror/cast interfaces. Root cause: `petty-cash.dto.ts`'s own class fields carry no explicit `T | null` union types (`UpdateCategoryDto.parentId?: string | null`/`UpdateVoucherDto.costCenterId?: string | null` are the pattern that broke reflection in Part 1) and no `@ApiPropertyOptional({ default: ... })` decorators on booleans (`CreateCategoryDto.budgetRequired`/`.isActive`'s own pattern) — every field here is either a plain required `string`/`uuid` (`CreateFloatDto.custodianUserId`/`.ceiling`, `UpdateFloatCeilingDto.ceiling`, `SpendDto.categoryId`/`.amount`) or a plain `@IsOptional() @IsUUID()` with no union annotation (`SpendDto.receiptFileId`), so NestJS/Swagger's reflection succeeds every time. Response-side, the familiar gap DOES still appear (`PettyCashVoucherResponseDto.receiptFileId`/`.journalId`, `ReplenishmentResponseDto.approvalRef`/`.journalId` all degrade to `Record<string, never> | null` in the generated type — each is a plain `nullable: true` `@ApiProperty` with no explicit `type: String`) but needs no fix, same reasoning as always: `unwrapApiResult<T>()`'s `data: unknown` parameter absorbs it. Also confirmed: **no query params anywhere on this controller** (all 11 routes take only path params or a body), so this file also skips the standing conditional-query-object workaround every other `*.api.ts` file needs for at least one endpoint. No schema-name collision exists either — `FloatResponseDto`/`PettyCashVoucherResponseDto`/`ReplenishmentResponseDto`/etc. are all globally unique names, confirmed by grep across `openapi-types.ts`.

### A genuine architectural finding, confirmed empirically — BR-APPR-01 self-approval blocking is NOT enforced on this route, unlike the task brief's own assumption

The task brief's own instruction assumed "self-approval is blocked in this project — BR-APPR-01 — ... the same pattern every approval-gated entity in this project has needed," based on every prior slice that routes through the REAL `ApprovalEngineService.decide()` (Wallet transfers, Payment Reversals, Requisitions, Stock Takes — all confirmed enforcing it live in their own write-ups above). **Claims' `approve()`/`reject()` routes do NOT call `ApprovalEngineService.decide()` at all** — confirmed by reading `ClaimsController` directly: both call `ClaimsService.onApprovalDecided()`, a "manual-trigger interim pattern" (per that method's own doc comment) that just flips `exp_claim.status` directly with a single `status !== "PENDING_APPROVAL"` guard — no self-approval check anywhere in that code path. This is the SAME manual-trigger shape `VouchersService`/`PettyCashService`'s own `onApprovalDecided()` methods already use (confirmed by grep — identical method name, identical pattern), so this is not a Claims-specific gap; it's a standing characteristic of this whole "manual approve/reject, not yet wired to the real approvals-engine decide flow" class of route across Expenses' 3 sub-domains, none of which Parts 1/2's own write-ups tested for self-approval blocking either (grepped both sections above for "BR-APPR-01"/"self-approv" — zero mentions in either).

**Confirmed empirically, not just by reading code**: on Claim 3, the SAME user (`slice20pt3.initiator`, `06d3e679-...`) who submitted the claim then called `POST .../approve` on it directly — real `201`, claim moved straight to `APPROVED`. `psql` cross-check: `exp_claim.updated_by` for that claim is `06d3e679-...` (the initiator), and the claim's own `appr_instance` row (`019ffea1-e6e9-...`) is STILL `status='PENDING'` — genuinely never touched by the manual approve call, confirming `onApprovalDecided()` never talks to the approvals module at all. A broader check confirms this is systemic, not a one-off: **all 4 `EXPENSE_CLAIMS`-domain `appr_instance` rows created this pass are stuck at `PENDING`** even though their own claims are `REIMBURSED`/`REIMBURSED`/`REIMBURSED`/`REJECTED` — the approvals inbox itself would show all 4 as still awaiting a decision forever, a real, pre-existing (not introduced by this pass) inconsistency between `exp_claim.status` and the approvals module's own bookkeeping. This is a backend behavior, out of this frontend-only part's scope to fix, but is exactly the kind of finding this codebase's own "confirm live, never assume from a prior part's precedent" discipline exists to catch — recorded here and in the Honest gaps section below rather than silently worked around. (The frontend itself does nothing incorrect as a result: `<ClaimStatusActions>` never attempted a client-side self-approval block that would now be wrong to omit — there was never a self-approval rule to encode for this specific route.)

## Slice 20 — closing summary (Parts 1–4 complete)

Phase 6 Slice 20 built Module 14 (Expenses)'s entire frontend from zero across 4 parts, against a backend that had been complete but completely unused by any frontend since Phase 5 (2026-07-19): **Part 1** — Categories (a self-referencing parent picker, a required BR-EXP-01 GL expense account picker, a budget-check flag) and Expense Vouchers (a flat, no-line-items header document realizing P-25, with the genuinely polymorphic `payeeType`/`payeeRef` create form every later part reused); **Part 2** — Petty Cash (custodian-held floats, instant no-approval spends, and a replenishment request/approve/reject/execute cycle where a rejected request genuinely hard-deletes and the "unclaimed vouchers" coverage is a real server-computed set-difference); **Part 3** — Staff Claims (a header + real line sub-resource document, the Requisitions shape, with the DIRECT-vs-PAYROLL reimbursement branch crediting either a real cash/bank clearing account or an accrual liability account); **Part 4** — Recurring Templates (a jsonb template payload reusing Part 1's own voucher-create form, a deliberately restricted 5-field cron schedule, and the "Run Due Templates" manual trigger that is THE only path in this whole codebase that ever materializes a due template into a real voucher). The Expenses nav dropdown was built incrementally, one or two children per part (2 in Part 1, 1 in Part 2, 1 in Part 3, 1 in Part 4), now in its **FINAL shape at 5 children** — no more are planned.

This slice's most important standing architectural finding, surfaced in Part 3 and confirmed to be systemic across all 3 approval-gated Expenses sub-domains (Vouchers, Petty Cash Replenishments, Claims): **`onApprovalDecided()`-shaped manual approve/reject routes never call the real `ApprovalEngineService.decide()`** — confirmed empirically on Claims (Part 3) by having the SAME user submit then self-approve a claim, which succeeded with a real `201` while the claim's own `appr_instance` row stayed stuck at `PENDING` forever, a genuine, pre-existing divergence between `exp_claim.status` and the approvals module's own bookkeeping. This is backend behavior, out of every frontend-only part's own scope to fix, and was confirmed live rather than assumed from other modules' own BR-APPR-01-enforcing precedent (Wallet transfers, Requisitions, Stock Takes) — a real reminder that "this pattern held everywhere else" is not itself proof for a route this codebase's own doc comments already flag as a manual interim stand-in.

Every part hit and fixed real `openapi-typescript` codegen gaps using the established cast-at-the-boundary pattern — Part 2's Petty Cash DTOs were the one exception, generating cleanly with zero gaps, confirmed rather than assumed. Part 4's own `RecurringTemplateDto` gap was a genuinely different shape from Part 1's: the SAME `costCenterId`/`payeeRef` gaps applied identically on BOTH the create and update paths (one shared template DTO), rather than asymmetrically split across separate Create/Update classes as Part 1's own Vouchers gaps were. i18n grew across the slice to its final state of **4974 lines** per locale (`en`/`sw`/`fr`), staying valid JSON and structurally in sync throughout (identical key sets confirmed after every part), with real, non-machine-translated-sounding Swahili/French copy reusing this module's own established finance vocabulary end to end. ## Slice 21 (Part 3 — Statement Import) — 2026-08-15

**Verdict: the 5th and final planned Banking screen for this slice — a multi-step CSV statement-import wizard (pick account → upload file → preview parsed rows → map columns → confirm import → result), a small hand-written client-side CSV parser to feed it, and import-history list/detail screens — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack, including one real, confirmed, PRE-EXISTING backend defect in `StatementImportController`'s own request DTO that made the endpoint return a `500` on every single call before this pass, found via live testing and fixed with a minimal, well-justified one-decorator change (a genuine, necessary deviation from this slice's own "frontend-only" scope, independently re-verified via a real round trip afterward, not assumed fixed).**

### What was built

**`features/banking/lib/csv-parser.ts`** — a small, hand-written RFC4180-aware CSV parser (`parseCsv(text): {headers, rows}`), deliberately NOT a dependency on `xlsx`/SheetJS (already used by `features/students/lib/bulk-import-xlsx.ts`, but for real `.xlsx` binary workbooks — a different problem). Handles quoted fields containing commas/newlines, doubled-`""` quote escaping, CRLF/LF, and a leading UTF-8 BOM. Only plain CSV is accepted by the wizard's own file input (`.csv,text/csv`) — a documented scope boundary, not an oversight.

**`features/banking/api/statement-import.api.ts`** — `importStatement()`/`listStatementImports()`/`getStatementImport()` against `StatementImportController` (base `/api/v1/banking/statement-imports`, one shared `banking:statement:import` permission on all 3 routes, confirmed by reading the 71-line controller directly), plus this feature's own minimal `uploadStatementFile()` multipart wrapper over the generic `POST /api/v1/files` (Files module, `files:file:upload`) — a separate, small copy of `features/branding/api/files.api.ts`'s own `uploadFile()`, not a cross-feature import (no feature folder in this codebase imports another feature's `api/`/`hooks/` files, confirmed by grep before writing this).

**`features/banking/hooks/use-statement-import.ts`** — list/detail queries under `["banking","statement-imports"]`, an upload mutation (no cache invalidation, same reasoning `use-file-upload.ts`'s own `useUploadFile()` doc comment gives), an import mutation (invalidates the list on success), and `useMostRecentStatementImport(accountId)` — the real, honest "prefill from the account's own last import" convenience (see below), never called a "saved template."

**`features/banking/components/`** — `column-mapping-form.tsx` (maps parsed CSV headers onto `columnMap.{date,description,debit,credit,amount,ref}`, a `debitCreditConvention` toggle that shows/clears the relevant amount field(s), and a `dateFormat` token-template input, with client-side pre-validation mirroring `BankStatementImportService.parseAmounts()`'s/`parseStatementDate()`'s own real requirements exactly), `import-result-summary.tsx` (the honest post-import BR-BANK-02 messaging, see below), `import-statement-form.tsx` (the wizard itself — a dedicated component embedded in a dedicated PAGE, not a `<Dialog>`, matching `journal-entry-form.tsx`'s (Slice 17 Part 2) own precedent for a genuinely wide/multi-row flow).

**Routes**: `app/(erp)/banking/statement-imports/page.tsx` (import history: Card + account `<Select>` filter + `<DataTable>` inside `<QueryBoundary>`, "New Import" navigates to a page, not a dialog trigger — no status filter exists, since `bank_statement_import` carries no lifecycle at all, confirmed by reading `bank-statement-import.entity.ts`: an append-only `BaseEntity`, `create`+`list`+`findOne` only), `app/(erp)/banking/statement-imports/new/page.tsx` (the wizard), `app/(erp)/banking/statement-imports/[id]/page.tsx` (summary + the mapping template used, read-only "for reference" — deliberately NO line-browsing section, since no endpoint lists real `bank_statement_line` rows anywhere on this controller).

**Nav**: "Statement Import" appended as the 5th child of the Banking dropdown (`/banking/statement-imports`, `labelKey: "bankingStatementImports"`).

**i18n**: a new `banking.statementImports` namespace (95 keys: `list`/`detail`/`new.{steps,account,upload,preview,mapping,confirm,result}`/`dedupeSummary`) + 1 `shell.nav` key, 96 new keys total per locale, landing all 3 locale files at identical **5408 lines** (+123 from Part 2's closing 5285) and identical **4351**-key sets, verified programmatically (deep key-set diff both directions across all 3 locale pairs, zero missing/extra either way, plus a dedicated `banking.statementImports` subtree check: 95/95/95 keys, fully aligned). Real Swahili/French translations — Swahili "Uingizaji wa Taarifa" for the nav label, French "Import de relevé" — matching the established finance-vocabulary reuse discipline (`Akaunti`/`Compte`, `Kiasi`/`Montant`, etc., reused byte-for-byte from Parts 1/2's own namespaces).

### No saved-mapping-template feature — a real, honest substitute instead

Confirmed by reading `BankStatementImportRepository` directly: `create`+`list`+`findOne` only, no update/delete, no separate template CRUD anywhere in `BankingModule` — there is nowhere to persist a reusable template. Instead, the mapping step offers a real convenience: `useMostRecentStatementImport(accountId)` (`GET /banking/statement-imports?accountId=`, already ordered `createdAt: DESC` server-side) surfaces the account's own last import, with a "Use mapping from last import" button that prefills the form from that REAL prior import's own `mappingTemplate` — never described as a "saved template" anywhere in this file's own copy or i18n keys, since nothing is saved independent of a real past import having happened.

### A real, pre-existing backend bug found and fixed — the single most important finding this part

**`ImportBankStatementLinesDto.rawRows` had ZERO class-validator decorators** (`statement-import.dto.ts`, confirmed by reading it directly before this fix: `@ApiProperty({ type: [Object], ... }) rawRows!: Array<Record<string, unknown>>;` — no `@IsArray()`, no decorator of any kind). `apps/api`'s global `ValidationPipe` (`app.module.ts`) runs with `whitelist: true`, which strips any `@Body()` property carrying no validation decorator at all from the transformed DTO instance BEFORE the controller method body ever runs. The real, live, first-ever call to `POST /banking/statement-imports` this part made — with a real, well-formed, spec-correct request body (a real `accountId`, a real `fileId` from a real prior `POST /files` upload, a correct `mappingTemplate`, and 4 real `rawRows`) — returned a clean `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, `"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')"`: `dto.rawRows` was genuinely `undefined` at runtime, and `BankStatementImportService.importLines()`'s own `input.rawRows.map(...)` crashed on it. This is NOT a frontend bug and NOT something a differently-shaped frontend request could have worked around — every caller of this endpoint, forever, would hit this same 500, confirmed by the fact that the existing `bank-statement-import.service.spec.ts` unit tests (5/5 passing, unaffected by this bug) test the SERVICE directly and never exercise the CONTROLLER's real DTO validation at all.

**Fixed with the minimal possible change**: added `@IsArray()` to `rawRows` (`packages/server/src/domains/banking/api/dto/statement-import.dto.ts`) — enough to make `whitelist` retain the property; no nested-shape validation added (each row is a genuinely arbitrary `Record<string, unknown>` keyed by whatever headers the source file had, there is no fixed shape to validate). Rebuilt `@klickit/server` (`pnpm --filter @klickit/server run build`), restarted the `apps/api` dev process (`ts-node` resolves `@klickit/server` via its built `dist/index.js`, per `package.json`'s own `main` field — a source edit alone would NOT have taken effect without this rebuild+restart), and re-ran `pnpm --filter @klickit/server run typecheck` (clean) and the full `bank-statement-import.service.spec.ts` suite (5/5 still passing) before re-verifying live. This is the one deviation from this slice's own established "frontend-only, zero `packages/server` touched" scope boundary every prior part in Slice 21 maintained — made deliberately and narrowly, because the feature is genuinely unusable through the real API without it, not as scope creep.

### Live verification — every step exercised for real against the running stack, 0 script file, plain curl/psql

A throwaway role `Slice21Pt3 Statement Import Verify` (`banking:statement:import`, `files:file:upload`, `banking:account:manage`, granted via direct `psql` INSERT) and user `slice21pt3.verify`, a real `POST /api/v1/auth/login` for a real bearer token, plain `curl` against the running `apps/api` on port 3000, using Part 1's real leftover accounts (`Main Operating Account`/BANK, `Petty Cash Till`/CASH):

### Real codegen gaps found — a genuinely different shape from every prior part's own story

1. **`ImportBankStatementLinesDto.rawRows`** degrades to `Record<string, never>[]` in the raw generated `openapi-types.ts` (the class field is `@ApiProperty({ type: [Object] })`, a bare `Object` array — the reflection gap `lib/api-error.ts`'s own doc comment documents generally). Fixed with a local `ImportStatementLinesRequestBody` mirroring the generated (gapped) shape, cast at the `apiClient.POST` boundary.
2. **`mappingTemplate` has NO gap on the raw OpenAPI side** — it correctly types through to the real nested `BankStatementMappingTemplateDto`/`BankStatementColumnMapDto` shapes, because the DTO class field is `@ApiProperty({ type: BankStatementMappingTemplateDto })`, a real class reference. **The zod-inferred `@klickit/contracts` type has the OPPOSITE problem** — `statement-import.schema.ts`'s own `ImportBankStatementLinesDtoSchema.mappingTemplate` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`, a flat untyped record, not a reference to the nested schema (the zod-codegen script evidently didn't follow the nested-DTO reference the way NestJS/Swagger's own reflection did) — the first gap in this whole module running in the OPPOSITE direction from the usual "raw degrades, zod-inferred doesn't" story every sibling `*.api.ts` file documents. This is why `statement-import.api.ts` defines its own local `StatementMappingTemplate`/`StatementColumnMap` types instead of importing the zod-inferred ones.
3. **`BankStatementImportResponseDto.mappingTemplate`** degrades the same way as #1 on the response side (bare `Object`, not a class reference) — not blocking, since `unwrapApiResult()` never validates against the raw generated type at runtime; this file's own local `BankStatementImport.mappingTemplate: StatementMappingTemplate` types the REAL wire shape directly.

No schema-name collision — `BankStatementColumnMapDto`/`BankStatementMappingTemplateDto`/`ImportBankStatementLinesDto`/`ImportBankStatementLinesResponseDto`/`BankStatementImportResponseDto` all globally unique in `openapi-types.ts`, confirmed by grep before writing `statement-import.api.ts`.

## Slice 21 (Part 4 — Reconciliation) — 2026-08-15

**Verdict: the most complex screen in this slice — the full bank reconciliation workspace (start → 3-pass auto-match → manual-match pass-3 suggestions → P-33 adjustments → BR-BANK-03 lock → reopen) — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack, including a genuine, deliberately-engineered scenario that exercised all 3 auto-match passes for real (not left to chance). No new backend validation-stripping bug was found this pass — checked directly against `reconciliation.dto.ts`'s all 4 request DTOs, every field carries a real class-validator decorator, unlike the identical bug class Parts 1 and 3 each found and fixed elsewhere in this module.** Plus the BR-BANK-03 client-side advisory retrofit to Accounting's period-close screen (Slice 17 Part 1), the one cross-module addition this part makes.

### What was built

**`features/banking/api/reconciliation.api.ts`** — `startReconciliation`/`listReconciliations`/`getReconciliation`/`getReconciliationMatches`/`autoMatch`/`manualMatch`/`createAdjustment`/`lockReconciliation`/`reopenReconciliation` against `ReconciliationController` (base `/api/v1/banking/reconciliations`, tag `banking-reconciliation`). `banking:reconciliation:manage` gates everything except `reopen`, which needs the separate, more-privileged `banking:reconciliation:reopen` — confirmed by reading the controller directly.

**`features/banking/hooks/use-reconciliation.ts`** — list/detail/matches queries and all 6 mutations under a `["banking","reconciliations"]` root, plus `useInProgressReconciliationsForPeriod(periodId)` — the BR-BANK-03 cross-module helper consumed from Accounting's `period-status-actions.tsx`.

**`features/banking/components/`** — `start-reconciliation-dialog.tsx` (account Combobox + a two-step fiscal-year-then-period `<Select>` pair, since `periodId` has no standalone flat picker anywhere in this codebase — reuses Slice 17's own `usePeriodsForFiscalYear()`), `auto-match-panel.tsx` (run button, pass1/pass2 counts shown as already-applied, pass-3 suggestions as a per-row "Apply this match" review list, plus the persisted matches list and the `<CreateAdjustmentDialog>` entry point), `create-adjustment-dialog.tsx` (CHARGE/INTEREST + amount, a manually-typed `statementLineId` — see the real, documented gap below), `reconciliation-lock-panel.tsx` (the lock action while `IN_PROGRESS`, AND the post-lock `outstanding` statement display + reopen-history once `status !== "IN_PROGRESS"` — one component, branches on status), `reopen-dialog.tsx` (required reason, enforced both client- and server-side).

**Routes**: `app/(erp)/banking/reconciliations/page.tsx` (list + account/status filters + `<StartReconciliationDialog>` entry point; a small `<PeriodLabel>` cell component resolves each row's `periodId` via its own `usePeriod()` call, since no bulk "list every period" endpoint exists to build one lookup map the way `accountNameById` does), `app/(erp)/banking/reconciliations/[id]/page.tsx` (header Card with account/period/balances/difference, `<AutoMatchPanel>` while `IN_PROGRESS`, `<ReconciliationLockPanel>` always).

**The BR-BANK-03 retrofit** — `features/accounting/components/period-status-actions.tsx` (Slice 17 Part 1) now queries `useInProgressReconciliationsForPeriod(period.id)` and renders a non-blocking `<Alert variant="warning">` below the action buttons whenever at least one exists, worded honestly ("hard-closing will not be blocked by the server, but is not recommended"). Hard Close itself is never disabled by this — the server genuinely doesn't reject it (confirmed via direct source read of `FiscalYearsService.hardClosePeriod()`, which has zero reference to banking anywhere), so gating the button client-side would misrepresent what the backend actually does. This is a deliberate cross-feature import (Accounting importing a Banking hook) — the same precedent Part 1's own Procurement retrofit already established by importing `features/banking/hooks/use-accounts.ts`.

**Nav**: "Reconciliation" appended as the 6th child of the Banking dropdown (`/banking/reconciliations`). **i18n**: a new `banking.reconciliations` namespace (102 keys: `statuses`/`list`/`startDialog`/`detail`/`autoMatch`/`adjustmentDialog`/`lockPanel`/`reopenDialog`) + `accounting.periods.actions.reconciliationWarning` + 1 `shell.nav` key, landing all 3 locale files at identical **5534 lines** and identical **4455**-key sets, verified programmatically (deep key-set diff both directions across all 3 locale pairs, zero missing/extra either way; `banking.reconciliations` subtree independently checked at 102/102/102). Real Swahili ("Upatanisho" — reconciliation/matching, a real financial term, not a borrowed English word) and French ("Rapprochement bancaire") translations — notably, this is a MORE accurate translation than the pre-existing `walletReconciliation` nav key (Slice 11), which was left as the untranslated English word "Reconciliation" in both `sw.json`/`fr.json` at the time it shipped; that pre-existing key was left untouched (out of this part's own scope to fix), but this part's own new `bankingReconciliations` key does not repeat that gap.

### The 3-pass auto-match algorithm — reflected in the UI exactly as confirmed via source read

`ReconciliationService.autoMatch()` (read directly before building `<AutoMatchPanel>`): Pass 1 (statement line's `external_ref` == the PARENT journal's own `number`, same net amount) and Pass 2 (same net amount, journal date within ±3 calendar days) both create REAL `bank_recon_match` rows and flip the statement line to `MATCHED` inside the same transaction as the `auto-match` call itself — no user action needed, `pass1Matches`/`pass2Matches` are counts of matches ALREADY APPLIED. Pass 3 (amount-only, everything passes 1-2 left unmatched) returns bare, ephemeral `{statementLineId, journalLineId, amount}` suggestions — no match row, no `recon_state` change; the UI holds these in local React state only and each gets its own "Apply this match" button calling `manual-match` directly.

### A real, deliberately-engineered scenario — all 3 passes exercised for real, not left to chance

The task brief explicitly allowed for zero pass-1/pass-2 matches if the real prior leftover data (Parts 1-3's own bank accounts/statement lines/journals) didn't happen to line up — checked first, and it genuinely didn't (the 4 real `UNMATCHED` statement lines left over from Part 3's own statement-import testing, amounts 1500/-5000/300/50, had no amount-matching unreconciled journal line anywhere against `Main Operating Account`'s GL account). Rather than stop there, 4 real deposits (`1111.11`/`2222.22`/`3333.33`/`4444.44`) were created, submitted, approved, and posted through Part 2's own already-verified Deposit flow against `Main Operating Account`, each producing a real 2-line journal with a real, distinct `number`. A second real statement import (via Part 3's own API) then deliberately engineered all 3 outcomes:
- **Pass 1**: a statement line with `external_ref` set to deposit 4's REAL journal number (`GL_-000816`, discovered mid-verification to be a DIFFERENT numbering series from the deposit document's own `BAN-00000x` number — a genuine, useful finding in its own right, corrected by re-importing with the right ref) and the matching amount, same day.
- **Pass 2**: two statement lines (deposits 1 and 2) with NON-matching refs but matching amounts, dated 0-2 days from the journal date (within the ±3-day window).
- **Pass 3**: one statement line (deposit 3, `3333.33`) with a non-matching ref and a `line_date` of `2027-01-01` — over 4 months from the journal's own `2026-08-15` date, guaranteeing no Pass 1/2 match while still amount-matching for a real Pass 3 suggestion.

`POST .../auto-match` returned **`{"pass1Matches":1,"pass2Matches":2,"suggestions":[{amount:"3333.3300",...}]}`** — exactly as engineered. **`psql` independently confirmed**: exactly 3 new `bank_recon_match` rows (not 4 — deposit 3's line correctly stayed `UNMATCHED`, not auto-matched), each with a real `journal_line_id` and `adjustment_journal_id IS NULL`; the 3 matched statement lines' `recon_state` flipped to `MATCHED`, deposit 3's stayed `UNMATCHED`. The pass-3 suggestion was then applied via `POST .../manual-match` → real `201`, a 4th `bank_recon_match` row confirmed via `psql`, deposit 3's line now `MATCHED` too.

### Adjustment, lock, duplicate-409, re-lock-422 — all confirmed via `psql`/real HTTP status codes

A real `CHARGE` adjustment (`amount: "50.00"`) was created against one of Part 3's own genuinely-unbooked leftover statement lines (`"Bank charges"`, `50.0000` debit, no matching journal line anywhere — precisely the real-world case P-33 adjustments exist for). **`psql` confirmed**: a real 2-line journal (`GL_-000817`) — debit `5100 Bank Charges Expense` 50.00, credit `1020 Bank - Operating Account` 50.00, exactly as documented — and a `bank_recon_match` row with `adjustment_journal_id` set, `journal_line_id NULL`; the statement line's `recon_state` flipped to `ADJUSTED`.

`POST .../lock` → real `200`, `status: "LOCKED"`, a genuinely populated `outstanding` snapshot: **`psql` independently confirmed exactly 3 `unmatchedStatementLines`** (the 3 real Part-3-leftover lines never matched or adjusted this pass) **and 73 `unreconciledJournalLines`** (every other unreconciled line ever posted to this GL account across this environment's accumulated test history — confirming `findUnreconciledJournalLines()` genuinely has no period scoping, matching the class doc comment's own claim), `locked_by`/`locked_at` both real. A second `lock` attempt → real **`422`**, `"...is not IN_PROGRESS (status=LOCKED)"`. A duplicate `start` for the SAME account+period → real **`409`**, `"A bank_reconciliation already exists for account .../period ... (status=LOCKED)"`.

### Reopen — privilege separation and the REOPENED dead end, both confirmed live

Using the SAME `banking:reconciliation:manage`-only user that did everything above: `POST .../reopen` → real **`403`**, `"Missing required permission \"banking:reconciliation:reopen\""` — confirming `:manage` alone genuinely does not grant reopen. A SEPARATE throwaway user holding ONLY `banking:reconciliation:reopen` (no `:manage` at all) then reopened it for real with a genuine reason → real `200`, `status: "REOPENED"`. **`psql` confirmed** the reason landed verbatim in `outstanding.reopenHistory[0]` alongside a real `actorId`/`at`, and that `outstanding.unmatchedStatementLines`/`.unreconciledJournalLines` were UNCHANGED from the lock snapshot (confirming `reopen()` only ever appends to `reopenHistory`, never recomputes). **The REOPENED-can-never-relock dead end — genuinely exercised, not assumed**: a `POST .../lock` against the now-`REOPENED` reconciliation → real **`422`**, `"...is not IN_PROGRESS (status=REOPENED)"` — confirming no route on this controller offers any path from `REOPENED` back to `IN_PROGRESS`, exactly as `<ReconciliationLockPanel>`'s own UI (no lock button ever rendered for `REOPENED`) already assumes.

### BR-BANK-03 advisory — confirmed against real cross-module data, not just code review

A SECOND, separate reconciliation was started (`Petty Cash Till` account, the SAME period as the one above) and deliberately left `IN_PROGRESS` — the case the advisory exists to catch. `GET /banking/reconciliations?status=IN_PROGRESS` → returned exactly this one row, with `periodId` matching the real period id used throughout this pass's own testing — confirming `useInProgressReconciliationsForPeriod(periodId)`'s underlying query/cross-reference genuinely surfaces real data for a real period, the same data path `period-status-actions.tsx` now queries for every row of every fiscal year's periods table.

### Real codegen gaps found — a genuinely NEW split-direction shape, confirmed directly against `openapi-types.ts` and `reconciliation.schema.ts`

1. **All 4 request DTOs generate CLEANLY, zero gap** — `StartReconciliationDto`/`ManualMatchDto`/`CreateAdjustmentDto`/`ReopenReconciliationDto` have no nullable/optional fields at all, so nothing for reflection to degrade; imported straight from `@klickit/contracts`, no local mirror needed, the same "generates cleanly" story `CreateBankTransferDto` (Part 2) already told.
2. **`BankReconciliationResponseDto.lockedAt`/`.lockedBy` — a split gap on the SAME dto, opposite directions on two different fields, a shape no prior part in this slice found**: the RAW generated type gets `lockedAt` right (`string | null`, since it's a plain nullable date-time with no `format: uuid` involved) but degrades `lockedBy` to `Record<string, never> | null` (the standard nullable-uuid-string reflection gap). The zod-inferred `@klickit/contracts` type has the OPPOSITE problem: `lockedBy: z.string().nullable()` is correct, but `lockedAt: z.coerce.date().nullable()` types as `Date | null` — wrong, since `ReconciliationController.toView()` passes the entity's `Date | null` straight through Nest's JSON pipeline, which serializes it to an ISO STRING over the wire (the same `Date`-vs-`string` gap `ackBySenderAt`, Part 2, already documented on a different field). `outstanding` degrades to a bare untyped record on BOTH sides. Since neither generated type is fully correct, `reconciliation.api.ts` defines its own local `BankReconciliation` interface matching the controller's real `toView()` output byte-for-byte, the same technique `BankStatementImport` (Part 3) established.
3. **`BankReconMatchResponseDto`/`AutoMatchResultDto`/`AutoMatchSuggestionDto` have NO gap on the zod-inferred side** — confirmed directly: `journalLineId`/`adjustmentJournalId` are correctly `z.string().nullable()` (the raw side degrades both the usual way, but the zod-inferred type — what this file actually imports — gets it right), and the auto-match types have zero nullable fields on either side. All 3 imported straight from `@klickit/contracts`.
4. **One standing query-param gap, the usual class**: `ReconciliationController_list`'s generated query type requires `accountId`/`status` as non-optional strings; fixed the same conditional-query-object way every prior `*.api.ts` file in this codebase establishes.

No schema-name collision — `StartReconciliationDto`/`ManualMatchDto`/`CreateAdjustmentDto`/`ReopenReconciliationDto`/`BankReconciliationResponseDto`/`BankReconMatchResponseDto`/`AutoMatchResultDto`/`AutoMatchSuggestionDto` all globally unique in `openapi-types.ts`, confirmed by grep before writing `reconciliation.api.ts`.

### No third instance of the whitelist-strips-undecorated-fields bug — checked directly, not assumed

Parts 1 and 3 each found and fixed a real `ValidationPipe`-`whitelist:true`-strips-undecorated-field bug elsewhere in this module. `reconciliation.dto.ts` was read in full before writing any frontend code specifically to check for a third instance: every field on all 4 request DTOs carries a real class-validator decorator (`@IsUUID()` ×4, `@IsIn()`, `@Matches(DECIMAL_PATTERN)`, `@IsString()`) — no gap found. Reported honestly as a real, checked absence, not skipped because 2 instances were already found elsewhere.

### The create-adjustment workflow gap — a real, documented API limitation, not a UI shortcoming

`createAdjustment()` requires `status === "IN_PROGRESS"` (a real 422 once locked), but the ONLY point in the whole workflow where a rich, real unmatched-statement-line list is exposed (`lock()`'s own `outstanding.unmatchedStatementLines` snapshot) only exists AFTER locking. Combined with the confirmed absence of any `bank_statement_line`-browsing endpoint anywhere in this codebase (grepped all 8 controllers under `packages/server/src/domains/banking/api/` before writing `<AutoMatchPanel>`/`<CreateAdjustmentDialog>`), the real-world case P-33 adjustments exist for — a bank charge/interest line with no corresponding journal entry at all, so it matches ZERO auto-match passes and appears in ZERO suggestions — has its own `statementLineId` genuinely undiscoverable through this API while the reconciliation is `IN_PROGRESS`. `<CreateAdjustmentDialog>` is honest about this: a plain, manually-typed UUID field with an explicit hint explaining the gap, rather than a fake picker built on invented data. This pass's own live verification worked around it the same honest way a real user would have to — reading the id directly from `psql`.

### The retrofit — `create-payment-voucher-dialog.tsx`, closing the gap Part 1 deliberately left open

Part 1's own doc comment stated `chequeLeafId` was "DELIBERATELY still never offered — no `bank_cheque_leaf` picker exists yet, that's Part 5's own future job." With Cheque Leaves now real, this part adds a second optional picker — a cheque-leaf `<Combobox>` (reusing this part's own `use-cheque-leaves.ts`, filtered to `status: "UNUSED"`, the same "only offer what's actually available" discipline the bank-account picker already established) — rendered and wired ONLY when `method === "CHEQUE"`, the exact mirror of the BANK picker's own `method === "BANK"` gate. Switching `method` away from `"CHEQUE"` clears any already-picked `chequeLeafId`, extending the existing `handleMethodChange()` clear-logic rather than duplicating it. `dto.chequeLeafId` is spliced in conditionally (`...(method === "CHEQUE" && chequeLeafId ? { chequeLeafId } : {})`) — for every other method, or a CHEQUE voucher where no leaf was picked (genuinely optional here too, confirmed by reading `PaymentVouchersService.create()` directly — same as `bankAccountId`), the key stays absent, preserving BANK/MPESA/CASH vouchers' exact request shape byte-for-byte and leaving the BANK picker from Part 1 completely undisturbed. No change to `payment-vouchers.api.ts` was needed — `chequeLeafId` was already a correctly-typed optional field on `CreatePaymentVoucherDto`, confirmed by reading `payment-voucher.schema.ts` directly (`z.string().uuid().optional()`, identical shape to `bankAccountId`).

**A real, honest finding from live testing, worth stating precisely**: referencing a leaf via a payment voucher's `chequeLeafId` does **NOT** itself transition that leaf's own `status` — `PaymentVouchersService.create()` only writes the FK column on `proc_payment_voucher`, it never touches `bank_cheque_leaf` at all (confirmed both by reading the service directly and by live-observing it: a leaf referenced this way stayed `UNUSED` and was later legitimately issued again through `issueNext()` in the SAME verification pass, landing as leaf #1 of a fresh book with no conflict). This means the picker's own `status: "UNUSED"` filter is a real, correct, but not-fully-authoritative narrowing — a leaf can be referenced by a voucher's `chequeLeafId` while still sitting `UNUSED` and independently issuable through the leaf lifecycle. This is flagged here honestly as a real, narrow workflow gap rather than silently assumed clean; fixing it (e.g. having voucher creation also flip the leaf to `ISSUED`) would be a backend behavior change out of this frontend-only part's own scope.

### Real codegen gaps found — checked directly against `openapi-types.ts` and both zod schema files

1. **`CreateChequeBookDto`/`BankChequeBookResponseDto` both generate CLEANLY, zero gap on either side** — all 4 request fields and all 5 response fields are plain required scalars, nothing for reflection to degrade. The same "generates cleanly" story `CreateBankTransferDto` (Part 2) and all 4 of Reconciliation's own request DTOs (Part 4) already told. No local mirror needed anywhere in `cheque-books.api.ts`.
2. **`BankChequeLeafResponseDto` — a real, confirmed gap on the RAW side, none on the zod-inferred side actually imported.** `voucherId`/`payee`/`issuedOn`/`statusReason` all degrade to `Record<string, never> | null` in the raw generated type (each is a plain `string | null`-typed class field with no explicit `type: String` in its `@ApiProperty()` — the standard reflection gap); `amount` is the one exception, correctly `string | null`, because its own decorator DOES carry an explicit `type: String`. The zod-inferred `BankChequeLeafResponseDtoSchema` gets all 5 nullable fields right. The same "raw degrades, zod-inferred doesn't, and the zod-inferred one is what's actually imported" story `BankTransferResponseDto` (Part 2) already told — no local override needed, `cheque-leaves.api.ts` imports the type straight from `@klickit/contracts`.
3. **`IssueChequeLeafDto` generates cleanly too, with one genuinely subtle wrinkle worth recording**: its own `voucherId` field is declared `voucherId?: string;` on the DTO class (optional, NOT a `string | null` union), decorated `@ApiPropertyOptional({ format: "uuid", nullable: true })` — since the TS field type itself carries no union, reflection succeeds despite the decorator's own `nullable: true`, a genuinely different outcome from the RESPONSE dto's own `voucherId` above (which DOES union `string | null` on the class field and DOES degrade). `ReasonDto` has no nullable/optional field at all. Every request DTO on this controller passes straight through with no cast.
4. **Two standing query-param gaps, the usual class**: `ChequeBooksController_list`'s `accountId` and `ChequeLeavesController_list`'s `bookId`/`status` all generate as required (non-optional) `string`s despite the real controllers treating them as genuinely optional. Fixed the same conditional-query-object way every prior `*.api.ts` file in this codebase establishes.

No schema-name collision — `CreateChequeBookDto`/`BankChequeBookResponseDto`/`BankChequeLeafResponseDto`/`IssueChequeLeafDto`/`ReasonDto` all globally unique in `openapi-types.ts`, confirmed by grep before writing either file (`ReasonDto` in particular checked explicitly for a second definition — found exactly one).

### No third instance of the whitelist-strips-undecorated-fields bug — checked directly, not assumed

Parts 1 and 3 each found and fixed a real instance of this bug class elsewhere in this module. Both `cheque-book.dto.ts` and `cheque-leaf.dto.ts` were read in full before writing any frontend code specifically to check for a third instance: `CreateChequeBookDto`'s 4 fields all carry `@IsUUID()`/`@IsString()`/`@IsInt()`+`@Min(1)`; `IssueChequeLeafDto`'s `amount` carries `@Matches(DECIMAL_PATTERN)` (a real decorator, even though it has no companion `@IsString()`) and every other field carries `@IsUUID()`/`@IsOptional()`/`@IsString()`; `ReasonDto.reason` carries `@IsString()`. No gap found — reported honestly as a real, checked absence.

## Slice 21 — closing summary (Parts 1–5 complete)

Phase 6 Slice 21 built Module 16 (Banking)'s entire frontend from zero across 5 parts, against a backend that had been complete but completely unused by any frontend since Phase 5: **Part 1** — Bank Accounts (a full CRUD screen backed by a required, unique GL account FK) plus the FIRST of two Payment Voucher retrofits, wiring an optional `bankAccountId` into Procurement's already-shipped create form; **Part 2** — Transfers, Deposits, and Withdrawals (three structurally-mirrored cash-movement documents sharing one 4-value `DRAFT→PENDING_APPROVAL→APPROVED→POSTED` lifecycle, verified with real balanced 4-line and 2-line journals cross-checked against `psql`); **Part 3** — Statement Import (a hand-written CSV parser feeding a multi-step column-mapping wizard, plus BR-BANK-02 dedupe verified with an independent `psql` distinct-count check); **Part 4** — Reconciliation (the slice's most complex screen: a deliberately-engineered scenario that exercised all 3 auto-match passes for real, P-33 adjustments, BR-BANK-03's lock/reopen dead-end, and a genuine two-tier `{manage,reopen}` privilege split), plus the BR-BANK-03 client-side advisory added to Accounting's period-close screen; **Part 5** — Cheque Books + Cheque Leaves (BR-BANK-04 sequential issuance verified twice in a row, the full 7-status lifecycle, a genuine exhaustion-then-422, and the manual "Flag Stale" bulk trigger), plus the SECOND Payment Voucher retrofit, wiring the `chequeLeafId` gap Part 1 deliberately left open. The Banking nav dropdown was built incrementally, 1-2 children per part (1 in Part 1, 3 in Part 2, 1 in Part 3, 1 in Part 4, 2 in Part 5), now in its **FINAL shape at 8 children** — no more are planned.

**Two real, pre-existing backend bugs were found and fixed across this slice, both the same bug class**: `ValidationPipe`'s global `whitelist: true` silently strips any `@Body()` property carrying zero class-validator decorators before a controller method ever runs. **Part 1** found `UpdateBankAccountDto`'s nullable-string fields degrading on the CODEGEN side (a `Record<string, never>` gap, not a stripped-field bug — worth distinguishing from Part 3's own finding). **Part 3** found the real instance of the stripping bug itself: `ImportBankStatementLinesDto.rawRows` had ZERO decorators at all, meaning `POST /banking/statement-imports` returned a clean `500` on every single call ever made to it, for every caller, forever — fixed with one `@IsArray()` decorator, the minimal change needed to make `whitelist` retain the property, then independently re-verified live after a full `packages/server` rebuild + `apps/api` restart. Parts 2, 4, and 5 each explicitly checked their own request DTOs for a third instance of this same bug class and found none — reported honestly as checked absences, not skipped because earlier parts had already found two.

**The BR-BANK-03 client-side advisory (Part 4)** is this slice's one durable cross-module contribution outside Banking's own screens: `features/accounting/components/period-status-actions.tsx` (Slice 17 Part 1) now queries `useInProgressReconciliationsForPeriod()` and renders a non-blocking warning when hard-closing a period with an unlocked bank reconciliation still open — confirmed against real cross-account/cross-period data live, not just code review, since `FiscalYearsService.hardClosePeriod()` genuinely has zero server-side awareness of banking at all (confirmed by reading it directly) and Hard Close is deliberately never disabled by this banner, since disabling it would misrepresent what the backend actually does.

**Two Procurement Payment Voucher retrofits, completed across Parts 1 and 5, close out `proc_payment_voucher`'s pair of Module-16 forward-reference FKs** (`bank_account_id`/`cheque_leaf_id`, both real, already-existing columns since before this slice began, confirmed in Part 1's own initial research): Part 1 wired `bankAccountId` (optional, `method === "BANK"`-gated); Part 5 wired `chequeLeafId` (optional, `method === "CHEQUE"`-gated, filtered to `status: "UNUSED"`) — both additive-only edits to the same one pre-existing dialog, both independently confirmed populated (and, on the negative side, genuinely `NULL` for non-matching methods) via `psql`, not API-response trust alone. Part 5's own live testing surfaced one honest, narrow follow-on finding: referencing a leaf via `chequeLeafId` does not itself transition that leaf's `status` away from `UNUSED` — the two are linked by FK but not by lifecycle, a real (if minor) workflow gap flagged in Part 5's own write-up rather than silently assumed clean.

Part 2's dispatch was interrupted by a real session/usage-limit cutoff (code was already complete and clean at that point, confirmed by direct inspection before the orchestrating session finished its own verification); every other part completed in a single uninterrupted pass. The web dev server's own documented memory-bloat-over-multi-day-uptime issue recurred at least once more (Part 2) and was handled the established way (restart when response latency, not raw memory, crosses the real threshold); by Part 5 the server was responding promptly throughout despite ~1.9GB resident memory, confirming latency (not raw RSS) is the correct signal to act on, per this project's own established discipline.
