## Slice 22 (Part 1 — Employees + Components) — 2026-08-15

**Verdict: Payroll's first two screens — the employee master (create/edit/exit/search/filter, plus a separate explicit-reveal panel for encrypted bank & pay details) and the payroll component catalogue (the 8 real seeded earning/deduction line types plus create/edit) — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack. The opportunistic `pyrl_component.code` 409 fix was attempted, completed, and independently re-verified live. One real, significant, live-confirmed finding contradicts this part's own task brief: `nationalId`/`kraPin` are NEVER redacted or actually encrypted anywhere on `EmployeesController` — both are plain `varchar` columns, unlike the 4 genuinely `jsonb`-encrypted `payDetails`/`bankName`/`branch`/`account` fields — found via a real round trip, not assumed, and the frontend's own copy was written (and re-written, once found) to reflect that real behavior rather than the brief's incorrect claim.**

### What was built

**`features/payroll/api/{employees,components,users-lookup}.api.ts`** — thin wrappers over `EmployeesController`/`ComponentsController`. `employees.api.ts` uses the zod-inferred `PyrlEmployeeResponseDto` directly as its read-return type (checked directly against `employee.schema.ts`: correctly typed, no gap) rather than mirroring the raw generated type, which DOES have the usual `Record<string, never>` reflection gaps on `userId`/`nssfNo`/`shifNo`/`exitDate` (nullable fields with no explicit `type:`) plus an object-shaped (not string-accepting) `payDetails`/`bankName`/`branch`/`account`. Two request-body gaps needed a boundary cast: the 4 opaque encrypted fields (frontend sends plain strings per this part's own brief; the generated shape expects `Record<string, unknown> | null`), and — a genuinely new gap class for this slice — `kind`/`employmentType` are typed plain `z.string()` on BOTH `CreatePyrlComponentDtoSchema`/`CreatePyrlEmployeeDtoSchema` (the zod-codegen script mirrors `@IsString()`, since neither `PyrlComponentKind` nor `PyrlEmploymentType` is a runtime enum class-validator can reflect via `@IsEnum()`), while the RAW generated `openapi-types.ts` gets both right as real literal unions (from `@ApiProperty({ enum: ... })`, which `@nestjs/swagger`'s reflection DOES pick up) — the opposite-direction gap `statement-import.api.ts`'s own `mappingTemplate` finding (Slice 21 Part 3) already established elsewhere in this codebase. A third, smaller gap: `CreatePyrlComponentDto.isStatutory` generates as REQUIRED (`boolean`, no `?`) despite `@IsOptional()` on the class, since `openapi-typescript` treats a Swagger `default: false` as making the field non-optional — a type-level-only accommodation (the form always supplies a real boolean).

**`features/payroll/hooks/{use-employees,use-components,use-users-lookup}.ts`** — query-key roots `["payroll","employees"]`/`["payroll","components"]`, mirroring every other feature folder's convention. `useEmployeeDecrypted()` defaults `enabled: false` — it only ever fires on the bank-details-panel's own explicit reveal click, never on page mount.

**`features/payroll/components/`** — `create-employee-dialog.tsx`/`edit-employee-dialog.tsx` (the edit form omits `staffNo`/`nationalId`/`kraPin`/`hireDate` entirely — create-only/immutable per `UpdatePyrlEmployeeDto`'s own field set; the 4 encrypted fields get a "clear-or-replace" tri-state row each, since a blank input can never safely mean "clear" for a field this dialog never gets to see the real value of), `employee-exit-dialog.tsx` (BR-PYRL-04, a required `exitDate` defaulting to today), `employee-bank-details-panel.tsx` (the ONE place `payDetails`/`bankName`/`branch`/`account` real plaintext is ever shown — `GET .../decrypted`, `payroll:employee:manage`-gated, never auto-fetched), `create-component-dialog.tsx`/`edit-component-dialog.tsx` (`code`/`kind` create-only/immutable, omitted from edit; both dialogs carry a real, load-bearing "code is permanent" notice, not decorative copy, since the run-computation engine looks up several of the 8 seeded rows by exact code string).

**Routes**: `app/(erp)/payroll/employees/{page.tsx,[id]/page.tsx}` (list: a debounced `GET .../search` trigram box + `isActive`/`departmentId` `<Select>` filters, only one of search/list query ever `enabled` at a time, the same shape `procurement/suppliers/page.tsx` establishes; detail: header card + edit/exit actions + the bank-details-panel section), `app/(erp)/payroll/components/{page.tsx,[id]/page.tsx}` (list: `kind`/`isStatutory` filters + a permanent visible "code is load-bearing" `<Alert>`; detail: repeats the same notice).

**Nav**: a new top-level Payroll dropdown (`HandCoins` icon, not previously used in `nav-links.tsx`) inserted immediately after Banking's closing `},` and before Communications, per this part's own plan — confirmed against the file's real current top-level order (…Banking, Communications, Users, Settings) before inserting, not assumed. 2 children to start (Employees, Components); explicitly NOT this dropdown's final shape — 5 more parts (salary structures/assignments, loans, one-offs, statutory tables, runs) will append the rest of Module 15's real backend surface.

**i18n**: a new `payroll` namespace (196 keys per locale: `employmentTypes` enum, `employees.{list,createDialog,editDialog,exitDialog,bankDetailsPanel,detail}`, `components.{kinds,list,createDialog,editDialog,detail}`) plus 3 `shell.nav` keys (`payroll`/`payrollEmployees`/`payrollComponents`), landing all 3 locales at identical **5920 lines** / **4773 keys**, verified programmatically both directions (zero missing/extra in either `sw`/`fr` vs `en`). Real Swahili/French translations, reusing this codebase's own established HR/finance vocabulary where it already existed (`departments.json`'s own `Idara`/`Département` pattern for department copy, `banking`'s own `Kiasi`/`Montant`-style finance-term discipline).

### Backend fix — `pyrl_component.code` duplicate now returns a clean 409

`packages/server/src/domains/payroll/application/components.service.ts`'s `create()` previously let a raw Postgres `23505` unique-violation on `uq_pyrl_component_code` reach the caller as an unhandled `500`. Fixed with the exact same catch-and-translate pattern `BankAccountsService.create()`/`EmployeeAssignmentsService.assign()` already establish elsewhere in this codebase (a small `isUniqueViolation()` helper checking `error.code ?? error.driverError?.code === "23505"`, wrapped around the repository call, re-thrown as `ConflictException` with a clear `` `pyrl_component: code "${code}" already exists` `` message; anything else re-thrown untouched). `packages/server` was rebuilt (`pnpm --filter @klickit/server run build`, clean) and `apps/api` was killed and restarted (`ts-node` resolves `@klickit/server` via its built `dist/`, so a source-only edit would not have taken effect) before live re-verification. `pnpm --filter @klickit/server run typecheck` clean; `pnpm --filter @klickit/server exec jest components.service` — 12/12 passing, unaffected (existing tests call the service directly and never previously exercised this catch path either way).

**Live-reverified, not just code-reviewed**: created a component with a fresh `code` (`201`), immediately attempted a second create with the SAME `code` — real `409 CONFLICT`, `"pyrl_component: code \"S22PT1_TEST_COMP\" already exists"`, not a raw `500`.

### A real, significant finding — `nationalId`/`kraPin` are never redacted or encrypted, contradicting this part's own task brief

The task brief this part was built from explicitly stated `nationalId`/`kraPin` are "ENCRYPTED at rest," alongside `payDetails`/`bankName`/`branch`/`account`, and that all 4 fields show as `"***"` on every read except `/decrypted`. Live testing during this part's own verification pass found this false for `nationalId`/`kraPin` specifically:

- `pyrl-employee.entity.ts` types `nationalId`/`kraPin` as plain `varchar` columns — NOT the `jsonb` "(enc)" shape `payDetails`/`bankName`/`branch`/`account` genuinely use.
- `EmployeesService.redact()` (the function every non-`/decrypted` read path calls) only ever touches `payDetails`/`bankName`/`branch`/`account` — `nationalId`/`kraPin` pass through completely untouched.
- **Confirmed live, both directions**: created an employee with `nationalId: "23456789"`, `kraPin: "A123456789Z"` → the CREATE response, a subsequent plain `GET /payroll/employees/{id}`, and `GET .../decrypted` ALL returned the identical real plaintext for both fields — never `"***"`. `psql` independently confirmed `pyrl_employee.national_id`/`kra_pin` store the literal plaintext strings in the database, while `pay_details`/`bank_name`/`branch`/`account` on the SAME row store real base64 AES-256-GCM ciphertext (confirmed by direct column inspection).

This is a genuine backend gap (arguably a real FR-PYRL-012.1 concern — "payroll data isolation" implies sensitive PII should be protected), not a frontend bug and not something this part's own narrow, pre-authorized backend-touch scope (the `pyrl_component.code` 409 fix, specifically) covered — **left unfixed, honestly flagged, not silently patched over**. The frontend's own copy was written (`create-employee-dialog.tsx`'s `encryptedFieldHint`, `employee-bank-details-panel.tsx`'s `sensitiveWarning`, the employee detail page's `bankDetailsSectionHint`, and every affected file's own doc comment) to state the REAL behavior — not masked, not encrypted, visible in plain text on the list/search/detail/create response alike — rather than repeat the brief's incorrect claim. `payDetails`/`bankName`/`branch`/`account` remain genuinely `"***"`-redacted and encrypted exactly as documented; only `nationalId`/`kraPin` are affected.

## Slice 22 (Part 2 — Salary Structures) — 2026-08-15

**Verdict: Salary Structures — the header CRUD (create/edit/list/detail, no delete route exists) plus its component-line editor (add/edit/remove FIXED-amount or percent-of-basic-pay lines against Part 1's own component catalogue) — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack. The opportunistic `pyrl_salary_structure.name` 409 fix was attempted, completed, and independently re-verified live. One real, significant, live-confirmed finding, unrelated to anything the task brief anticipated: `SalaryStructuresController.addLine()`/`updateLine()` always route a line's data through the `formula` jsonb column, even for `type: "FIXED"` — the dedicated `amount` NUMERIC column is permanently `null` for every line the real API can ever create, confirmed via a live HTTP round trip and independently via direct DB inspection. Payroll computation itself is unaffected (`resolveComponentAmount()` already handles a `{type:"FIXED", amount}` formula shape correctly), but this part's own frontend had to be built around the REAL behavior, not the documented "one dedicated column per type" contract.**

### What was built

**`features/payroll/api/salary-structures.api.ts`** — thin wrapper over `SalaryStructuresController` (base `/api/v1/payroll/salary-structures`, tag `payroll-salary-structures`) — the same single shared `payroll:structure:manage` permission gates all 8 routes, including both LIST routes (confirmed by reading the controller directly, 119 lines — no separate `:view` code, no DELETE route for the structure header itself). **Zero request-body codegen gaps here — a real, different-shaped finding from Part 1's own Components/Employees DTOs, checked directly rather than assumed**: `CreatePyrlSalaryStructureDtoSchema`/`UpdatePyrlSalaryStructureDtoSchema`/`StructureComponentLineDtoSchema` (the zod-inferred types) all generate cleanly, since `StructureComponentLineDto.type` is validated server-side via `@IsIn([...])` (which the zod-codegen script mirrors as a real literal union) rather than `@IsString()` (which drops the union, Part 1's own `kind`/`employmentType` finding) — every write function passes its `dto` straight through with no cast, confirmed by a clean `tsc --noEmit`. One response-side gap exists (`PyrlSalaryStructureResponseDto.grade` degrades to `Record<string, never> | null` in the RAW generated `openapi-types.ts`, the same nullable-without-an-explicit-type-hint gap documented elsewhere in this codebase), already absorbed for free by using the zod-inferred type directly as every read function's return type, per `employees.api.ts`'s own precedent.

**`features/payroll/hooks/use-salary-structures.ts`** — query-key root `["payroll","salary-structures"]`, plus a nested `["payroll","salary-structures",structureId,"lines"]` lines key, mirroring `use-budgets.ts`'s own `{budgetId, ...}`-shaped line-mutation convention (Accounting Budgets, Slice 17 Part 3) for the 3 line mutations.

**`features/payroll/components/component-combobox.tsx`** — a small, standalone, REUSABLE component picker wired directly to Part 1's own `useComponents()` hook, labeling each item `code — name` (e.g. `HOUSE_ALLOWANCE — House Allowance`). Built standalone (not a private sub-component of the line editor) since later parts — employee-component overrides, one-offs — will need the identical picker, per this part's own task brief.

**`features/payroll/lib/percent.ts`** — exact decimal-string percent <-> fraction conversion (`"15"` <-> `"0.15"`) for the line editor's rate field, implemented as a pure base-10 decimal-point shift (never `parseFloat`/`* 100`/`/ 100`) to avoid the classic binary-float round-trip drift (`0.29 * 100 === 29.000000000000004` in JS) — the same discipline `lib/money.ts`'s own BigInt-based `formatMoney()`/`sumMoneyStrings()` already establish for KES amounts, applied here to a rate instead.

**`features/payroll/components/create-salary-structure-dialog.tsx`/`edit-salary-structure-dialog.tsx`** — `name`/`grade`/`effectiveFrom`, all genuinely editable on both (unlike Part 1's Components/Employees, nothing here is create-only/immutable, confirmed against `UpdatePyrlSalaryStructureDto` directly). Both carry a real `effectiveFromHint`: this date is purely descriptive metadata that plays no role in any real time-versioned lookup — the actual time boundary that matters at payroll-compute time lives on `pyrl_employee_assignment.effectiveFrom/To` (Part 3, not built yet).

No KES figure is ever computed or shown for a PERCENT_OF_BASIC line (the table shows the plain rate, e.g. "15% of basic pay") — a `resolvedAtPayrollTimeNotice` `<Alert>` states plainly that the real value is only knowable once an employee with a real `basicPay` is assigned (Part 3's own scope).

`packages/server/src/domains/payroll/application/salary-structures.service.ts`'s `create()` previously let a raw Postgres `23505` unique-violation on `uq_pyrl_salary_structure_name` (confirmed via `packages/server/src/migrations/0130-create-payroll-tables.ts:141`) reach the caller as an unhandled `500`. **Live-reverified, not just code-reviewed**: created a structure with a fresh `name` (`201`), immediately attempted a second create with the SAME `name` — real `409 CONFLICT`, `"pyrl_salary_structure: name \"S22Pt2 Grade 5\" already exists"`, not a raw `500`.

### A real, significant finding — FIXED lines are always stored via `formula`, never via the dedicated `amount` column

The task brief this part was built from (matching `salary-structures.service.ts`'s own doc comment) describes a strict "exactly one of the entity's own `amount` Money column OR `formula` jsonb column is set per row" contract, and predicted `line.amount !== null` as the way to tell a FIXED line apart from a PERCENT_OF_BASIC one. Live testing during this part's own verification pass found this is not what the real API does:

- `SalaryStructuresController.addLine()`/`updateLine()` both build their service call via a local `toFormula(dto)` helper that returns `{ type: "FIXED", amount: dto.amount }` as a FORMULA object whenever `dto.type === "FIXED"` — never as the dedicated `amount: Money` argument `SalaryStructuresService.addLine()`/`updateLine()` genuinely accept and route to the entity's own `amount` column (confirmed correct in isolation: `salary-structures.service.spec.ts`'s own "accepts a FIXED amount line" unit test calls the service directly with a real `amount: Money` and gets it stored on that column).
- **Confirmed live, both via the HTTP response and independently via direct DB inspection**: a FIXED line created with `{componentId, type:"FIXED", amount:"5000"}` came back `{"amount":null,"formula":{"type":"FIXED","amount":"5000"}}` — and a direct query against `app.pyrl_structure_component` confirmed the same: `amount` column `null`, `formula` jsonb column holding the full `{type,amount}` object, on the same row. A `PATCH` switching that line to PERCENT_OF_BASIC left `amount` unchanged (still `null` — it was never populated in the first place) and correctly overwrote `formula` to `{type:"PERCENT_OF_BASIC", rate:"0.05"}`.
- **Payroll computation itself is unaffected by this bug** — `resolveComponentAmount()` (a pure function, `salary-structures.service.ts:44-57`) already handles a `{type:"FIXED", amount}` formula shape correctly, since that's a real member of its own `StructureComponentFormula` union; Pass B's future run-computation engine will resolve FIXED lines correctly regardless.

This is a genuine, live-confirmed backend bug in the controller's own request-mapping logic, out of this part's own pre-authorized backend-touch scope (the `create()` 409 fix, specifically) — **left unfixed, honestly flagged, not silently patched over**. The frontend was built around the REAL behavior instead of the documented one: `structure-line-editor.tsx`'s own `resolveLineDisplay()` reads the top-level `amount` column first (the documented, intended shape — stays correct for free if this controller bug is ever fixed), falling back to `formula.amount`/`formula.rate` (what the live API actually returns today) — both `salary-structures.api.ts` and `structure-line-editor.tsx` carry full doc comments on this finding.

## Slice 22 (Part 4 — Statutory Tables) — 2026-08-15

**Verdict: the admin-editable Kenyan statutory rate/band tables (PAYE bands + personal relief, NSSF's 2 fixed tiers, SHIF's rate + optional floor, AHL's 2 fixed rates) — kind-first create/edit dialogs with 4 structurally distinct params sub-forms, a kind-aware read-only params view, and BR-PYRL-01's real "what table applies on this date" effective-lookup utility — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack. The opportunistic `pyrl_statutory_table (kind, effective_from)` 409 fix was attempted, completed, and independently re-verified live. With this part complete, real statutory tables now exist for the first time — combined with Parts 1-3's master data (employees, components, salary structures, assignments), a real payroll run (Part 6) is finally computable end-to-end once built.**

### What was built

**`features/payroll/lib/statutory-params.ts`** — the 4 real, seeded `params` jsonb shapes (`PayeParams`/`NssfParams`/`ShifParams`/`AhlParams`), mirrored word-for-word from `StatutoryCalculationService`'s own documented interfaces, plus `as*Params()` runtime guards (params is opaque, DTO-unvalidated jsonb — a row's real data could in principle not match its own kind's shape) and `defaultParamsForKind()` for a fresh create-dialog's starting state. Every rate field (`rate`, `tier1.rate`, `tier2.rate`, `employeeRate`, `employerRate`) is a plain JS number shown/edited as the real stored fraction directly (e.g. `0.06` for NSSF's 6%) via plain `<input type="number">`-backed state — deliberately NOT reusing `lib/percent.ts`'s decimal-string percent↔fraction conversion (Part 2), since that routine targets a different field (`StructureComponentLineDto.rate`, a validated decimal STRING) on a different table; building a second conversion routine for a different underlying type was judged unnecessary risk for a real production payroll-affecting figure, per this part's own task brief.

**`features/payroll/api/statutory-tables.api.ts`** — thin wrapper over `StatutoryTablesController` (base `/api/v1/payroll/statutory-tables`, tag `payroll-statutory-tables`) — one shared `payroll:statutory-table:manage` permission gates all 5 routes, including both LIST-shaped ones (`listByKind`/`findEffectiveFor`), no DELETE route exists (confirmed by reading the 71-line controller directly). `params: Record<string, unknown>` genuinely generates cleanly and identically on both the raw generated type and the zod-inferred one (verified directly per this part's own task brief instruction, not assumed). **One real gap found, the same class as Part 1's own `kind`/`employmentType` finding**: the zod-inferred `CreatePyrlStatutoryTableDtoSchema.kind` is plain `z.string()` (the zod-codegen script mirrors `@IsString()`, since `PyrlStatutoryKind` is a TS union, not a runtime enum `@IsEnum()` could reflect), losing the literal union the RAW generated type gets right (`@ApiProperty({ enum: PYRL_STATUTORY_KINDS })`). This actually bit at the `apiClient.POST()` call site (a real `tsc` error, not just a doc-comment note) — `createStatutoryTable()` casts at the boundary via a local `CreatePyrlStatutoryTableRequestBody` interface, the same shape `components.api.ts`'s own `createComponent()` already establishes.

**`features/payroll/hooks/use-statutory-tables.ts`** — query-key root `["payroll","statutory-tables"]`, list keyed by kind (`[...root,"list",kind]`), plus `useEffectiveStatutoryTable(kind, periodEndDate)` (`enabled` only once a date is chosen, `retry: false` since a `404` here is a legitimate "no table configured" outcome, not a transient failure to retry).

Every rate field carries an inline "as a decimal fraction, e.g. 0.06 for 6%" hint.

`packages/server/src/domains/payroll/application/statutory-tables.service.ts`'s `create()` previously let a raw Postgres `23505` unique-violation on `uq_pyrl_statutory_table_kind_effective_from` (confirmed via `packages/server/src/migrations/0130-create-payroll-tables.ts:234`) reach the caller as an unhandled `500`. ## Slice 22 (Part 5 — Loans) — 2026-08-15

**Verdict: staff loan applications — a dedicated `/payroll/loans` employee-picker list, a detail page with the full FLAT/REDUCING amortization lifecycle (approve/reject, manual recovery recording, early settlement, all status-gated), and a real schedule table — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack. No backend fix was needed or attempted this part, per the brief's own expectation: `LoansController`'s conflict/validation handling was already clean, real `ValidationException`s throughout, confirmed by direct read before starting. The FLAT-vs-REDUCING amortization math was independently confirmed correct via direct DB inspection (constant vs. declining interest, both reconciling exactly to the original principal), and the "reject means Written Off, never Rejected" semantic the brief called out as safety-critical is enforced in copy at every layer (status badge, confirm dialog, i18n) exactly as instructed.**

### What was built

**`features/payroll/api/loans.api.ts`** — thin wrapper over `LoansController` (base `/api/v1/payroll/loans`, tag `payroll-loans`) — `payroll:loan:create` reused for every read route (no dedicated `:view` code, confirmed by reading the controller's own doc comment directly), `payroll:loan:decide` gating `decide`/`record-recovery`/`settle-early`. **Zero request-body codegen gaps here — a real, different finding from Parts 1's/4's own `kind`/`employmentType` findings, checked directly rather than assumed**: `CreatePyrlLoanDtoSchema.rateKind` (the zod-inferred type) IS a real `z.enum(["FLAT", "REDUCING"])`, matching the raw generated type's `rateKind: "FLAT" | "REDUCING"` exactly, because `loan.dto.ts` validates it via `@IsIn(PYRL_LOAN_RATE_KINDS)` rather than the `@IsString()` shape that lost the union on Parts 1/4's own fields. Every write function passes its `dto` straight through with no `as unknown as` cast. One response-side gap exists on `PyrlLoanResponseDto.approvalRef` (`Record<string, never> | null` on the raw generated type, `z.string().nullable()` on the zod-inferred one — the same nullable-without-an-explicit-`type:`-hint reflection gap Parts 2/3/4 already documented for `grade`/`effectiveTo`), absorbed for free by using the zod-inferred type directly as every read function's return type, matching `employees.api.ts`'s own established precedent. `@klickit/contracts` exports no standalone `PyrlLoanRateKind`/`PyrlLoanStatus` type (unlike `PyrlStatutoryKind`, which Part 4 had to define locally in `lib/statutory-params.ts` for the identical reason) — both are derived here via indexed access on `PyrlLoanResponseDto` and re-exported for every component in this part to share.

**`features/payroll/hooks/use-loans.ts`** — query-key root `["payroll","loans",employeeId]` for the list, `["payroll","loans","detail",id]` for a single loan, `["payroll","loans","detail",id,"schedule"]` for the schedule, exactly as specified. Every mutation invalidates all 3 shapes unconditionally (a loan action always changes the detail row, and every write except create also potentially changes the schedule — `decide` GENERATES it, `record-recovery`/`settle-early` both mutate existing rows), simpler and safer than tracking exactly which subset each call site needs.

**`features/payroll/components/`** — `create-loan-dialog.tsx` (employee via a real `<EmployeeCombobox>` field, seeded from a `defaultEmployeeId` prop but always genuinely editable per the brief's explicit instruction to reuse Part 3's picker directly; `principal` via `<MoneyInput>`; `rate` as a plain `<Input>`, NOT a `<MoneyInput>` — it's a rate, not a currency amount, and `MoneyInput`'s own "KES" prefix would be actively misleading — but still validated via `lib/money.ts`'s `normalizeMoneyInput()`, since `rate` genuinely matches the same `DECIMAL_PATTERN` shape `principal` does, a deliberately different call from Part 4's own decision NOT to reuse `lib/percent.ts` for its unrelated plain-number rate fields; the rate hint states plainly this is the ANNUAL rate as a decimal fraction — e.g. `0.145` for 14.5%/year, never monthly, never a whole-number percentage — in all 3 languages; FLAT/REDUCING hints describe the real amortization mechanics honestly, sourced from reading `loans.service.ts:47-130` directly, not paraphrased from memory; a permanent "no preview" notice sets expectations honestly since the real schedule only exists after a real `decide(approved:true)` call), `loan-decide-dialog.tsx` (`LoanDecideActions`, one file with both Approve and Reject confirm-only dialogs — `DecidePyrlLoanDto` has no comment field, so there's nothing to type, just confirm; the reject dialog's own copy says "this will mark the loan as Written Off," with a dedicated warning that there is no separate "Rejected" status and a written-off loan stays that way permanently — never implying a distinct Rejected state exists, per the brief's explicit safety instruction), `loan-schedule-table.tsx` (renders its own dedicated "not generated yet" / "written off, never went active" message for `PENDING_APPROVAL`/`WRITTEN_OFF` WITHOUT ever firing the schedule query for those two statuses, rather than relying on `<QueryBoundary>`'s generic empty-state copy, which would have read like something went wrong for a case that's genuinely expected; a `cancelledBadge` flags rows zeroed by an early settlement), `record-recovery-dialog.tsx` (the `periodKey` field is a real `<Select>` sourced from the loan's own live `useLoanSchedule()` rows, never free-typed — picking a period prefills the amount with that installment's real remaining due via `sumMoneyStrings()`'s exact BigInt arithmetic, genuinely editable afterward since this is an out-of-band correction tool), `settle-early-dialog.tsx` (explicit lump-sum-payoff copy: cancels the remaining schedule and closes at zero balance unconditionally, not a partial payment), `loan-status-badge.tsx` (the 4 real statuses, `WRITTEN_OFF` deliberately not split into two visual variants since the response carries nothing to distinguish a rejected application from a — currently impossible via this controller — written-off active loan).

**Routes**: `app/(erp)/payroll/loans/page.tsx` (an `<EmployeeCombobox>` picker drives scope — `GET /payroll/loans?employeeId=` genuinely requires it, no global list exists — then that employee's loan history + "New Loan" trigger, the same "picker selects scope, list follows" shape Part 4's kind-tabs page established; a dedicated "no employee selected" prompt renders instead of firing `useLoans(undefined)`, which would otherwise misreport as an endless loading state per `query-boundary.tsx`'s own `isPending` semantics) and `.../[id]/page.tsx` (header card with employee name resolved via Part 1's `useEmployee()`, not just a bare uuid; the 3 real actions each self-gate their own visibility by status; `<LoanScheduleTable>` below).

**Nav**: a 5th and — per the brief's own instruction to say so explicitly — still not necessarily final Payroll child appended: Loans (`/payroll/loans`, `payroll:loan:create`). One-offs and Payroll Runs remain for future parts.

**i18n**: a new `payroll.loans` block (`statuses`, `rateKinds`, `list`, `createDialog`, `decideDialog`, `scheduleTable`, `recordRecoveryDialog`, `settleEarlyDialog`, `detail`) plus the 1 new `shell.nav.payrollLoans` key, added via the same scratchpad JSON.parse→assign→JSON.stringify(data,null,2) merge-script mechanism every prior part established. Landed all 3 locales at identical **6298 lines / 5689 keys** counting every object-level key (or **5083 keys** counting leaves only — Part 4's own dual-convention note applies here too, both are internally consistent, the delta over Part 4's own 6176/5579 baseline is +122 lines / +110 all-depth keys), verified programmatically both directions — zero missing/extra keys in either `sw`/`fr` vs `en`. The interest-rate hint (the brief's own named financial-safety risk) was translated carefully in Swahili and French to preserve the exact same load-bearing claim, not translated loosely: Swahili keeps "MWAKA" (YEAR) capitalized and explicit ("Weka kiwango cha MWAKA kama sehemu ya desimali — mfano, 0.145 kwa 14.5% kwa mwaka... si cha mwezi kamwe, wala si asilimia iliyoandikwa kama namba nzima"), French keeps "ANNUEL" capitalized identically ("Saisissez le taux ANNUEL sous forme de fraction décimale... jamais un taux mensuel, et jamais un pourcentage écrit comme un nombre entier"). The reject/Written-Off distinction was translated with the same care (Swahili: *"Kukataa kunaweka mkopo huu kama Umefutwa, si 'Umekataliwa' — hakuna hali tofauti ya Kukataliwa"*; French: *"Refuser marque ce prêt comme Passé en perte, pas comme « Refusé » — il n'existe pas de statut Refusé distinct"*). Swahili's "Mkopo" (loan) is the same word this codebase's own Accounting namespace already uses for "Credit" in a journal-line context — a real, correct, standard Swahili financial term shared by both concepts (not a translation error), kept namespaced apart (`payroll.loans` vs `accounting.journals`) so no runtime string collision is possible; page-level copy says "Mikopo ya Wafanyakazi" (Staff Loans) to keep it unambiguous to a human reader too.

### Live verification

A throwaway role (`Slice22Pt5 Payroll Verify <timestamp>`, `payroll:loan:create` + `payroll:loan:decide`) and user, created via a direct Node+`pg` script (no `psql` binary on `PATH` in this environment, the same substitution Parts 2-4 already established — real direct SQL either way) against `app.usr_role`/`app.usr_role_permission`/`app.usr_user`/`app.usr_user_role`, a real `POST /api/v1/auth/login` (`identifier`/`password`, not `username` — the real `LoginDto` field name, confirmed by reading it directly) for a genuine bearer token, plain `fetch` against the running `apps/api` on port 3000, reusing Part 1's real seeded employees (`EMP-S22PT1-001`/`002`):

1. **FLAT loan create**: principal 60000, rate `"0.12"`, termMonths 6 → real `201`, `status: "PENDING_APPROVAL"`, `balance: "60000.0000"` (equals principal), a real `approvalRef` uuid present. `GET .../schedule` before approval → genuinely empty `[]`.
2. **`decide(approved:true)` on the FLAT loan** → `status: "ACTIVE"`, `balance` reset to `"60000.0000"`. `GET .../schedule` → 6 real rows now exist. **Independently confirmed via direct DB query, not just the API response**: every row's `principal_due` is a constant `10000.0000` (60000÷6) and every row's `interest_due` is a constant `600.0000` (60000×0.12÷12) — the defining FLAT trait, interest never recalculated against a declining balance — sum of `principal_due` reconciles exactly to `60000`.
3. **REDUCING loan create + approve** (employee 2, same principal/rate/term) → **confirmed via direct DB query**: `interest_due` strictly DECLINES row over row (`600, 502.471, 403.9667, 304.4773, 203.9931, 102.504`), and the sum of all 6 `principal_due` values reconciles exactly to `60000.0000` — the last row's principal absorbing the exact rounding remainder, as documented.
4. **`record-recovery` on the FLAT loan** for its real first `duePeriod` (`2026-08`), amount `10600` → `balance` decreased to `49400.0000`, the matching schedule row's `recoveredAmount` updated to `10600.0000`, confirmed via a direct DB re-query. **A `periodKey` matching no real schedule row** (`"2099-01"`) → real `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`, message exactly `` `pyrl_loan {id} has no installment due in period 2099-01` ``, byte-for-byte as documented.
5. **`settle-early` on the REDUCING loan** (settlement date = today) → `balance: "0.0000"`, `status: "SETTLED"`. **Confirmed via direct DB query**: the row due in the settlement month itself was left untouched (its real, positive `principal_due`/`interest_due` unchanged, since it was never actually recovered against), while every row due AFTER the settlement month had both `principal_due` and `interest_due` zeroed — exactly the "cancel future unrecovered installments" mechanics documented in `settleEarly()`'s own doc comment.

Permission restored afterward.

### A real, honest surprise — `decide`/`record-recovery`/`settle-early` all return `201`, not the documented `200`

`LoansController` carries no `@HttpCode` decorator anywhere (confirmed by reading it directly) — every `@Post()` route, including `decide`/`record-recovery`/`settle-early`, falls through to NestJS's own default `201 Created` status, even though each one's own `@ApiResponse({ status: 200, ... })` swagger annotation documents `200`. Live-confirmed on all 3 endpoints during verification above. This is the same class of doc-vs-actual mismatch Part 3 already found and flagged for `EmployeeAssignmentsController`/`EmployeeComponentsController`'s own `/end` routes (Slice 21 Part 5's `flag-stale` precedent) — genuinely harmless to this frontend (`unwrapApiResult()` checks `response.ok`, i.e. any 2xx, never an exact status code), so no frontend code needed to change and no backend fix was attempted (consistent with the brief's own "no fix expected this part" framing) — flagged here purely so a future reader of `loans.controller.ts`'s own `@ApiResponse` annotations doesn't take the documented `200` at face value.

## Slice 22 (Part 6 — Payroll Runs, setup through approval) — 2026-08-16

**Verdict: the payroll run engine's own frontend — create → compute → review → submit → decide, plus a period-scoped one-offs panel embedded on the run detail page — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack, including a REAL, fully-reconciled computed payroll run that reached `APPROVED`. Two real backend bugs were found and fixed, one of them significant: `DecidePyrlRunDto.approved` carried zero class-validator decorators, meaning the global `whitelist: true` `ValidationPipe` silently stripped it from every request — `decide()` could never actually approve a run through the real API before this fix, only ever take the "return to REVIEW" branch regardless of what a caller sent. A THIRD real backend gap was found during this pass's own independent verification (not by the build agent) and is left unfixed, honestly flagged: `compute()`'s loan-recovery logic only ever considers `activeLoans[0]` — an employee holding two or more concurrently ACTIVE loans has every loan after the first silently, permanently ignored by real payroll computation, with no error, no field, no trace.**

### Process note — this part's build was interrupted twice, both handled per this project's established practice

The first dispatch stalled with no code written and was redispatched fresh. The second dispatch produced essentially the ENTIRE part — all API wrappers, hooks, components, both routes, the full i18n namespace across all 3 locales, AND both real backend fixes, complete with its own frontend doc comments explaining each — plus ran its own live verification far enough to compute a real run, add and recompute against a real one-off, and carry it through the full `submit → decide(false) → REVIEW → submit again → decide(true) → APPROVED` cycle, all before a session-limit reset cut it off right as it began writing its own PROGRESS.md entry. I (the orchestrating session) independently confirmed the code was complete and correct — `tsc --noEmit` clean on both `web` and `server`, both backend diffs reviewed and matching the exact established fix pattern from Parts 1/2/4 — then rebuilt `@klickit/server`, restarted `apps/api` (a source-only edit does not take effect under `ts-node` without this, per every prior backend-fix part's own precedent), and completed the remaining live verification and this write-up myself, re-deriving and independently cross-checking the interrupted agent's own already-real database state rather than re-running the whole scenario from scratch.

### What was built

**`features/payroll/api/{payroll-runs,oneoffs}.api.ts`** — thin wrappers over `PayrollRunsController`/`OneoffsController`. `totals`/`varianceReport` on `PyrlRunResponseDto` are genuinely untyped `Record<string,unknown>` on the backend itself (no fixed OpenAPI shape to generate against either way) — `features/payroll/lib/run-totals.ts` defines the real `PyrlRunTotals`/`PyrlRunVarianceReport` interfaces client-side, mirroring `payroll-runs.service.ts:72-85`/`:578-585` field-for-field, with safe-cast helpers that don't assume every field is present pre-compute (`totals: {}`).

### Backend fix #1 — `DecidePyrlRunDto.approved` was silently always `undefined` (significant)

`packages/server/src/domains/payroll/api/dto/payroll-run.dto.ts`: `DecidePyrlRunDto.approved` carried `@ApiProperty()` but ZERO `class-validator` decorators — the same bug CLASS this whole project has now found and fixed FIVE times (Stock Takes, Bank Statement Import, `pyrl_component.code`, `pyrl_salary_structure.name`, and now this), but this instance is materially more serious than any of the prior four: because `approved` is a plain `boolean`, `!approved` in `onApprovalDecided()` (`payroll-runs.service.ts:628-633`) treats `undefined` exactly like `false` — meaning **every single `decide()` call, regardless of whether the caller sent `{"approved":true}` or `{"approved":false}`, always executed the "return to REVIEW" branch**. A run could be submitted for approval, but a decision-maker's genuine, real "approve" click would have silently done nothing but bounce it back to REVIEW, forever, with a real `200` response giving no hint anything was wrong. Fixed with one `@IsBoolean()` decorator. Rebuilt `@klickit/server`, restarted `apps/api`, and this fix's own effectiveness is PROVEN by the live database state left behind: `pyrl_run` id `01a0076c-023c-7181-81ec-bc24da886aee` genuinely reached `status: APPROVED` with a real `approved_by` populated — impossible before this fix, since `approved:true` could never have taken effect.

### Backend fix #2 — `pyrl_oneoff` duplicate `(employeeId, periodKey, componentId)` now returns a clean 409

`packages/server/src/domains/payroll/application/oneoffs.service.ts`'s `create()` — same catch-`23505`-throw-`ConflictException` pattern as `ComponentsService`/`SalaryStructuresService`/`StatutoryTablesService` (Parts 1/2/4), citing the real constraint `uq_pyrl_oneoff_employee_period_component` (`packages/server/src/migrations/0130-create-payroll-tables.ts:395`).

### A third real finding — `compute()` only ever recovers against the FIRST active loan, found during THIS pass's own independent verification

Not found or documented by the build agent — discovered while independently reconciling the live database state left behind. `payroll-runs.service.ts:416-418`:

```ts
const activeLoans = await this.loanRepository.findActiveForEmployee(employee.id, em);
if (activeLoans.length > 0) {
  const loan = activeLoans[0];
  // ...only this one loan's schedule is ever consulted for this period's recovery...
```

Nothing in this codebase prevents an employee from holding two or more concurrently `ACTIVE` loans — confirmed live, not hypothetically: Part 5's own verification left employee `EMP-S22PT1-001` (Amina) with TWO simultaneously `ACTIVE` loans (`PYR-000001`, `PYR-000002`). This part's own real computed run for period `2026-08` (see below) shows `loan_recovered: 10600.0000` — hand-reconciled to be EXACTLY `PYR-000001`'s own period-1 installment (`principal_due:10000 + interest_due:600`, `recovered_amount:0`, `findActiveForEmployee()`'s own "oldest-created-first" ordering putting `PYR-000001` at index 0). `PYR-000002` — which ALREADY had a real, deliberate manual recovery of `10600` recorded against it in Part 5's own verification, for this SAME period — is completely invisible to this run's own computation; it is never even queried. An employee's second (and any further) active loan is therefore, in practice, only ever reachable through the manual out-of-band `record-recovery` endpoint (Part 5) — never through a real payroll run — for as long as their first active loan remains active. This is a genuine business-logic gap (which loan should take priority? should recovery capacity split proportionally across all active loans instead of exhausting the oldest first? — a real product decision, not a narrow bug), left unfixed and flagged prominently here rather than silently worked around; a future pass revisiting Loans/Payroll Runs together should treat this as a real, load-bearing finding, not a hypothetical edge case.

**Verdict: the payroll run lifecycle's final three stages — `commit` (P-27, one aggregated GL journal + real loan-recovery finalization), `pay` (P-28, a separate disbursement journal via a method-only selector) and `file` (administrative-only, no real filing documents) — plus a genuine client-assembled payslip view, built and verified end-to-end against the real, now fully-`FILED` run Part 6 left live. Every figure this pass's own UI would show — the run-level totals, the loan-balance change, both journals' balance, and the full component breakdown — was independently cross-checked against direct `psql`-equivalent queries, not trusted from the API response alone. One real, SIGNIFICANT, live-discovered finding directly contradicts this part's own task brief, which had called BR-PYRL-02 "already correctly translated (nothing to fix)": `uq_pyrl_main_run_p`'s partial unique index is scoped ONLY to `status = 'COMMITTED'`, not the full completed-lifecycle set — the instant a legitimate run progresses past `COMMITTED` to `PAID`/`FILED` (which every real payroll run is SUPPOSED to do), the index's protection evaporates and a second, independent MAIN run for the identical period can be computed, approved, and committed with ZERO conflict, posting a genuinely separate real GL journal for the same period. Live-proven, not theorized: this pass's own verification run left **two real, permanent `COMMITTED`-or-later MAIN runs for period `2026-08`**, doubling `5010 Salaries and Wages Expense`'s real posted balance for that period (`117500.0000` instead of the correct `58750.0000`) — a genuine, serious accounting-integrity gap, left deliberately unfixed this pass (a real migration-level schema change, out of this part's own narrow, unauthorized-for-schema-changes scope) and flagged prominently below.**

### A real, SIGNIFICANT finding — BR-PYRL-02's real-world protection is far weaker than the brief (and this codebase's own doc comments) claim

The task brief this part was built from states BR-PYRL-02 is "a real, clean `409`, already correctly translated (nothing to fix)." Live testing during this part's own optional BR-PYRL-02 conflict test (the brief's own step 4, attempted since time allowed) found this materially incomplete:

- The real DDL (`packages/server/src/migrations/0130-create-payroll-tables.ts:319-321`, read directly): `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_pyrl_main_run_p ON app.pyrl_run (period_key) WHERE run_kind = 'MAIN' AND status = 'COMMITTED'`. This is a **partial** index — it only ever constrains rows whose CURRENT status is the literal string `'COMMITTED'`. `pyrl_run.status` is a forward-only progression (`COMMITTED -> PAID -> FILED`, confirmed by reading every lifecycle method directly — nothing ever moves a run backward from `COMMITTED`), so the instant a legitimately-committed run advances to `PAID` or `FILED` — which is the NORMAL, EXPECTED, GUARANTEED outcome for every real payroll run that completes its own lifecycle — that row silently drops out of the partial index's own `WHERE` clause, and the constraint stops protecting that period AT ALL.
- **Live-proven, not theorized**: with the real `APPROVED` fixture run (`01a0076c-...`) already carried through `commit -> pay -> file` to a genuine `FILED` state (see Live verification below), a SECOND, brand-new MAIN run for the SAME period `2026-08` was created, computed, reviewed, submitted, and approved (reusing this part's own newly-verified real actions plus Part 6's own already-verified earlier ones) — its own `commit()` call succeeded with a real `201`/`COMMITTED`, genuinely posting a SECOND real P-27 journal (`GL_-000822`) for the identical period, with **zero conflict raised**. A direct query against `app.pyrl_run` confirms both rows now permanently coexist (`01a0076c-...` `FILED`, `01a00912-...` `COMMITTED`) for `period_key = '2026-08'`, `run_kind = 'MAIN'`. A direct query against `app.gl_journal_line` confirms the concrete real-world harm: `5010 Salaries and Wages Expense` was debited `58750.0000` TWICE for the same period — a real, permanent `117500.0000` posted balance where the correct figure is `58750.0000`.
- This is the OPPOSITE of a narrow, safe, isolated fix (the `isUniqueViolation()`/`ConflictException` pattern this slice has now applied cleanly four times) — closing this gap for real requires widening the partial index's own `WHERE` clause (e.g. to `status IN ('COMMITTED','PAID','FILED')`) via a genuine new migration, on a table that (per this very test) now already contains two real rows that would need to be reconciled against the WIDENED rule before it could even be added cleanly. This is squarely a dedicated-pass-level schema change, not something to patch opportunistically mid-part the way this slice's four 409-translation fixes were — **left deliberately unfixed, flagged prominently here rather than silently worked around or hidden by simply not attempting the optional test that surfaced it.**
- The two real runs/journals this finding produced are permanent, live, and were left exactly as this test produced them (per this part's own brief's own explicit instruction never to attempt a revert on committed data, and because no delete route exists for `pyrl_run`/`gl_journal` anywhere in this codebase either way) — they now serve as a concrete, permanent, live piece of evidence of this real gap for any future pass that revisits BR-PYRL-02.

## Slice 22 — closing summary (Parts 1–7 complete)

Phase 6 Slice 22 built Module 15 (Payroll)'s entire frontend from zero across 7 parts, against a large, already-complete backend (`packages/server/src/domains/payroll/`) that had no frontend at all before this slice began: **Part 1** — Employees (create/edit/exit/search/filter + a separate explicit-reveal encrypted-bank-details panel) and Components (the 8 seeded earning/deduction line types); **Part 2** — Salary Structures (header CRUD + a FIXED/PERCENT_OF_BASIC component-line editor); **Part 3** — Employee Assignments (the basicPay-snapshot history + 2-call end-then-reassign workflow) and Employee Components (personal overrides, with a persistent, load-bearing "this ADDS to, never replaces, a structure line" warning), both built as new sections on the existing employee detail page rather than new nav routes, since neither backend controller has a cross-employee list route; **Part 4** — Statutory Tables (PAYE bands, NSSF/SHIF/AHL rates, BR-PYRL-01's real effective-dated lookup utility); **Part 5** — Loans (the full FLAT/REDUCING amortization lifecycle, approve/reject-as-written-off/record-recovery/settle-early, all status-gated); **Part 6** — Payroll Runs' own `create -> compute -> review -> submit -> decide` half of the lifecycle, plus a period-scoped one-offs panel, reaching a REAL `APPROVED` run for the first time in this whole project; **Part 7** — the run lifecycle's remaining `commit -> pay -> file` half plus a real, honest, client-assembled payslip view, carrying that same real run all the way to `FILED`. The Payroll nav dropdown was built incrementally, 1-2 children per part (2 in Part 1, 1 each in Parts 2/4/5/6, 0 in Part 3 and Part 7 — both deliberate, since neither part's own work had a natural cross-entity list route to back a new top-level link), now in its **FINAL shape at 6 children** (Employees, Components, Salary Structures, Statutory Tables, Loans, Payroll Runs) — no more are planned.

**Two genuinely different real backend bug CLASSES were found and fixed across this slice, get the count right rather than conflating them**: (1) **FOUR real `ConflictException`-pattern fixes** — the identical `isUniqueViolation()`-checking-`23505`-then-throwing-`ConflictException` catch pattern, applied to a raw, previously-unhandled `500` on a real unique-constraint violation: `pyrl_component.code` (Part 1), `pyrl_salary_structure.name` (Part 2), `pyrl_statutory_table (kind, effective_from)` (Part 4), and `pyrl_oneoff (employeeId, periodKey, componentId)` (Part 6) — each independently live-reverified after its own `packages/server` rebuild + `apps/api` restart, each confirmed to produce a real, clean `409` with the documented message afterward, not just code-reviewed. (2) **ONE real `ValidationPipe`-whitelist-strips-undecorated-fields fix, a categorically different bug class** — `DecidePyrlRunDto.approved` (Part 6) carried `@ApiProperty()` but ZERO class-validator decorators, meaning the global `whitelist: true` `ValidationPipe` silently stripped it from every request regardless of what a caller sent, so `decide()` could never actually approve a payroll run through the real API before this fix (only ever the "return to REVIEW" branch, forever) — fixed with one `@IsBoolean()` decorator, live-proven by the very fact that a real run reached `APPROVED` at all afterward. These are NOT the same bug class: the `ConflictException` fixes are about translating a raw DB-level `500` into a clean domain `409`; the `ValidationPipe` fix is about a request body field being silently discarded before the controller method even runs. Parts 3 and 5 each explicitly checked their own request DTOs/controllers for further instances of either class and found none — reported honestly as checked absences, matching this whole project's own established discipline of never assuming a later part's finding generalizes without checking.

**Three real, significant backend gaps were found and deliberately left open across this slice — get this list right too, since it grew by one this slice's own final part**: (1) **`nationalId`/`kraPin` non-redaction** (Part 1) — both fields are plain `varchar`, never encrypted or masked on any read path, contradicting Part 1's own original task brief's claim that they were; (2) **`compute()`'s `activeLoans[0]`-only loan-recovery limitation** (Part 6) — an employee holding two or more concurrently `ACTIVE` loans has every loan after the first silently, permanently invisible to real payroll computation, a real business-logic design gap (which loan should take priority?), not a narrow bug; (3) **BR-PYRL-02's real partial-index gap** (Part 7, this part's own standout finding, contradicting its own task brief's claim that "nothing needs fixing" here) — `uq_pyrl_main_run_p`'s protection evaporates the instant a legitimately-committed run advances to `PAID`/`FILED`, the normal completion of every real payroll run, permitting real, live-demonstrated double-GL-posting of payroll expense for the same period with zero system-level protection. All three remain genuinely open, deliberately not patched opportunistically — each is a real design/schema-level decision, not a narrow isolated fix like the four `ConflictException` translations or the one `@IsBoolean()` decorator above.

**Two confirmed, permanent, no-workaround-attempted forward gaps were handled by this slice's own final part exactly as the slice's own original plan document anticipated back before Part 1 even started**: **no real bank-account integration for payroll disbursement** (`resolveBankDisbursementAccount()` is a fixed CoA-code map keyed only by `method`, `PayrollModule` doesn't even import `BankingModule`, confirmed directly by Part 7 — the pay dialog deliberately offers ONLY a method selector, never a bank-account picker with nowhere for its value to go); and **no payslip PDF generation exists anywhere** (`pyrl_run_line.payslip_file_id` permanently `null`, FR-PYRL-008.1 deferred, confirmed directly by Part 7 before building anything — the payslip view is assembled entirely client-side from real, already-existing API data, with a genuine "Print" button calling `window.print()`, never a "Download PDF" button implying something that doesn't exist).

Every part hit and documented real `openapi-typescript`/zod-codegen gaps using the established cast-at-the-boundary pattern; several DTO families across the slice — Loans' `rateKind` (Part 5), Employee Assignments'/Employee Components' request bodies (Part 3), and both `PayPyrlRunDto`/`DecidePyrlRunDto` (Part 7) — generated cleanly with zero gap at all, confirmed directly rather than assumed either way every single time, per this slice's own explicit discipline. i18n grew across the slice to its final state of **6574 lines** and **5941 all-depth keys / 5310 leaf keys** per locale (`en`/`sw`/`fr`), staying valid JSON and structurally in sync throughout (identical key sets confirmed after every part), with real, non-machine-translated-sounding Swahili/French copy reusing this module's own established finance/HR vocabulary end to end (`Mshahara`/`Salaire` for salary, `Kipengele`/`Composant` for component, `Mkopo`/`Prêt` for loan, `Kuthibitisha`/`Valider` for commit, `Idara`/`Département` for department, all reused byte-for-byte across parts rather than re-invented per part). No browser-automation tool was available at any point in this whole slice — every part's verification relied on real HTTP round trips cross-checked directly against the live database (via a Node+`pg` script substituting for an unavailable `psql` binary on `PATH`, the same substitution every part from Part 2 onward independently established), plus `curl`-based SSR sanity checks, with Part 4's own honest finding that this app's client-side-only auth store means a plain unauthenticated `curl` can confirm HTTP status/error-marker-free rendering but never real row-level DATA appearing in initial SSR HTML — a limitation every later part correctly carried forward rather than re-discovering. This slice's build was interrupted by session-limit resets more than any prior slice (Part 3 twice, Part 6 once) — each time handled the same established way: the orchestrating session independently confirmed the interrupted agent's own code was complete and correct via direct file review before continuing, never blindly trusting a self-reported "done."

With Slice 22 now complete, Module 15 (Payroll) is **functionally complete end-to-end on the frontend** — Employees, Components, Salary Structures, Employee Assignments/Component Overrides, Statutory Tables, Loans, and the full Payroll Runs lifecycle (create through file) plus a real payslip view all have real, working, verified screens reachable from one completed 6-child nav dropdown, matching Modules 7, 12, 13, 14, and 16's own prior completions. **Unlike every prior module closure in this project, this one closes with a real, live-demonstrated, unresolved accounting-integrity gap (BR-PYRL-02's partial-index weakness) that a near-term future pass should prioritize fixing before this module is relied upon for a real production payroll cycle** — stated plainly here rather than left as a buried footnote, since the whole point of this project's own verification discipline is to surface exactly this kind of finding where it will actually be seen.

## Slice 23 (Part 1 — Categories + Assets) — 2026-08-16

**Verdict: Module 17 (Fixed Assets)'s first two screens — the depreciation-policy category catalogue (kind-first CRUD, genuinely fully editable, no delete route) and the asset register (create/edit/condition-update/search/barcode-lookup/filter, 8 real create-only/immutable fields) — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack. Both opportunistic backend fixes (`fa_category.name` and `fa_asset.code`/`fa_asset.barcode` duplicate-key 409s) were attempted, completed, and independently re-verified live, including a genuine two-constraint disambiguation (`error.constraint`/`driverError.constraint`) that correctly named `code` vs `barcode` on two separate live 409s from the same insert. A real, live-confirmed codegen gap not anticipated by this part's own task brief: `UpdateFaAssetDto`'s 5 nullable-clearable fields (`serialNo`/`barcode`/`custodianUserId`/`lifeMonthsOverride`/`insurance`) type as `T | undefined` on both the zod-inferred AND raw generated shapes — never `T | null` — despite being genuinely clearable server-side; found by `tsc`, not assumed, and fixed with a dedicated `UpdateAssetInput` boundary-cast type.**

One real request-body gap on BOTH create/update (`insurance` degrades to `Record<string, never> | null` from `@ApiPropertyOptional({ type: Object, nullable: true })`, `type: Object` alone giving `openapi-typescript` nothing to infer a shape from) — cast at the boundary. A SECOND, genuinely different gap found only by `tsc` while wiring the edit dialog (not predicted by this part's own brief): `UpdateFaAssetDto`'s `serialNo`/`barcode`/`custodianUserId`/`lifeMonthsOverride`/`insurance` all carry Swagger `nullable: true` and are genuinely clearable server-side (`AssetsService.update()`'s own `UpdateFaAssetInput` interface types all 5 `T | null`), but the DTO CLASS's own field type omits `| null` (`serialNo?: string;`, not `serialNo?: string | null;`) — `class-validator`'s `@IsOptional()` still lets a literal `null` in the request body through untouched (it skips every other decorator whenever the value is `null` OR `undefined`), so this is a real type-level-only gap, not a functional one. Fixed via a new exported `UpdateAssetInput` type (the wrapper's own accepted shape, `T | null` on exactly these 5 fields) cast to a `UpdateFaAssetRequestBody` mirror at the `apiClient` boundary.

### Backend fixes — both opportunistic 409s, attempted and completed

`packages/server/src/domains/fixed-assets/application/categories.service.ts`'s `create()`/`update()` previously let a raw Postgres `23505` on `uq_fa_category_name` reach the caller as an unhandled `500`. `packages/server/src/domains/fixed-assets/application/assets.service.ts`'s `create()` previously let a raw `23505` on EITHER `uq_fa_asset_code` OR `uq_fa_asset_barcode` (two different constraints on the same insert) through the same way. Both fixed with the identical `isUniqueViolation()`-checking-`23505`-then-`ConflictException` pattern `DisposalService.create()` (this same `fixed-assets/` module) already established for `uq_fa_disposal_asset_id` — used directly as the template, per this part's own task brief, no need to look outside the module. The assets fix goes one step further than the brief's own minimum: a second helper, `uniqueViolationConstraint()`, reads `error.constraint`/`error.driverError?.constraint` to identify WHICH of the two constraints actually fired, giving an accurate `code "..."` vs `barcode "..."` message rather than a generic combined one — **confirmed live this actually works** (see below), falling back to a combined "code or barcode already exists" message (the same shape `BankAccountsService.create()`'s own 2-constraint case already uses) only if that property ever isn't present on some other driver/error wrapper. `packages/server` was rebuilt (`pnpm --filter @klickit/server run build`, clean) and `apps/api` was killed (both the `pnpm --filter @klickit/api run start:dev` wrapper and its `ts-node` child) and restarted before live re-verification — `ts-node` resolves `@klickit/server` via its built `dist/`, so a source-only edit would not have taken effect otherwise.

**Live-reverified, not just code-reviewed**:
- Category: created `S23Pt1 Vehicles` (`201`), immediately attempted a second create with the SAME name — real `409 CONFLICT`, `"fa_category: name \"S23Pt1 Vehicles\" already exists"`.
- Asset: created `S23PT1-A001` (`201`), gave it barcode `BC-S23PT1-001`. A second create with the SAME `code` (different barcode) → real `409`, `"fa_asset: code \"S23PT1-A001\" already exists"`. A THIRD create with a different `code` but the SAME `barcode` → real `409`, `"fa_asset: barcode \"BC-S23PT1-001\" already exists"` — **the two-constraint disambiguation genuinely works**, confirmed by two separate live 409s each naming the correct, DIFFERENT constraint, not a generic combined message either time.

### A real, unanticipated codegen gap — `UpdateFaAssetDto`'s nullable fields lose `| null` entirely

Not predicted by this part's own task brief. `asset.dto.ts`'s `UpdateFaAssetDto` class marks `serialNo`/`barcode`/`custodianUserId`/`lifeMonthsOverride`/`insurance` all `@ApiPropertyOptional({ nullable: true, ... })` — genuinely clearable, and `AssetsService.update()`'s own `UpdateFaAssetInput` interface types every one of them `T | null` — but the DTO class's own TS field declarations only ever write `serialNo?: string;` (never `serialNo?: string | null;`). Both the zod-codegen script AND `openapi-typescript` mirror that TS declaration faithfully, so BOTH `UpdateFaAssetDto` shapes (zod-inferred and raw-generated) type these 5 fields `T | undefined` only — attempting to build `edit-asset-dialog.tsx`'s clear-to-`null` diff logic against the real `UpdateFaAssetDto` type failed `tsc` on exactly these 5 assignments, which is how this was found (not assumed from reading the DTO source alone). `class-validator`'s `@IsOptional()` decorator skips every other validator (including `@IsString()`) whenever the incoming value is `null` OR `undefined`, so a literal `null` in the request body genuinely reaches the service untouched — this is a real type-level-only gap, not a functional block. Fixed by exporting a new `UpdateAssetInput` type from `assets.api.ts` (identical to `UpdateFaAssetDto` except these 5 fields allow `| null`) as `updateAsset()`'s real parameter type, cast to a `UpdateFaAssetRequestBody` mirror of the raw gapped shape at the `apiClient` boundary — `edit-asset-dialog.tsx`/`use-assets.ts` both consume `UpdateAssetInput`, never the raw DTO type, for this reason.

### Honest gaps

- **`supplierId`/`poId`/`grnId` are plain optional text-uuid inputs, not real pickers** — a deliberate judgment call, checked directly first: no reusable supplier/purchase-order/GRN `<Combobox>` exists anywhere in `features/procurement/`/`features/inventory/` yet (only hooks/api wrappers do, confirmed by grep), and building 3 new cross-feature comboboxes was out of this part's own scope. - **`photos` is deliberately omitted from the create form entirely** — no cheap file-upload-then-reference pattern exists in this codebase to reuse quickly (a loose `uuid[]` of pre-uploaded `file_object` ids), per this part's own task brief's own explicit permission to defer this rather than build new upload infrastructure. Deferred, not silently dropped.
- **`insurance`'s free-text `{notes: text}` shape is a judgment call, not a real schema** — the field is genuinely opaque jsonb server-side with no fixed structure documented anywhere; a future pass with a real insurance-record requirement would need to migrate this shape.
- **Categories still has no `:view`/`:manage` permission split** — a role without `fixed-assets:category:manage` cannot even list categories, confirmed by reading `CategoriesController` directly (matches the brief's own documented, pre-known gap) — not something this part's own narrow, pre-authorized backend-touch scope (the 2 opportunistic 409 fixes) covered or should have.

### Backend fix — a real, previously-unhandled `500` on a bad `costExpenseVoucherId`, found live, not anticipated by this part's own brief

This part's own task brief explicitly stated `costExpenseVoucherId` "isn't validated for existence at this layer per the DTO" — true at the DTO/class-validator level (`@IsUUID()` only), but **`fa_maintenance.cost_expense_voucher_id` IS a real FK to `exp_voucher`** (`fk_fa_maintenance_cost_expense_voucher_id`), confirmed by reading `FaMaintenanceEntity` directly only after a live call surfaced the gap. Completing a maintenance event with a syntactically-valid but non-existent `costExpenseVoucherId` previously reached the caller as a raw, unhandled `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` ("insert or update on table \"fa_maintenance\" violates foreign key constraint..."), not a clean 4xx — live-reproduced BEFORE any fix, not assumed from reading the schema alone. Fixed in `packages/server/src/domains/fixed-assets/application/maintenance.service.ts`'s `complete()`: the `save()` call is now wrapped in a `try/catch` that detects the real Postgres `23503` foreign_key_violation SQLSTATE (a new `isForeignKeyViolation()` helper, reading `.code`/`.driverError.code` — the exact same driver-error-shape-reading pattern `assets.service.ts`'s own `isUniqueViolation()` established for `23505` in Part 1, just a different SQLSTATE) and throws a real `ValidationException` (`` `fa_maintenance.cost_expense_voucher_id "${id}" does not reference an existing exp_voucher` ``) instead of letting the raw driver error propagate. Additive only — no other path through `complete()` changed. `packages/server` was rebuilt (`pnpm --filter @klickit/server run build`, clean) and `apps/api` was killed (the full `pnpm --filter @klickit/api run start:dev` process tree — wrapper, `cmd.exe`, and the `ts-node` child, confirmed via `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` parent-chain inspection before killing) and restarted before live re-verification.

**Live-reverified, not just code-reviewed**: the SAME `POST .../complete` call with the SAME bad uuid (`3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6`) that 500'd before the fix now returns a real `422` with the exact message above; the maintenance event's own `doneOn`/asset `status` were confirmed UNCHANGED after the failed attempt (the failing `INSERT`/`UPDATE` rolled back cleanly inside the existing transaction — no partial state); a follow-up call with a REAL `exp_voucher` id (`019ffae2-2a17-7ebd-9ea5-97fde86dd61b`, queried live via `psql`) succeeded with a real `201`, `costExpenseVoucherId` echoed back exactly, and the asset's `status` correctly flipped back to `ACTIVE`. `pnpm --filter @klickit/server exec jest maintenance.service transfers.service` → **26/26 passing** across all 4 matched suites, unaffected by the fix (existing tests never previously exercised the FK-violation catch path either way).

## Slice 23 (Part 3 — Depreciation Runs) — 2026-08-16

**Verdict: Module 17's core financial engine — the depreciation run lifecycle (`create` computes+creates in one call, then `submit -> decide -> post`, only 4 real steps, not 5) — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack, including a real, first-ever GL posting from this module: a genuine balanced journal (4 lines, 2 categories) and real `accum_depreciation` increases on 4 live assets, both independently confirmed via `psql` before/after comparison. Every figure was hand-verified against the SL/RB formulas before trusting the API's own output — not assumed. A real, previously-undocumented architectural finding was confirmed live (not fixed, per this part's own scoped-out backend-touch budget): `DepreciationRunsController`'s own `POST .../decide` never touches the real `appr_instance` at all — the SAME "manual-trigger bypasses the real instance" gap Payroll Slice 22 Part 6 already documented for its own run engine, confirmed here to apply identically to Fixed Assets' depreciation workflow.**

### What was built

**`features/fixed-assets/api/depreciation-runs.api.ts`** — thin wrapper over `DepreciationRunsController` (base `/api/v1/fixed-assets/depreciation-runs`, tag `fixed-assets-depreciation-runs`). Three genuinely separate permissions across 6 routes (`fixed-assets:depreciation:run` for list/detail/lines/create/submit; `:decide` and `:post` each their own, narrower codes for exactly one route each) — confirmed by reading the controller directly, not Categories'/Transfers' bundled-permission shape. Zero codegen gap on either side, checked against BOTH the zod-inferred types (`packages/contracts/src/domains/fixed-assets/depreciation-run.schema.ts`) AND the raw `openapi-types.ts` shape — the raw type DOES degrade `approvalRef`/`journalId` to `Record<string, never> | null` (the same reflection gap every other Part 1/2 `*.api.ts` file already documents), absorbed for free by using the zod type directly as the read-return type, no cast anywhere. `list()`'s `status` query param gets the same conditional-query-object treatment `assets.api.ts` already established for its own optional-but-required-on-raw-type gap.

**`features/fixed-assets/hooks/use-depreciation-runs.ts`** — query-key root `["fixed-assets","depreciation-runs"]`, lines keyed under the run's own detail key (mirrors `use-payroll-runs.ts`'s `linesKey()` shape). `usePostDepreciationRun()` is the one mutation that also invalidates Part 1's `FIXED_ASSETS_ASSETS_QUERY_KEY` — `post()` genuinely mutates every affected asset's own `accumDepreciation` as a side effect, the same "a write here changes another feature's own cached data" pattern `use-transfers.ts`/`use-maintenance.ts` (Part 2) already established.

**`features/fixed-assets/components/create-depreciation-run-dialog.tsx`** — the FY-then-period cascade picker, reusing Accounting's own `useFiscalYears()`/`usePeriodsForFiscalYear()` DIRECTLY (cross-feature-folder), the exact precedent `start-reconciliation-dialog.tsx` (Banking Slice 21 Part 4) established for the identical "no bulk period-list endpoint exists" problem. Copy states plainly that this one call both creates AND computes (no separate compute step). The real `uq_fa_depreciation_run_period_id` 409 is surfaced verbatim, never pre-validated client-side.

**`features/fixed-assets/components/depreciation-run-status-actions.tsx`** — submit/decide(approve+return)/post, one shared `ConfirmKind` dialog per `run-status-actions.tsx`'s (Payroll Slice 22 Part 6) own precedent. Also exports `DepreciationRunStatusBadge` (reused by both the list table and this run's own detail header) since this part's own file list didn't call out a separate badge component and the 3-status enum is small enough to co-locate. **Post is shown throughout `PENDING_APPROVAL`, not gated on "has this run actually been approved yet"** — a deliberate judgment call, documented in the component's own doc comment: there is no client-visible signal that distinguishes "submitted" from "genuinely approved" without a separate cross-module read into the real `appr_instance` (out of this part's own scope), so `post()`'s own real server-side re-verification is left to speak for itself via a verbatim-surfaced error, the same "never guess, let the real error speak" discipline this codebase already applies elsewhere. On a successful APPROVE decide, a transient `<Alert variant="success">` confirms the decision was recorded (no toast primitive exists anywhere in this codebase, confirmed before building this, the same real, documented deviation `run-sweep-button.tsx`'s own doc comment already establishes) — the persisted status badge elsewhere on the page never optimistically flips to a nonexistent "Approved" appearance.

**`features/fixed-assets/components/depreciation-run-lines-table.tsx`** — resolves `assetId`/category via Part 1's `useAssets()`/`useCategories()` (both read separately from the primary lines query, falling back to the raw id on 403/404/loading, never blocking the table). A "fully depreciated" badge is computed via a real, honest inference (`isAtResidualValue()`): BR-FA-01's cap math is mathematically EXACT, not approximate — a capped line's `nbvAfter` always equals `asset.residualValue` to the cent, confirmed by deriving the algebra directly from `createRun()`'s own cap formula, not guessed. A category-totals card previews P-30's own per-category aggregation (computed client-side via `lib/money.ts`'s existing `sumMoneyStrings()`, no new BigInt arithmetic written). No "not computed yet" empty state is needed, unlike Payroll's own `RunLinesTable` — `createRun()` computes every line in the same call that creates the run, so a `DRAFT` run already has real lines (or is legitimately, permanently empty) from the moment it exists.

**Routes**: `app/(erp)/fixed-assets/depreciation-runs/page.tsx` (list + status filter + create trigger, mirrors `payroll/runs/page.tsx`) and `.../[id]/page.tsx` (header card with period/status/journal fields, `<DepreciationRunStatusActions>`, `<DepreciationRunLinesTable>` always rendered). Both resolve `periodId` to a real `seq`/date-range label via Accounting's own `usePeriod()`; the detail page resolves a posted `journalId` to a real journal number/link via Accounting's own `useJournal()` — both cross-feature READ-for-display hooks, the same precedent this module's own asset detail page already established.

### A real, live-confirmed architectural finding — not a bug, not fixed, matching Payroll's own precedent

Not anticipated in this part's own task brief beyond the "no persisted Approved state" enum shape it already flagged. Reading `DepreciationRunsService.onApprovalDecided()` directly (not assumed) shows it calls `this.approvalEngine.submit()` (in `submitForApproval()`) and `this.approvalEngine.getStatus()` (in `post()`) — but **never** `this.approvalEngine.decide()`. This means `POST /fixed-assets/depreciation-runs/:id/decide` genuinely cannot, by itself, ever make a run postable: it records nothing on the real `appr_instance` at all. **Live-confirmed, not assumed**: calling this module's own `decide` with `{decision:"APPROVE"}` returned `200`/`status:"PENDING_APPROVAL"` as documented, but an independent `psql` re-check of the real `appr_instance` row showed it was STILL `status='PENDING'` afterward — and a subsequent `post()` attempt correctly failed with a clean `422` (`"...DEPRECIATION approval instance is not APPROVED (current: PENDING)"`). The ONLY real path to a genuinely `APPROVED` instance is the generic Approvals module's own `POST /approvals/instances/:id/decide` (`approvals:instance:decide`, a DIFFERENT permission again) — and even that requires a caller who (a) currently holds the ROLE the workflow's single level was seeded against (`System Admin`, per `0900-seed-permissions-and-roles.ts`'s `seedSingleLevelWorkflow()`) and (b) is NOT the run's own initiator (`BR-APPR-01`, live-confirmed with a real `403` on a genuine self-approval attempt before switching to a second throwaway user). This is the SAME "manual-trigger bypasses the real instance" pattern `run-status-actions.tsx`'s own doc comment already documents for Payroll's `onApprovalDecided()` — confirmed here to be a real, identical, codebase-wide interim pattern for EVERY domain using this "manual decide endpoint" shape, not unique to Fixed Assets. Left unfixed, per this part's own scoped-out backend-touch budget (the brief authorized only the already-clean 409, which needed no fix) — `depreciation-run-status-actions.tsx`'s own doc comment states this plainly rather than silently building around it.

## Slice 23 (Part 4 — Disposals) — 2026-08-16

**Verdict: The disposal wizard — `fa_disposal`'s `create` (computes and FREEZES `gainLoss = proceeds − NBV` server-side) → `submit` → `decide` → `post` (realizes P-31, up to 4 journal lines, always balances by construction) — built and verified end-to-end against the live stack, including the module's SECOND real GL-posting workflow and its first-ever `asset.status = 'DISPOSED'` transitions. Three real disposals were carried all the way to POSTED (one engineered loss on SALE, one zero-proceeds DONATION, one SCRAP used for the 403 check), every gain/loss and every journal balance hand-verified against `psql`-queried source values before trusting the API's own output — not assumed. A genuine, CONFIRMED contrast with Part 3's own Depreciation Runs finding: `fa_disposal.status` really does gain a persisted `APPROVED` value and stays that way, independently re-`GET`-confirmed, unlike Depreciation Runs' 3-value enum. A real, honest architectural note was found by reading `post()` directly (not live-reproduced, not fixed, out of this part's own scoped-out backend-touch budget): the frozen `gainLoss` and the LIVE `accumDepreciation` line `post()` reads at posting time can diverge if a depreciation run posts for the same asset in between — see the journal-preview component's own doc comment.**

### A real, honest architectural note — found by reading `post()` directly, not live-reproduced

`disposal.gainLoss` is FROZEN at creation time using the asset's `accumDepreciation` AT THAT MOMENT (`create()`, `disposal.service.ts:56-84`), but `post()` re-reads the asset's CURRENT `accumDepreciation` for the accum-dep journal line specifically (`disposal.service.ts:199-208`) — these are the SAME value only if no depreciation run posts for this asset between the disposal's creation and its posting. If one does, the frozen `gainLoss` and the live accum-dep line diverge, and by the exact algebra `post()`'s own doc comment states (`gain_loss` DEFINED as `proceeds − (cost − accum_depreciation_AT_CREATION)`), the resulting journal's own debit/credit totals would differ by exactly that divergence — a genuine TOCTOU-shaped gap. **Not confirmed live** — no depreciation run was executed mid-lifecycle during this part's own verification (all 3 test disposals went create→submit→decide→post within minutes, and no Part 3-style run was re-triggered in between), so this is a real, code-derived finding, not a live-reproduced bug. Flagged in `disposal-journal-preview.tsx`'s own doc comment (`livePreviewNote`) rather than silently built around; not fixed, per this part's own scoped-out backend-touch budget (the brief authorized no backend changes this part, and this wasn't the pre-authorized 409 fix).
